sites.name: Circuit Central
sites.bookText:
Circuit Central
“The  flickering  glow  of  shattered  display  screens 
paints eerie shadows on the cluttered walls of Circuit 
Central. Torn banners promoting the latest phones 
and gaming consoles dangle limply from the ceiling. 
Wires snake across the floor, tangled and knotted, 
while  static  occasionally  bursts  from  damaged 
speakers—whispers of static echoing throughout the 
shop.  A  faint,  repetitive  electronic  chirping  from  a 
malfunctioning  alarm  punctuates  the  silence, 
occasionally  broken  by  a  distant,  low  moan  from 
deeper inside.”
Description:
Circuit Central was once the heart of consumer tech in 
the mall, now reduced to a hazardous maze of toppled 
shelves, broken screens, and sparking wires. Zombies 
wander aimlessly through the aisles, attracted by 
intermittent static bursts from failing electronics. The 
store’s stockrooms and display cases might yet hold 
valuable technological loot—if survivors dare to 
navigate the electrical dangers and the undead roaming 
inside.

Lighting Condition:
| 1d6 | Lighting Condition | 

| 1-2 | Dark; power completely dead | 

| 3-4 | Dim flickering emergency lights | 

| 5-6 | Occasional blinding sparks from 
damaged wiring |
 342 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Hazards and Environmental Risks Table (1d6): | 
Roll | Hazard Encountered | 
| 1 | Exposed electrical wires (DEX save or take 1d6 
shock damage) | 
| 2 | Loose shelves collapse if disturbed (DC 12 DEX 
save or pinned for 1 round) | 
| 3 | Floor coated in broken glass (stealth 
disadvantage, 1d4 damage if barefoot) | 
| 4 | Exploding phone battery (loud noise attracts 1d4 
zombies) | 
| 5 | Security alarm triggers randomly (raises Tension 
by 5) | 
| 6 | Ceiling tile collapses unexpectedly (DEX save or 
knocked prone) |
Zombie Encounter Types Table (1d6): | Roll | 
Zombie Encounter |
| 1-2 | Shambling zombies tangled in cables (easy 
targets, slowed movement) | 
| 3 | Cyber-Zombie (fast zombie with malfunctioning 
electronic implants) | 
| 4 | Static Shambler (zombie covered in electrified 
wires, causes damage if touched) | 
| 5 | Screamer Zombie (“Karen”) trapped under fallen 
shelves | 
| 6 | Stalker Zombie hiding behind display TVs |
Interactables/Loot:

EMP Grenade (rare):
Causes a localized EMP burst, disabling 
electronics and temporarily stunning Cyber-
Zombies for 1d4 rounds.

Battery Packs (common):
Provides power to radios, flashlights, and 
other battery-operated devices.
(Each pack: 3 SV)

Walkie-Talkies (pair):
Restorable communication devices useful for 
coordinating across mall sections.

Circuit Central Security Keycard:
Grants access to the mall’s security office or 
secret rooms.

Broken Surveillance Drone (repairable):
A valuable drone that, once repaired by a 
Smart Survivor, can scout locations and 
detect zombie concentrations.

Mysterious USB Drive:
Contains encrypted files providing 
ambiguous information about the mall 
apocalypse (see Ambiguous Lore below).
Ambiguous Lore:

A hidden office computer terminal holds 
corrupted emails referencing secret shipments 
to “BioDyne Corp,” mentioning something 
called “Project Lazarus.”

Flyers littered around the store reference an 
upcoming cosmic alignment event sponsored 
by “StellarTech,” hinting at alien or 
supernatural involvement.

A manager’s tablet contains a partially 
corrupted video of armed soldiers confiscating 
tech labeled as “bio-enhancement modules.”
XP & Survival Value (SV):


25 SV

Tension, immediate zombie reinforcements).

sites.name: SuperSave Mart
sites.bookText:
SuperSave Mart
Once  a  thriving  supermarket  that  drew  massive 
crowds with promises of bargain prices and weekly 
deals, SuperSave Mart now stands desolate, a dim 
shadow  of  its  former  bustling  self.  Flickering 
fluorescent  lights  cast  eerie  shadows  over  aisles 
littered with overturned shopping carts, spilled canned 
goods, and the rotting remains of produce scattered 
across a cracked tile floor. Pools of stagnant water 
leak  from  long-defrosted  freezer  units,  creating 
slippery puddles. Rotting meat and spoiled dairy give 
the air a rancid stench, attracting swarms of insects 
and  hungry  vermin.  Occasionally,  the  store’s  PA 
system  crackles  to  life,  echoing  distorted 
advertisements  and  cheerful  jingles  that  now  feel 
disturbingly out of place.
Hazards:

Spoiled Stock (Disease Risk):
o
Contact with spoiled food triggers a 
Constitution Save (DC 13) or 
contract Food Poisoning, imposing 
disadvantage on checks and attacks 
for 24 hours.

Collapsed Shelves (Structural):
o
Heavy shelving units precariously 
lean, toppling if disturbed (DEX Save 
DC 13 or suffer 2d6 bludgeoning 
damage and attract zombies).

Waterlogged Floors (Slip Hazard):
o
Moving quickly requires a DEX save 
(DC 12) or characters fall prone, 
drawing attention from nearby 
zombies.

Malfunctioning PA System:
1.
Occasionally activates loudly (20% 
chance every 10 minutes), 
immediately increasing Tension by 
+1d6 and attracting 1d6 zombies from 
outside.

(Roll d6 Every 15 mins):

sites.name: Strings & Things
sites.bookText:
Strings & Things
“The once-welcoming storefront of ‘Strings & Things’ 
 345 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
is  now  hauntingly  quiet,  its  large  glass  windows 
fractured but surprisingly intact. Dust-covered guitars 
hang  silently  along  the  walls,  their  polished  wood 
catching flickers of fading daylight, and drum kits sit 
overturned, drumsticks scattered around in splinters 
like  the  remains  of  a  long-past  struggle.  A  single 
fluorescent bulb flickers intermittently, casting shifting 
shadows on sheet music scattered chaotically across 
the  tiled  floor.  Behind  the  counter,  an  ominously 
blood-streaked door leads to the back storage room.”
Room Description: Strings & Things is a music 
instrument store located on the upper level of the mall. 
Though relatively untouched compared to other stores, 
evidence of a struggle—scattered sheet music, 
splintered drumsticks, overturned stands—suggests 
something violent happened here. Players entering 
might trigger traps, accidentally alert hidden threats, or 
uncover secrets hidden amongst musical instruments 
and equipment.

sites.name: Dough & Co.
sites.bookText:
Dough & Co.
The sweet smell of rot and sugar mixes nauseatingly 
in the stale air of Dough & Co. Pastry displays, once 
proudly showing glazed donuts and flaky croissants, 
now  hold  mold-covered  lumps  and  clouds  of  flies 
buzzing  lazily  through  shattered  glass.  Tables  sit 
overturned,  chairs  scattered  like  barricades  hastily 
abandoned.  Behind  the  counter,  the  espresso 
machine  sparks  intermittently,  spilling  thick  brown 
liquid  across  the  floor.  A  faint,  gurgling  hum  of  a 
malfunctioning refrigeration unit drones ominously in 
the  background.  The  cash  register  hangs  open, 
empty except for a scattering of pennies and a blood-
stained receipt.
Environmental Hazards:
- Slippery Floor: Leaking syrup and spoiled milk create 
slippery surfaces.
(DEX Save DC 12 or fall prone.) - Broken Espresso 
Machine: Occasionally sparks, risking mild 
electrocution.
(Touching machine: CON save DC 13 or take 1d4 
electrical damage.) - Flour Dust Cloud: Shelves are 
precariously balanced; disturbing them creates a cloud 
of flour.
(Con Save DC 13 or coughing loudly, increasing 
Tension by +2.)
Random Encounter (Roll 1d6 
on entry):
d6
Encounter Description
1
Bakery Zombies (2d4 Shamblers) 
are clustered around an employee 
corpse in back.
2
A Karen Screamer hides behind the 
counter, waiting to shriek at intruders.
3
Rat Infestation: 1d6 infected rats 
hide in pastry cabinets.
4
Desperate Survivor (panicked NPC 
named “Mia”) hiding behind the 
counter, armed with a knife.
5
Corpse Explosion: A Bloater lies 
dormant on the floor, looking like a 
bloated, decaying corpse.
6
Empty: No immediate threat, but 
distant sounds indicate possible 
danger elsewhere.
 347

(roll 1d4):
d4

1
Crumpled note: “Closed by order of 
BioDyne Health Department.”
2

Sixth Seal is Broken!”
3
Receipt with strange alien glyphs 
scribbled on the back.
4
Newspaper clipping: “Meteor 
Shower Coincides with Strange Flu 
Outbreak.”
Interactables & Additional 
Loot:

Pastry Display Cases:
(Breakable glass—makes noise, +5 Tension. 
1-in-3 chance of additional loot roll.)

Employee Locker (locked, DC 13 Lockpick):
o
Roll once on Bakery Loot Table above.

Wall-mounted Emergency Fire Extinguisher:
(Usable as weapon, 1d6 blunt, sprays foam 
once to blind target.)
Ambiguous Lore:
Dough & Co. was inexplicably closed just days before 
the apocalypse began, as if someone knew what was 
coming. Clues point to either a corporate cover-up by 
BioDyne, a religious panic, or perhaps something 
stranger and cosmic in origin.
XP & Survival Value (SV): - Average total available 
SV: ~30-40 SV (food, crafting, weapons, currency) - 
Defeating threats:
- Zombies or Rats: +25 SV
- Karen Screamer: +15 SV - Recruiting NPC Survivor 
Mia: +500 SV (if successfully calmed and recruited)
Tension Impact: - Base Tension Increase: +2 for 
entering. - Noise/Combat: +5 per loud action (breaking 
glass, combat, shouting). - Interacting with 
Environmental Hazards: +1 per event.

next 3 CON saves)

sites.name: Frosty Delights
sites.bookText:
Frosty Delights
Once a beloved gathering spot, Frosty Delights is 
now  an  eerie,  mold-riddled  monument  to  happier 
times.  Bright  pastel  walls  and  smiling  cartoon 
mascots contrast disturbingly with the layers of grime, 
mold, and dried puddles of ice cream. Chairs and 
tables lie toppled, with congealed pools of melted ice 
cream and scattered toppings covering the floors and 
countertops. A soft buzzing drone echoes from a still-
running freezer unit, blending with the ominous hum 
of malfunctioning fluorescent lights. Occasionally, a 
haunting  jingle  from  the  broken-down  ice  cream 
machine briefly fills the silence, drawing unwanted 
attention.

sites.name: Torque & Tune
sites.bookText:
Torque & Tune
“Scattered auto parts litter the polished tiles of this 
automotive accessory store. Racks of tires loom like 
silent sentinels, casting unsettling shadows beneath 
flickering fluorescents. A faint smell of rubber and 
motor oil hangs in the air, mixing unpleasantly with 
the  sickly-sweet  stench  of  decay  drifting  in  from 
deeper  within.  The  far  corner  is  obscured  by 
overturned  shelves,  tools  lying  discarded  as  if 
someone hurriedly tried—and failed—to fix something 
important.”
Room Details
Environment:
Torque & Tune was once popular with car enthusiasts 
seeking aftermarket upgrades, maintenance gear, and 
racing accessories. Now, abandoned in panic, it’s a 
jumbled mess of car parts, overturned shelves, and 
spilled fluids, making stealth difficult. Tools and car 
accessories are abundant, but navigation is tricky due 
to scattered debris.
 350 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level

Lighting: Dim and flickering; risk of darkness.

Sound: Metal clangs at random intervals due 
to falling debris or distant movement.

Visibility: Limited line-of-sight due to stacked 
tires and shelves.
Environmental Hazards Table (Roll 1d6 upon entry): 
| d6 | Hazard |
| 1 | Oil Spill: Dex save (DC 13) or fall prone, creating 
noise | 
| 2 | Fallen Shelf: Blocks main path, Strength check 
(DC 15) to move | 
| 3 | Car Battery Leak: Acidic fluid deals 1d4 acid 
damage if stepped on | 
| 4 | Precarious Tire Stack: May fall if disturbed, 
attracting 1d4 zombies | 
| 5 | Leaking Gas Canister: Could explode if gunfire 
occurs nearby (2d8 fire damage in 10-ft radius, Dex DC 
13 half damage) | 
| 6 | No Hazard: Safe navigation this time |
Interactables & Loot
Torque & Tune holds valuable survival items for 
resourceful survivors:
d6
Item Found
1
Tire Iron (Melee Weapon, 1d8 
damage, can pry doors/windows)
2
Jumper Cables (useful for 
electronics, vehicles, or improvised 
shock traps)
3

barricades or traps, AC +3 to 
entryways)
4
Toolbox (Improvised crafting & 
repairs, grants +2 to Mechanical 
Repair checks)
5
Can of Fuel (2 gallons, essential for 
generators or vehicles)
5
Car Battery (Craft battery-powered 
items or makeshift explosive traps)
6
Emergency Roadside Flares (1d6 
Fire damage, or used for signaling 
allies)
Interactables/Loot:
- Racing Tires (Set of 4): Perfect for quickly reinforcing 
or barricading doors/windows. (+10 SV each) - 
Mechanic’s Toolkit: Enables complex vehicle repairs 
or crafting improvised weapons (+25 SV) - 
Emergency Roadside Kit: Includes flashlight, flare, 
and first aid (+15 SV) - 
Vehicle Manual: Grants a bonus to Intelligence checks 
when repairing vehicles (+5 SV, +Lore clue) - 
Portable Air Compressor: Allows tire inflation, 
pneumatic weapon crafting, or noise distraction (+15 
SV) - 
Suspiciously Modified Car Battery: Possibly rigged to 
explode or electrify attackers (+15 SV, dangerous!)
Ambiguous Lore: - A torn memo pinned to the counter 
references “BioDyne deliveries” to the mall’s loading 
docks. Were these automotive shipments or covert 
biological transports? - Faded graffiti on the wall behind 
shelves reads cryptically: “They lied – it’s airborne. 
Cover your face.” - A repair receipt mentions “urgent 
repairs” to a vehicle with license plates matching a car 
in the parking garage—now mutated into a zombie-
machine hybrid.

sites.name: Vitality Foods
sites.bookText:
Vitality Foods
“The store’s sign—Vitality Foods—hangs loosely over 
the entrance, letters flickering weakly from residual 
power. Inside, neatly stocked shelves boast rows of 
colorful  containers:  protein  powders,  vitamins, 
supplements, and health bars—all strangely pristine, 
as if waiting for customers who never returned. A faint 
herbal scent masks the decay outside, though the 
eerie  stillness  suggests  something  unnatural  lurks 
within.”
Description:

Lighting: Dimly lit by flickering fluorescent 
lights overhead, occasionally sparking 
erratically.

Environment: The shop smells medicinal, with 
hints of herbs, powders, and the faint odor of 
spoiled wheatgrass. Shelves remain 
surprisingly orderly compared to other stores in 
the mall, suggesting minimal looting occurred 
here. The register is open and empty, a 
strange contrast to the neatly arranged 
products.

sites.name: Pulse Activewear
sites.bookText:
Pulse Activewear
“Behind  shattered  windows  and  under  flickering 
fluorescent lights, Pulse Activewear stands in eerie 
silence, racks of athletic clothing still neatly arranged 
as  if  the  apocalypse  had  politely  knocked  and 
stepped  aside.  Posters  featuring  smiling  fitness 
enthusiasts contrast grimly with bloody smears on the 
floor and walls. A faint metallic clang echoes from the 
fitting rooms in the back, followed by low, guttural 
breathing.  A  mannequin,  dressed  head-to-toe  in 
luminous neon running gear, stares blankly toward 
the  entrance—though  you’re  certain  its  head  was 
turned differently when you first entered…”
Description:
Pulse Activewear was once a popular store among 
fitness enthusiasts, boasting racks filled with athletic 
apparel, yoga mats, running shoes, and trendy 
moisture-wicking outfits. Now, its pristine displays and 
untouched shelves create a bizarre contrast with the 
devastation outside. Bright posters promising “Your 
Best You!” and “Run Faster, Live Longer!” mockingly 
adorn the walls, partially obscured by dark, dried blood 
splatters.

Hazard Level: Moderate

Lighting: Flickering fluorescents (occasional 
darkness, visibility reduced)

Zombie Threat: Moderate (hidden runners 
lurking between racks and changing rooms)
Environmental Hazards: - Slippery Floors: Blood 
stains or spilled energy drinks causing risk of slipping 
(DEX check or fall prone during combat) - Hanging 
Mannequins: Suspended mannequins that can swing 
down suddenly, startling survivors (WIS save or 
scream/raise Tension +1d4) - Security Gate: A half-
lowered security gate could trap or separate characters 
if disturbed carelessly (STR check to reopen)

sites.name: Tech & Trends
sites.bookText:
Tech & Trends
Flickering LED lights dance across shelves lined with 
shattered  screens  and  overturned  display  tables. 
Glass  crunches  beneath  your  feet  as  you  step 
carefully  through  a  landscape  of  obsolete  luxury 
gadgets  and  dangling  wires.  Amid  the  chaos, 
promotional holograms glitch and repeat their sales 
pitches  in  distorted  loops,  their  distorted  voices 
adding an eerie chorus to the oppressive silence. The 
faint  hum  of  a  malfunctioning  drone  intermittently 
breaks the silence, drifting erratically above.
Room Overview:
Tech & Trends was once the pinnacle of technological 
retail, proudly showcasing cutting-edge gadgets that 
became irrelevant overnight as civilization fell apart. 
The store layout is open yet cluttered, filled with 
scattered electronics and partially collapsed shelves 
providing ample cover—but also plenty of hidden 
dangers.
Environmental Conditions (1d4): | d4 | Condition | 
| 1 | Sparks and Electrical Fires – Exposed wires 
spark randomly, creating fire hazards and occasional 
electric shocks (1d6 damage). | 
| 2 | Leaking Batteries: Chemical spills create pools of 
corrosive fluids (DEX save or 1d4 acid damage). | 
| 3 | Flickering Screens: Screens occasionally burst to 
life with distorted imagery, distracting survivors (-1 on 
perception checks). | |
 4 | Tech Alarm: Motion-sensitive alarms may randomly 
activate, alerting zombies nearby (roll stealth to avoid 
detection). |
Zombies & Enemies (1d6): | d6 | Encounter |
| 1 | 1d4 Cyber-Zombies (reanimated customers with 
cybernetic implants) | 
| 2 | 2d4 Shamblers aimlessly wandering between 
displays | 
| 3 | Tech Cultists scavenging for rare electronic parts 
(hostile or negotiable) | 
| 4 | A single Brute Zombie tangled in wires, aggressive 
if disturbed | 
| 5 | 1d4 Stalker Zombies hidden among mannequins 
wearing smart watches | 
| 6 | Malfunctioning Security Drone (ranged taser 
attack, non-discriminatory) |

sites.name: Fix-a-Shoe
sites.bookText:
Fix-a-Shoe
Fix-a-Shoe is a cramped, cluttered shoe repair shop 
tucked into an overlooked corner of the mall’s upper 
level. The air is thick with the scent of leather and old 
glue,  mixing  unpleasantly  with  the  unmistakable 
stench of rot. Rows of shoes—some repaired, others 
in various states of disassembly—sit abandoned on 
dusty shelves. The cobbler’s workbench, littered with 
hammers, knives, heavy stitching awls, and jars of 
adhesives, stands exactly as the shopkeeper left it. 
Behind the counter hangs a yellowed poster, “We 
mend soles…but can we mend souls?”
The cramped space makes navigating difficult, 
increasing the danger if zombies breach the entrance.
Encounters & Random Events 
(1d6):
Roll when entering the store to determine initial 
conditions:
Roll 
(1d6)
Encounter/Event
1
A lone zombie cobbler still 
“working,” endlessly hammering 
shoes, oblivious unless disturbed.
2
Several shoes rigged with 
sharpened nails act as caltrops 
scattered across the floor (DEX 
save or 1d4 damage).
3
Hidden zombie lurks behind a stack 
of shoeboxes, surprising the first 
player to investigate.
4
A stray cat has made a home here, 
hissing but otherwise harmless 
unless startled loudly (attracting 
zombies).
5
The workbench lamp flickers 
erratically, occasionally plunging the 
room into darkness at the worst 
moment.
6
Radio behind the counter 
crackles faintly with static—if 
repaired, players hear 
fragmented military 
transmissions hinting at potential 
rescue or warnings of imminent 
danger.

be traded with other survivors)

vs. environmental hazards or

Clue

day.

Hazard Class B.”
3

sites.name: Opulence
sites.bookText:
Opulence (Upper Level - 
Shop #17)
The  elegant  sign,  though  tarnished  and  partially 
covered in grime, still reads  “Opulence” in flowing 
gold script. Stepping inside, your boots sink slightly 
into plush, mold-stained carpet as a faint aroma of 
mildew mingles with a lingering trace of fine perfume. 
Crystal  chandeliers,  long  darkened,  hang  over 
abandoned tables set for meals that never arrived. 
Dusty wine glasses, fine china plates, and polished 
silverware remain in eerie perfection, as if patrons 
had simply vanished mid-meal. Rows of untouched 
wine bottles gleam temptingly behind the ornate bar, 
and the smell of aged wine and decay hangs heavily 
in the air.
Description:
Once a high-end dining experience catering to the 
wealthiest of shoppers, Opulence now stands frozen in 
a decadent tableau of sudden abandonment. Tables 
are set with delicate china, silver utensils, and crystal 
glasses, many knocked askew by fleeing guests. The 
large central dining area is dimly lit, illuminated 
occasionally by flickering emergency lights casting eerie 
shadows across the velvet drapes and gilded mirrors.
At the back, a private dining room door hangs slightly 
ajar, hinting at secrets within. Behind the bar, hundreds 
of valuable vintage bottles rest temptingly, untouched 
amidst the apocalypse.
But the luxury conceals horrors. Something moves 
quietly among overturned chairs and beneath cloth-
covered tables, listening carefully for prey.
Hazards & Encounters:
 359 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall

Stalking Waitstaff: Two elegantly dressed 
zombies, former servers dressed in tuxedos 
and gowns, stealthily stalk survivors from 
beneath covered tables.


flooring near the private dining room may 
collapse into a flooded utility corridor below.
Random Encounter Table (d6): | d6 | Encounter/Event 
| 1 | Hidden Bloater: A bloated patron zombie waits 
under a table, ready to explode upon being disturbed. | 
| 2 | Ambush Waiters: Two agile zombies dressed in 
waiter uniforms silently stalk the survivors from the 
kitchen. | 
| 3 | Wine Shelf Collapse: Disturbing shelves causes 
bottles to crash loudly, attracting zombies (increase 
Tension by 5). | 
| 4 | Luxury Mimic: One of the plush chairs is a bio-
experiment mimic that attacks when sat upon or closely 
examined. | 
| 5 | Corpse Banquet: A gruesome dining table where 
infected rats swarm over half-eaten remains (chance of 
disease exposure). | 
| 6 | Fine-Dining Cultist: An insane survivor dressed in 
tuxedo worshipping an eldritch idol, attempting to 
“invite” survivors to join a feast ritual. |

sites.name: Glow Up
sites.bookText:
Glow Up Cosmetics 
Boutique
 As  you  enter  Glow  Up,  the  scent  of  expensive 
perfume  hangs  thick  in  the  air,  mingling  with 
something less pleasant—mildew and decay. Dust-
covered  mirrors  line  the  walls,  reflecting  distorted 
images of mannequins posed in unnatural positions. 
Shelves  display  luxurious  cosmetics,  their  once-
vibrant colors muted beneath grime. At the center of 
the  boutique  stands  a  promotional  display,  eerily 
pristine,  illuminated  by  a  single  flickering  spotlight 
overhead. You hear faint dripping, echoing softly from 
somewhere within, and you can’t shake the feeling 
you’re being watched…
Hazards & Environment: - 
Slippery Floors: A bottle of oily moisturizer has 
shattered, creating slick, hazardous areas. Characters 
passing through must succeed a DEX Saving Throw 
(DC 12) or fall prone, causing noise. - 
Perfume Clouds: Broken bottles periodically release 
bursts of chokingly strong perfume. Characters entering 
clouds must succeed a CON Saving Throw (DC 13) or 
become incapacitated by coughing for 1 turn. - 
Mirrors of Madness: The large mirrors distort 
reflections subtly, unnerving survivors. Characters who 
linger near mirrors must pass a WIS Saving Throw (DC 
13) or suffer -1 to Perception checks for 1 hour due to 
paranoia.
Random Mirror Encounters (1d6)
1: A fleeting shadow moves behind you, but 
nothing’s there.
2: Your reflection smiles, though you didn’t.
3: Cracked glass distorts your face 
grotesquely (WIS save or minor sanity loss).
4: Strange symbols briefly appear behind 
your reflection.
3: You notice something written in lipstick 
on a mirror: “JOIN US”.
4: A zombified face stares back briefly, then 
fades away.
5: Your reflection looks desperate, mouthing 
silent warnings.
 361 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
6: A mirror spontaneously cracks, 
triggering a noise event (+5 Tension).
Interactables/Loot:
Cosmetics (Potentially Useful): - 
Luxury Perfume Bottles (2d4): Worth 5 SV each 
(good for trading), flammable (improvised Molotov 
cocktails). - 
Makeup Kit: Improves Charisma-related interactions 
(+1 to CHA skill checks for 24 hours; 5 uses). - 
Compact Mirror: Useful for discreetly checking around 
corners, granting +1 on stealth perception checks.
Unique Items (1d6 Roll): 
| 1 | Luxury Perfume (“Intoxicating Temptress”): 
Valuable for trade (+25 SV), also flammable. | 
| 2 | Anti-aging Serum: Minor medical value (+5 
temporary HP), worth 20 SV. | 
| 3 | Manicure Kit: Precision tools grant +1 to 
Lockpicking attempts. | 
| 4 | Scented Candle (“Lavender Dreams”): Boost 
morale (+5 SV), reduce sanity loss temporarily. | 
| 5 | Makeup Kit (“Corpse Concealer”): Grants 
advantage on disguise checks among zombies for 1 
hour (one-time use). | 
| 6 | Lipstick with Hidden USB drive: Contains cryptic 
BioDyne research notes (see Ambiguous Lore). |
Ambiguous Lore: - Hidden among cosmetic samples 
is a crumpled pamphlet promoting a strange beauty 
treatment from the BioDyne Corporation, referencing 
“Project Eternal Youth.” It cryptically mentions “cellular 
rejuvenation,” “unexpected side effects,” and references 
an incident in “Sector 14C.”
Behind a shattered mirror panel, players might find 
hastily scribbled cult symbols alongside the phrase: 
“The veil thins; the Sixth Seal shatters. Ascension 
comes with sacrifice.”
Random Encounters (1d6):
| 1-2 | Beauty Zombies: Former employees now 
obsessed with applying cosmetics, smearing gore onto 
their faces (2-4 shamblers). | 
| 3 | Stalker Zombie: Hidden within the changing 
rooms, waiting to ambush isolated characters. | 
| 4 | Mannequin Mimic: Appears as a regular store 
mannequin, attacks anyone who touches it. | 
| 5 | Karen Screamer: Wanders aimlessly, shrieks 
loudly upon seeing survivors, attracting more undead. | 
| 6 | Cult Survivor (“Clara the Enlightened”): Non-
hostile at first; attempts to recruit or deceive survivors 
into her cause (can become ally or enemy). |
XP & Survival Value (SV): - Clearing and fully looting 
Glow Up grants 150 SV. - Finding the hidden USB 
drive adds an additional 250 SV (critical lore). - Each 
intact luxury cosmetic item (perfume/makeup) safely 
secured back at base grants 5 SV each.
Ambiguous Lore Summary: Glow Up hints at multiple 
possible origins of the apocalypse—whether it’s dark 
rituals hinted by symbols behind mirrors, BioDyne’s 
cosmetic experiments gone awry, or something cosmic 
causing cracks between realities. Players should feel 
drawn deeper into conspiracy theories without definitive 
answers.
XP & Survival Value (SV): | Action or Discovery | 
XP/SV Reward |

| Finding hidden USB Drive or Cult Lore | +250 SV |
 | Each luxury cosmetic item secured | +5 SV each |

sites.name: Tiny Threads
sites.bookText:
Tiny Threads
his chic children’s boutique was clearly once a haven 
for parents with more money than sense. Elegant 
racks of tiny suits, dresses, and designer sneakers 
still  stand  neatly  organized,  untouched  by  looters. 
Creepy mannequins posed like playful children stare 
blankly into the distance, their glossy eyes somehow 
always  seeming  to  follow  your  movements.  A 
haunting  lullaby  plays  softly  from  a  music  box 
somewhere  in  the  back,  creating  an  unsettling 
atmosphere.
Description: Tiny Threads was an upscale children’s 
clothing boutique known for extravagant garments and 
exclusive brands. Despite the chaos engulfing the world 
outside, this store remains strangely pristine—clothing 
neatly arranged by size and color, with pastel hues 
contrasting sharply against bloodied footprints that trail 
through the polished marble tiles. The air is stale, mixed 
 362

with the faint, chemical smell of fabric preservatives.

sites.name: Melody Makers
sites.bookText:
Melody Makers (Upper 
Level, Shop #20)
“Dusty violins hang in neat rows, their strings slack 
and  silent.  Once-polished  brass  instruments  now 
tarnish under dim emergency lighting. A grand piano 
sits at the center, lid slightly ajar, keys exposed like  
broken teeth. The shop feels oddly reverent, each 
step muffled by a thick carpet scattered with sheet 
music and faded concert flyers. You swear you hear 
soft humming or faint notes echoing occasionally, yet 
each  time  you  turn  around,  nothing  is  there.  The 
silence itself feels alive, waiting for something—or 
someone—to disturb it.”
Room Overview:
Melody Makers was a luxury musical instrument 
boutique known for custom-crafted and high-priced 
pieces. Now abandoned, it harbors eerie phenomena, 
hidden dangers, and peculiar clues hinting at the mall’s 
ambiguous apocalypse.
Description:
The store consists of a main showroom with shelves 
and displays, a locked storage room in the back, and a 
private practice room where customers once tested 
instruments. The air feels unnaturally cold and the 
acoustics amplify even the faintest footsteps, making 
stealth difficult.
Encounter Table (1d6):
d6
Encounter
1
Phantom Notes: Dissonant piano 
notes suddenly play, causing Tension 
d6
Encounter
+2.
2
Silent Observer: Mannequin holding 
a cello moves slightly when 
unobserved; sanity test or Tension 
+5.
3
Infested Instruments: Rats burst 
from drums when disturbed; minor 
fight encounter (1d4 Zombie Rats).
3
Crazed Composer: A single zombie 
dressed in a tuxedo attacks using a 
violin bow as a weapon (treat as Agile 
zombie).
4
Sound Trap: A cymbal display rigged 
to collapse noisily if disturbed, 
attracting 1d4 Shamblers.
5
Survivor Encounter: Frightened 
teenager hiding behind piano. Can be 
convinced to join group (Charisma 
check).
6
Hidden Cache: Hidden 
compartment beneath piano lid 
with valuable sheet music and a 
revolver (fully loaded).
Environmental Hazards:

Creaking Floorboards:
Certain sections squeak loudly; stepping 
carelessly risks noise attraction (Tension +1 
per failed Stealth check).

Glass Shards & Instruments:
Floor is littered with sharp glass and broken 
strings (DEX save or take 1d4 slashing 
damage and risk infection).

Mold & Decay:
High humidity and poor ventilation cause 
mold growth; CON save vs. mild illness if 
players linger too long (–1 to rolls until 
treated).

twice):

Mysteries):


A torn piece of sheet music with odd 
notations scribbled in the margins: 
references to “The Sixth Movement” and 
“final awakening.” Possibly ties into Rapture 
cult lore or hints at ritualistic involvement.

Mysterious Concert Flyer:
Flyer advertising “The Grand Symphony of 
Stars” performed by “The Cosmic Ensemble” 
scheduled precisely the night before the 
outbreak began—linking the apocalypse 
subtly to cosmic or Lovecraftian influences.


Cassette found in locked storage, labeled 
“Final Composition.” Played back, it is a 
distorted recording of a chanting voice 
intertwined with shrill musical notes and 
screams. Listening fully risks madness 
(Sanity Check required).

sites.name: Fantasy Wardrobe
sites.bookText:
Fantasy Wardrobe (Upper 
Level, Shop #21)
You push open the colorful but dusty curtains and 
step  into  a  surreal  scene—a  cosplay  boutique 
suspended  in  time.  Mannequins  posed  heroically 
stand  frozen,  decked  out  in  fantasy  armor  and 
superhero costumes that seem oddly comforting amid 
the  nightmare  outside.  Tattered  posters  of 
conventions past hang from the walls, their cheerful 
slogans  now  bitterly  ironic.  Behind  the  cluttered 
checkout  desk,  a  half-dressed  corpse  slumps 
awkwardly, gripping a sword that’s more prop than 
weapon.  But  something  feels  wrong;  eyes  from 
beneath rubber masks follow your every move, and 
the vibrant costumes seem to shift slightly whenever 
you’re not looking directly at them…
Hazards & Encounters:
When players enter, roll a d6 to determine the current 
threat:
d6 Roll Encounter / Hazard
1-2
Mannequin Mimics (2-4) — 
Zombies disguised as mannequins 
suddenly animate to ambush 
players (stats as regular zombies 
but gain advantage on surprise).
3
Trapped Floor Panel – A 
decorative dragon-head pressure 
plate near the register activates a 
spray of pressurized glitter (DC 14 
DEX save or blinded for 1d4 
rounds, attracting zombies with 
noise).
4
Cultist Cosplayers (1d4+1) – 
Deranged survivors wearing 
mismatched hero costumes, 
convinced they have superpowers. 
They demand tribute (food or 
medicine), or they attack.
5
Mannequin Mimics (2) – Clever 
zombies hidden among normal 
mannequins. They remain 
completely still until a survivor 
comes within melee range, then 
strike viciously.
6
Haunted Costume – An animate 
costume possessed by 
unknown cosmic energy attacks 
(AC 13, HP 25, attacks for 1d6 
psychic damage, immune to 
non-magical weapons but 
vulnerable to fire).
Random Costume Effects Table (Interactable)
Some costumes may still hold special qualities. Players 
may equip or use them, rolling on the following table:
d8 
Roll
Costume
1
Cape of Confidence: +2 to 
Charisma checks while worn (torn 
after one stressful use).
2
Elf Boots: Silent footsteps for 10 
minutes (Advantage on stealth rolls, 
single-use).
3
Warrior’s Helmet: Grants 
temporary bravery (+1 morale for 1 
hour).
4
Hero’s Cloak: Once per day, 
ignore the first zombie attack that 
would hit.
5
Sorcerer’s Robes: A scrap of 
eldritch text hints at cosmic origins 
of the apocalypse (see lore below).
6
Fake Vampire Teeth: Fool 
zombies into thinking you’re 
undead (for 1 minute zombies 
ignore you, single-use).
Interactables/Loot:
- Cosplay Armor Pieces: (AC 13, breaks after 
absorbing 3 hits) - 
Decorative Sword (1d6): Brittle, breaks on critical fail 
(natural 1). - 
 366 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Battery-Powered LED Staff: Illuminates dark areas 
without attracting zombies. - 
Box of Costume Supplies (Glue, scissors, fabrics): 
Useful crafting supplies (10 SV). - 
Convention First Aid Kit (15 SV, fully stocked) - 
Fantasy-Themed Energy Drink (3 SV): Grants 
advantage on next CON-based roll. - 
Strange Cult Pamphlet hidden in a wizard robe’s 
pocket (see Lore).
Ambiguous Lore (Cosmic Clue):
Hidden in the pocket of an ornate wizard robe is a 
scribbled pamphlet titled:
“The Great Awakening: How the Sixth Seal Opened the 
Gateway to the Beyond.”
It references alien glyphs found “beneath the mall,” and 
mentions cosplay events held here “to prepare 
humanity through symbolic transformation.” Conflicting 
margin notes in red ink read:
“Umbrella was right… but BioDyne awakened it.”
XP & Survival Value (SV): - Clearing Shop Fully: 250 
SV
- Securing LED Staff: 15 SV
- Armor and Costumes (per complete set): 20 SV
- Decorative Sword (intact): 5 SV
- Discovery of Lore Pamphlet: 100 SV (story 
advancement XP)
Additional Random Table: Hidden Surprises (Roll 
1d6):
d6 Roll Hidden Surprise
1
Secret stash of snacks hidden 
beneath a costume pile (10 SV in 
food).
2
One trapped survivor locked in a 
fitting room, terrified and 
dehydrated.
3
Small stash of first aid supplies 
hidden behind the counter (2 first 
aid kits, antibiotics).
4
Keyring marked “Security Access” 
(opens restricted area doors in the 
mall).
5
A portable battery charger (useful 
for electronics, 10 SV).
6
A friendly but scared pet cat, 
surviving hidden among the 
costumes.
Special NPC Encounter (Optional)
Behind the dressing room curtains, a single terrified 
survivor named Charlie the Cosplayer hides, 
convinced he’s a fantasy hero after losing his sanity. 
He’s harmless but delusional and may help or hinder 
depending on players’ social rolls. If befriended, he can 
lead players to a hidden stash of food in the Food Court 
(extra 100 SV reward).
22)

sites.name: Fur & Feathers
sites.bookText:
Fur & Feathers (Pet 
Shop)
The acrid scent of ammonia and stale kibble hits your 
nostrils as you enter the ruined pet shop. Overturned 
cages litter the floor, their doors hanging loosely or 
ripped completely off. Torn bags of pet food spill out 
onto cracked tiles, and something rustles quietly from 
deep  within  the  shadowed  shelves.  Dimly  lit 
aquariums bubble softly, their water now dark green 
and thick with algae. From somewhere deeper inside, 
a low, guttural growl breaks the silence—perhaps you 
aren’t alone after all.
Description
Once a cheerful place of barking puppies, chirping 
birds, and bubbling aquariums, Fur & Feathers now 
stands abandoned and ominous. Pet supplies are 
scattered chaotically—kibble crunches underfoot, and 
broken glass tanks leak cloudy water onto the tiles. 
Strange rust-colored stains mar the walls, hinting at the 
final struggles of those who tried to care for their 
beloved pets when the outbreak struck. Small bones, 
stripped clean, are scattered ominously around an 
overturned display of plush chew toys.
At the back, something moves behind rows of toppled 
shelves—a shadow darting through the gloom.
Environmental Hazards:
d6 
Roll
Hazard Encountered
1-2
Slippery Floors: Spilled kibble and 
water make footing precarious; DEX 
save or fall prone during combat.

noise, attracting zombies.
5

from cages.

Ambiguous Lore:
Careful examination of the pet shop reveals odd, 
unsettling clues scattered among ordinary supplies:

A torn BioDyne Corporation memo detailing 
shipments of animals for “Project Chimera” 
experiments.

Cultist graffiti scrawled inside a bird cage: “The 
Great Awakening demands blood and 
feathers.”

Pamphlets from an animal-rights group warning 
of “genetic atrocities” committed by BioDyne 
Corp, referencing bizarre mutations.

A newspaper clipping reporting sightings of 
unusual animal behavior days before the 
outbreak.

sites.name: Yesterday’s Best
sites.bookText:
Yesterday’s Best (Shop 
#23)
“The flickering fluorescent lights barely illuminate this 
dusty  vintage  shop,  casting  unsettling  shadows 
across furniture draped in faded floral sheets. Antique 
radios crackle softly with static as if trying to pick up 
forgotten voices from the past. Glassy-eyed porcelain 
dolls  sit  eerily  on  crowded  shelves,  their  painted 
smiles cracked and faded, watching your every move. 
A musky scent of age and mildew hangs heavily in 
the air, mingling with a faint metallic tang that makes 
your  skin  crawl.  Something  about  this  place  feels 
terribly off, like stepping into a memory that’s started 
to rot…”
General Description
Yesterday’s Best was once an upscale vintage shop 
known for its eclectic collection of antique furniture, 
vintage radios, record players, and peculiar porcelain 
dolls. Now abandoned, the shop’s carefully curated 
elegance has given way to eerie decay. The layout 
consists of cluttered shelves, scattered antique 
displays, and narrow pathways blocked by dusty 
cabinets and dressers. Occasional static hums from 
mysteriously powered radios create tension and 
suggest an unseen presence.

sites.name: Sugar & Crumbs
sites.bookText:
Sugar & Crumbs
“A saccharine scent still lingers in the air, mixing with 
the  stale  odor  of  decay.  The  once-vibrant  bakery, 
known for extravagant cakes and gourmet pastries, 
now  sits  in  eerie  silence.  Shattered  glass  cases 
expose empty trays, their contents long picked clean 
or  rotted  away.  Stale  crumbs  litter  the  tiled  floor, 
 371 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
crunching softly underfoot. A toppled wedding cake 
display lies against the wall, its frosting smeared like 
dried  blood.  The  flickering  menu  board  still  lists 
today’s specials—written in a cheerful font that now 
seems hauntingly out of place. A faint scraping sound 
echoes from behind the counter, just beyond sight.”
Room Description
Layout & Key Features:

Location: A boutique gourmet bakery near the 
food court, its once-inviting interior now a 
chilling reminder of normalcy lost.

Furniture:
o
A long counter with a broken register, 
some drawers still locked.
o
A display case missing its glass, with a 
few spoiled pastries inside.
o
A toppled wedding cake display, half-
frozen in time.
o
A walk-in freezer in the back, its door 
slightly ajar.

Environmental Conditions:
o
Flickering overhead lights, 
intermittently plunging the store into 
shadow.
o
The faint hum of refrigeration units that 
have long since lost power.
o
A dripping noise from the back, where 
a slow leak has formed a puddle near 
the freezer.

Points of Interest:
21. The Cash Register: Still locked—
could contain money (useless), a key, 
or a handwritten note.
22. The Freezer: The door is slightly 
open, revealing absolute darkness 
inside. Cold mist drifts from the 
threshold.
23. The Storage Room: A pantry stocked 
with bags of flour, sugar, and possibly 
something more valuable.
Creatures/Zombies Present

1d3 “Rotting Bakers” (Corpse Workers) 
hiding behind the counter, waiting to lunge at 
the scent of fresh meat.
o
AC: 12
o
HP: 18
o
Speed: 20 ft. (Shuffling)
o
Attacks: Claw (1d6 slashing) or Bite 
(1d8, chance of infection)
o
Special Abilities:

“Still on the Clock” – These 
zombies instinctively move in 
slow, practiced motions, 
resembling their former jobs. 
Until disturbed, they continue 
menial bakery tasks, stirring 
empty bowls or assembling 
invisible cakes.

“Sweets Rot the Teeth” – If 
one of these zombies lands a 
successful Bite attack, there is 
a 20% chance that its teeth 
shatter, preventing further bite 
attempts.
o
XP Reward: 50 XP per baker

The Freezer Surprise (Optional)
o
The walk-in freezer contains one 
frozen zombie, partially preserved in 
the cold. It does not move at first, 
blending into the frost-covered boxes.
o
If the players investigate the freezer 
for supplies, the zombie suddenly 
animates, attempting to lunge forward 
with stiff, frostbitten limbs.
o
Special Weakness: It is slower than 
normal but takes half damage from 
slashing attacks due to its frozen 
state.
 372 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Hazards, Puzzles, & Traps

Slippery Floor: The puddle near the freezer 
makes movement dangerous.
22. A failed DEX save results in slipping 
(prone) or knocking over a stack of 
trays, creating a loud noise (Tension 
+5).

Rotting Ingredients: Bags of flour, sugar, and 
yeast have partially spoiled.
o
If disturbed, they release a cloud of 
fine dust, making it harder to breathe.
o
If players try to bake with these 
ingredients later, the results could 
cause food poisoning (CON save or 
suffer disadvantage for 1 hour).

The Cash Register Puzzle: The register is 
locked, but there’s a sticky note nearby:
o
“Code is my birthday! -M”
o
Searching the room may reveal an old 
employee calendar with “Megan’s 
Birthday – July 14” written on it.
o
Entering 0714 unlocks the register, 
revealing a small key (which opens 
the storage room or freezer).
Interactable Objects

Bags of Flour & Sugar: Still usable if 
scavenged properly (5 SV each).

Broken Display Cases: Might contain 
something hidden beneath the wreckage 
(random loot table below).

Recipe Book: A survivor could use this to 
improve makeshift cooking (Advantage on 
survival-based cooking checks).

Employee Locker: Potentially still locked. 
Breaking it open requires a Strength check 
or the right key.
Loot Tables (Roll 1d6 for Each 
Searchable Area)
1. The Storage Room (Roll 1d6)
Roll
Item Found
1-2
Expired ingredients (useless, smells 
terrible).
3
2d6 cans of non-perishable food (10 
SV total).
4
A sealed container of coffee beans 
(high value in trades, 15 SV).
5
A box of high-energy snacks 
(protein bars, dried fruit, 20 SV).
6
Secret Stash – A locked tin 
containing $500 (useless) and a 
loaded revolver with 3 bullets.
2. The Cash Register (Roll 1d6)
Roll
Item Found
1-3
A handful of useless coins.
4
A pocket knife (1d4 damage, utility 
tool).
5
A note mentioning “BioDyne’s 
special order”—strange, why would 
a bakery get a delivery from them?
6
Employee key (opens a locked 
locker somewhere in the mall).
3. The Freezer (Roll 1d6)
Roll
Item Found
1-2
Frozen meat—long since spoiled.
3
A sealed emergency ration pack 
(20 SV).
4
A bottle of vodka (for morale, 
disinfecting, or trade, 15 SV).
5
A severed arm in plastic wrap 
(evidence of something disturbing).
6
BioDyne Pharmaceuticals Box – 
Inside is a set of syringes labeled 
“Specimen Z-3” (???).
 373 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
XP & Survival Value (SV) 
Rewards

Food & Water: Flour & Sugar (5 SV each), 
Rations (20 SV)

Medicine: Vodka (15 SV, can be used as 
antiseptic)

Weapons & Ammo: Pocket Knife (5 SV), 
Revolver (50 SV)

Tools & Materials: Employee Key (Opens 
another locked area in mall)

Lore Items: BioDyne Documents, Employee 
Notes
Threat Level & Tension 
Impact

If gunfire is used here, increase mall 
Tension by +5.

If the freezer zombie breaks out, increase 
Tension by +2.

Loud noises from breaking glass or register 
tampering add +3 Tension.
Ambiguous Lore Elements

BioDyne Pharmaceuticals Box suggests 
corporate involvement, but why here?

Employee locker note: “They paid extra for 
‘special orders’… I don’t ask questions.”

A wedding cake order sheet for a July 15th 
event—the day of the outbreak.

sites.name: Step Saver Repairs
sites.bookText:
Step Saver Repairs
“A  small  neon  sign  flickers  above  the  narrow 
storefront: Step Saver Repairs. The dusty glass door 
has a handwritten”Back in 5 Minutes” sign hanging 
from it—though it’s clear no one has stepped inside in 
far longer. The air smells faintly of polish and mildew. 
Inside, rows of half-repaired shoes sit abandoned on 
racks, their owners never returning to claim them. A  
battered cash register sits on the counter, next to an 
old rotary phone. The shop is eerily quiet… except for 
the soft tap… tap… tap* of something moving in the 
back room.”*
Description:

Layout: A compact shop with shoe racks, a 
repair counter, and a back storage room. 
Dust covers everything, except for a faint trail 
of smeared footprints leading toward the 
counter.

Threats: A Lurker Zombie Cobbler (formerly 
the shop’s owner, now reanimated) remains 
hunched behind the counter, clutching a rusted 
hammer. It only attacks when someone 
disturbs the tools or cash register.

Hazards: The floor is scattered with tacks, 
nails, and broken glass, making fast 
movement risky. A loose shelf tips over if 
bumped, causing noise and increasing mall 
Tension.

sites.name: Trinkets & Treasures
sites.bookText:
Trinkets & Treasures – 
Boutique Gift Shop
“A dimly lit boutique filled with dust-covered shelves 
of forgotten souvenirs and novelty gifts. Snow globes 
sit frozen in time, their liquid long since evaporated. 
Scented  candles  stand  in  neat  rows,  their  labels 
promising  aromas  of  ‘Cozy  Cabin’  and  ‘Autumn 
Harvest,’  though  the  air  here  only  smells  of  stale 
perfume  and  decay.  A  stand  of  greeting  cards
—‘Happy  Birthday’  and  ‘Get  Well  Soon’—flutters 
slightly in a breeze from a shattered skylight. In the 
far corner, a mannequin dressed as a mall Santa 
leans against a toppled rack of plush toys, its glassy 
eyes fixed on the doorway as if waiting for customers 
that will never come.”
Description:

Layout: Trinkets & Treasures is a small, 
cramped shop located near the second-floor 
balcony, with shelves packed tightly with 
delicate, useless items. The checkout counter 
has a locked glass case with high-end watches 
and jewelry, and a half-filled cash register. A 
storage room in the back contains shipping 
boxes, gift wrapping supplies, and a locked 
employee locker.

Threats:
o
1d4 ‘Gift-Wrapped’ Zombies – These 
zombies are tangled in wrapping paper 
and ribbons, some with shattered 
glass snow globes embedded in their 
flesh. They lurch forward awkwardly, 
their movement hindered by the 
clutter.
o
1 ‘Mannequin Stalker’ – The Santa 
mannequin isn’t just for show. It’s 
actually an infected husk, perfectly still
—until someone turns their back.

Hazards:
o
“Avalanche of Junk” – Any sudden 
movement among the shelves (failed 
Stealth check) causes a cascade of 
items to crash to the floor, making 
noise that increases Tension by +5 
and attracts zombies from nearby 
areas.
o
Glass Shards – Broken snow globes 
and display cases litter the floor. 
Moving quickly without caution (failed 
DEX save) inflicts 1d4 slashing 
damage.
Interactables & Loot:

Useful Items:
o
Butane Lighter (5 SV) – Can be used 
to ignite objects or light up dark areas.
o
Luxury Swiss Watch (20 SV) – Still 
ticking. Valuable for barter or trade.
o
Engraved Pocket Knife (1d4 damage, 
 376 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
10 SV) – A fancy but functional 
keepsake.
o
Novelty “World’s Best Dad” Mug (5 
SV) – No practical use, but could be a 
morale booster.
o
Scented Candle (3 SV each, 1d6 
found) – Can mask scent, possibly 
confusing zombies for a short time.

Strange Finds:
Mystery Music Box – A delicate, hand-cranked music 
box plays an eerie, off-key lullaby when opened. Those 
who listen for too long must make a WIS save (DC 12) 
or feel a creeping paranoia. The box is labeled “From 
the Vaults of BioDyne Industries.”
A Locked Letter – A sealed envelope marked “To My 
Love, If The End Comes.” Inside is an unmailed letter 
that hints at a hidden stash in another part of the mall.
Ambiguous Lore:

A half-burned sales ledger behind the counter 
lists shipments of “Exclusive Collectors’ Items” 
from an unnamed supplier. Some entries 
mention a delivery containing “FOR VIP 
CLIENT ONLY – Do Not Open.”

A security tag attached to a shelf reads: 
“Emergency Evac Access: See Mall Director.”

Scrawled in lipstick on a mirror: “The gifts keep 
coming. We are the presents now.”
XP & Survival Value (SV):

Total SV: ~50-100, depending on loot found.
o
Luxury Swiss Watch (20 SV)
o
Pocket Knife (10 SV)
o
Butane Lighter (5 SV)
o
Scented Candles (3 SV each, up to 6 
total)
o
Novelty Mug (5 SV, purely for comedic 
relief and morale boosts)
Tension Impact:

Noise from fallen shelves: +5 Tension

Smashing the glass case for valuables: +10 
Tension

Interacting with the mannequin (waking it 
up): +15 Tension

Leaving quietly without disturbing the 
scene: No Tension increase
Enemies:
Gift-Wrapped Zombies (1d4)

AC 10

HP 10

MV 20 ft (half movement if tangled in 
decorations)

Attack Claw swipe (1d6) or Bite (1d4 + 
infection risk)

Special: If knocked into a shelf, roll 1d6. On a 
4-6, another shelf collapses, making more 
noise and increasing Tension by +5.
Mannequin Stalker (1)
AC 13 (hard plastic body)
HP 15
MV 0 ft (when seen), 30 ft (when unobserved)
Attack: Silent Strangle (1d8 damage, CON save or be 
grappled)
Special: The mannequin only moves when no one is 
looking at it. If the party turns away or leaves it alone, 
it slowly follows. The longer it’s ignored, the closer it 
gets.
27)

sites.name: Perk Up! Café
sites.bookText:
Perk Up! Café ☕📻
“The air inside is thick with the ghost of roasted coffee 
beans and something faintly metallic, like old blood or 
 377 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
rusting machinery. A  dim neon sign buzzes faintly 
behind the counter, flashing the word ‘PERK UP!’ in 
sickly yellow light. The espresso machines are dark, 
but an  old radio behind the counter crackles to 
life, spitting out eerie static—then, for a brief moment, 
a  voice.  ‘…Hello?  Anyone  still  alive  out  there?…’ 
Then  silence.  The  café  looks  abandoned…  but 
something about the overturned chairs and coffee-
stained walls feels too recent to be comforting.”
Description:

Layout:
o
A cozy, hole-in-the-wall coffee shop 
tucked between larger stores, barely a 
dozen small tables and a counter.
o
The glass pastry display is cracked 
but still contains some mummified 
croissants.
o
A side door marked “Employees 
Only” leads to a small storeroom, now 
filled with hastily overturned 
shelves.
o
An old radio sits behind the 
counter, still plugged in, occasionally 
spitting out bursts of distorted music or 
cryptic transmissions.

Threats:
27. 1d4+1 “Caffeine Crawlers” (Fast 
Zombies):

These zombies seem 
unusually jittery and 
hyperactive, almost as if the 
coffee shop’s lingering energy 
soaked into their undead 
nerves.

They lurch and twitch with 
unnatural speed, their 
movements erratic and hard 
to predict.

Stealth check required (DC 
12)—disturbing the café too 
much aggravates them into 
an immediate attack.

Hazards:
o
Slippery Floor:

A spilled espresso machine 
leaks old coffee grounds 
and oil, making part of the 
floor treacherous (Dexterity 
Save DC 13 or prone).
o
Radio Interference:
28. Any attempt to use 
electronics nearby (radios, 
flashlights, walkie-talkies) 
results in brief static 
distortion and eerie whispers 
(possibly nothing… possibly 
something watching).
o
Mystery Transmission:

The radio might crackle to 
life at random with a brief, 
indecipherable message. (Roll 
a d6 on the Mystery Radio 
Broadcast Table below.)
Interactables & Loot:

Behind the Counter:
o
Battered Coffee Grinder – Could be 
repurposed into a makeshift crude 
bludgeon (1d4 damage, messy).
o
Barista Apron with Nametag (“Eli”) 
– Has a pocket with a single 
cigarette and a lighter (usable for 
fire-starting).
o
A nearly full bottle of vanilla syrup – 
Useless in combat, but a morale 
booster when mixed into rations.
o
Stack of expired protein bars (1d6) 
– Still technically edible.

In the Storage Room:
o
Cracked Cold Brew Keg – Could be 
refilled with water or fuel later.
o
Emergency First Aid Kit (SV 15 – 
one use).
o
Crumpled Note: Reads: “If you’re 
hearing this… meet us at the rooftop 
 378 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
by midnight. No lights. No noise. If 
you’re late, we’re gone.”
Ambiguous Lore:

The Radio is Important. Someone—or 
something—might still be out there, 
broadcasting. But who? And why do the 
voices sometimes sound distorted, stretched, 
inhuman?

The Last Barista: A blood-streaked barista 
apron lies near the back, still damp. No body 
is found.

The Storeroom’s Lock is Broken. It looks 
forced open from the inside… but there’s no 
other exit.
XP & Survival Value (SV):

Base SV: 30 (Survival Resources in Café)
o
Expired protein bars – 1 SV each
o
First Aid Kit – 15 SV
o
Coffee Grinder Weapon – 3 SV
o
Lighter – 5 SV
o
Vanilla Syrup – 2 SV (if morale 
system in play)
Tension Impact:
1574.
Searching noisily (+5 Tension) – 
Anything that makes too much sound may 
trigger the nearby zombies or alert zombies 
from outside.
1575.
Tuning the Radio (+10 Tension) – 
The louder the transmission, the more 
attention it draws from the undead.
1576.
Disturbing the Caffeine Crawlers 
(+15 Tension) – They attack immediately.
Caffeine Crawler (Fast 
Zombie)

AC: 12

HP: 15

Speed: 40 ft. (can dash as bonus action)

Attacks:
o
Wild Claw Swipe: +4 to hit, 1d6+2 
slashing
o
Rabid Bite: +3 to hit, 1d8+1 piercing, 
CON Save DC 13 vs. Infection

Special Traits:
o
Twitchy Reflexes: Has Advantage 
on initiative rolls.
o
Unpredictable: Every round, roll 1d4:


The Crawler attacks 
twice this round.

2.
It jumps 
unpredictably, 
making it harder to hit 
(+2 AC for one 
turn).


It lets out a shrieking 
static-like wail—
attracting 1d2 more 
zombies from 
outside.


It slips on the coffee 
spill and falls prone 
(no action this turn).
Mystery Radio Broadcast 
Table (d6)
(Roll whenever the survivors listen to the radio, or at 
 379 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
random intervals.)

“Help… I’m trapped… I’m at the—”STATIC 
”Oh God… it’s here…“** (Then silence.)

“The coffee machine still works! Just 
kidding. You’re all dead anyway.” – 
Distorted laughter follows.

A sequence of numbers plays: 17… 42… 
6… 99. No explanation.

A child’s voice hums an old lullaby. It 
sounds strangely warped at the end.

**“Don’t listen. Don’t trust the—”LOUD 
STATIC, then unintelligible whispering.

An unearthly voice sighs. “I see you.”
Random Encounter Table (d6) 
(For Unexpected Events at 
Perk Up! Café)
(Roll when players take too long, make noise, or 
interact with the radio.)

The Door Shuts Itself. The main café door 
slams shut, even though no one was near 
it.

Something Moves in the Air Ducts. A faint 
skittering noise echoes from the ceiling 
vent… then stops.

All the Coffee Mugs Shatter. At the same 
time. No explanation.

A New Radio Message Appears. It’s a 
direct response to something the players 
just said.

The Floor Feels Warm. Only for a 
moment… then ice-cold again.

A Survivor Runs In. Panicked, bleeding, 
they claim something is chasing them 
(they might be right).
28)

sites.name: Vinyl Vault
sites.bookText:
Vinyl Vault
“The scent of old paper and stale plastic lingers in the 
air as you step inside. Tall racks of vinyl records 
stretch from wall to wall, their spines covered in a fine 
layer of dust. Posters of long-forgotten bands hang at 
odd  angles,  their  edges  curling  with  age.  A  neon 
‘Open Late’ sign flickers sporadically, its weak glow 
barely illuminating a counter filled with scattered CDs 
and  a  rusted  cash  register.  In  the  far  corner,  a 
turntable sits atop a wooden display case, its needle 
frozen mid-spin—waiting for a song that will never 
play again.”
Description
Layout: Vinyl Vault is a mid-sized record shop with 
narrow aisles lined by wooden shelves packed with 
music memorabilia, vinyl records, cassette tapes, and 
rare CDs. A listening booth with shattered glass sits in 
the back, and a staff breakroom is behind the counter. 
A battery-operated radio flickers with static—perhaps a 
signal from somewhere?
Threats:
o
2d4 “Groovers” (Shamblers) – 
These slow-moving zombies seem to 
have once been music lovers. Some 
still wear headphones, twitching their 
heads as if they hear an unheard beat. 
They react to loud noises with frenzied 
aggression.
o
1 “Crowd Surfer” (Runner) – A 
former mall punk who seems to 
remember the mosh pit—this zombie 
launches itself unpredictably at 
survivors from shelves or counters.
Hazards:
o
Falling Shelves: A survivor who 
knocks over a rack (or causes loud 
noise) must roll DEX (DC 12) or be 
trapped under a cascade of tumbling 
vinyl. This also attracts additional 
zombies (1d4 from the mall corridors).
o
Magnetized Cassette Racks: 
Someone set up a crude 
electromagnetic field around a stash of 
tapes. Any nearby electronics 
(including radios or digital watches) 
 380 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
may malfunction if exposed too long.
o
Hidden Fire Damage: Part of the 
shop shows evidence of a small fire—
step wrong, and weakened floorboards 
may give way (DEX Save DC 14 to 
avoid a 10ft drop into the maintenance 
corridor below).
Interactables & Loot

Functional Turntable – The only working 
record player in the mall, could be useful for 
distractions or morale.

Creepy Mixtape – A cassette labeled ‘For 
You’ found in the staff breakroom. It contains 
an eerie, distorted voice repeating the phrase 
“The island is real”.

Vintage Band T-Shirts (SV 5 each) – Still in 
decent condition, might be useful for trade.

Rare Vinyl (SV 20) – A limited-edition Misfits - 
Night of the Living Dead album. Could be 
valuable to a collector… if any exist.

Battery-Powered Radio – Picking up only 
static, but a faint voice can sometimes be 
heard beneath the interference.
Ambiguous Lore Clues

A bloody handprint smears across the staff 
breakroom door, next to a scrawled message: 
“The sound is the key.”

An old concert flyer in the trash bin features a 
band named “The Six Seals”—possibly a 
reference to the apocalypse’s biblical origins?

One vinyl sleeve has been replaced with a 
sealed envelope. Inside is a mall security 
report about a ‘disturbance’ in the Electronics 
Store the night before the outbreak.

The radio occasionally sputters a transmission, 
mentioning ‘the basement is not safe’.
XP & Survival Value (SV)

Total SV Available: ~75-120 (depending on 
loot recovered)

Rare Vinyl: 20 SV

Working Battery-Powered Radio: 30 SV

Functional Turntable: 25 SV

Miscellaneous Trade Goods (T-shirts, posters, 
etc.): 5-10 SV each
Tension Impact

Falling Shelves or Loud Music: +10 Tension 
(Draws nearby zombies)

Listening to the Mysterious Tape: +5 
Tension (Mild unease among survivors)

Discovering the Secret Envelope: No 
immediate Tension increase, but may provide 
critical plot information.
Enemy Stat Blocks
Groovers (Shamblers)
The music never stopped for them… but neither did the 
hunger.
- AC: 8
- HP: 10 (2d6+2)
- MV: 20 ft
- AT: Slam (1d6)
- Special: Sound Sensitivity – Groovers become 
frenzied (+2 to attack, but -2 AC) when loud noise is 
played.
Crowd Surfer (Runner)
A punk who never left the pit, even in death.
- AC: 12
- HP: 15 (3d6+3)
- MV: 40 ft
- AT: Leaping Tackle (1d8 + grapple)
- Special: Mosh Charge – On a hit, the Crowd Surfer 
knocks the target prone unless they succeed on a STR 
Save (DC 12).
Encounters & Random Events 
(d6 Table)
1.
Vinyl Horror: A Groover is trapped behind a 
 381 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
shelf—until the players bump into it. Then, it 
lunges.
2.
Lost Survivor?: A muffled voice plays from 
the battery radio: “Is someone there? 
Please…” Then, static.
3.
Turntable Summoning: If someone plays a 
record, the vibrations awaken a hidden 
zombie.
4.
Cassette Puzzle: The mixtape’s message 
plays a distorted, reversed voice. Someone 
with a working tape deck may be able to 
decipher it.
5.
Security Broadcast: A garbled security 
announcement plays on the speakers, 
warning survivors to “evacuate the lower 
levels immediately.”
6.
Phantom Song: A record plays on its own… 
but the turntable isn’t powered.
29)

sites.name: Game Haven
sites.bookText:
Game Haven – Video 
Game Store
As you step inside Game Haven, the dim glow of 
neon gaming posters flickers against the shattered 
display  cases.  Rows  of  shelves  stand  in  eerie 
disarray, their contents looted or knocked over in a 
chaotic  rush.  Dusty  cardboard  cutouts  of  long-
forgotten game characters stand guard, their grinning 
faces now ominous in the half-light. The faint sound 
of an old arcade cabinet hums in the back, its attract 
mode  looping  the  same  pixelated  sequence 
endlessly.  A  mannequin  wearing  a  game-themed 
hoodie slumps against the counter, its head missing. 
The  register  lies  open—empty.  But  behind  the 
counter,  beneath  a  fallen  stack  of  game  cases, 
something just moved.
Description:

Layout: Game Haven is a mid-sized video 
game store with a long counter at the front, 
several aisles of shelving, a small arcade 
section in the back, and a storage room behind 
a security door.

Threats:
o
1d4+1 “Glitched” Zombies – These 
former customers or employees still 
wear game-themed shirts and VR 
headsets, their behavior erratic as if 
trapped in a phantom game. 
Occasionally, they pause, jerk their 
heads, and move in sudden bursts.
o
1 “Final Boss” Zombie – A security 
guard in riot gear, once a mall 
enforcer, now a slow but heavily-
armored brute who makes deep, 
guttural sounds resembling a distorted 
game voiceover.

Hazards:
o
Arcade Deathtrap – The arcade 
cabinet at the back still has power. If 
touched or knocked over, it sparks 
violently, electrocuting anything within 
5 feet (DC 13 DEX save, 2d6 lightning 
damage).
o
Creepy Mannequin – A headless 
mannequin behind the counter may 
make players think it’s a threat. It isn’t
—unless something else is hiding 
inside its clothing.
Interactables/Loot:

“Legendary Loot” Locked Display Case – 
Requires lockpicking or brute force to access 
(DC 14 STR or DEX). Contains:
o
Replica Katana (“Master Oni 
Blade”) – 1d8 slashing, fragile but 
effective.
o
Old-Gen Handheld Console 
(“GamePocket”) – Still has battery 
life, can be used to distract zombies 
with sound.
o
Collectible Figure (“Mecha Slayer 
X”) – Could be valuable to a collector 
or tradeable for supplies.

Storage Room (Requires Key or 
Lockpicking DC 12) – Includes:
o
Box of Energy Drinks (5 uses, 
restore 1d6 stamina each)
 382 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
o
Retro Console (“PixelBox”) – 
Useless now, but could be valuable to 
the right NPC.
o
Mall Map (Arcade Edition) – 
Highlights old power lines and 
maintenance tunnels in neon-colored 
ink.
Ambiguous Lore:

Bloodstained Customer Complaint Form – 
Complains about a game called “The Infection 
Protocol” crashing every time the “sixth seal” 
event triggers. The manager wrote, “Funny, 
that’s not even in the game files…”

Broken VR Headset – The words “SEE 
BEYOND” are scratched into its casing.

Strange Graffiti Behind the Counter: “It’s just 
a game. It’s just a game. It’s just a—” (it trails 
off in claw marks).
XP & Survival Value (SV):

Total SV: 650

Loot Breakdown:
o
Replica Katana (60 SV)
o
Energy Drinks (10 SV each)
o
Retro Console (100 SV to the right 
NPC)
o
Arcade Tokens (5 SV, tradeable)
o
GamePocket (20 SV, tradeable 
distraction tool)
Tension Impact:

Low Noise (Stealthy Search, Avoiding 
Zombies): No Tension Increase.

Medium Noise (Breaking the Display Case, 
Searching Storage Room): +5 Tension.

High Noise (Triggering the Arcade 
Deathtrap, Fighting the Glitched Zombies): 
+10 Tension.
Monsters & Stats:
Glitched Zombies (1d4+1)
AC: 11
HP: 15
Speed: 25 ft
Attacks:
Lagging Grab – +3 to hit, 1d6 bludgeoning. On hit, DC 
12 STR save or be grappled.
Erratic Lunge – Once per turn, can move an extra 10 ft 
in a random direction.
Final Boss Zombie (Mall Security, Mutated)

AC: 15 (riot gear)

HP: 40

Speed: 15 ft

Attacks:
o
Slow but Heavy Swing – +5 to hit, 
2d6 bludgeoning.
o
Unstoppable March – Can push 
through furniture and obstacles without 
slowing down.
o
Boss Mechanics:

The first time it reaches half 
HP, it lets out a loud 
“Respawn Roar”, 
summoning 1d4 additional 
Glitched Zombies from nearby 
areas.
30)

Bloodstained Customer Complaint Form – 
Complains about a game called “The Infection 
Protocol” crashing every time the “sixth seal” 
event triggers. The manager wrote, “Funny, 
that’s not even in the game files…”


BEYOND” are scratched into its casing.


a game. It’s just a game. It’s just a—” (it trails 
off in claw marks).

HP: 40

o

o
Boss Mechanics:

The first time it reaches half 
HP, it lets out a loud

sites.name: Pixel Paradise
sites.bookText:
Pixel Paradise – Retro 
Video Game Shop
As you step into Pixel Paradise, the faint scent of old 
circuit boards and stale popcorn lingers in the air. 
Neon  lights  flicker  weakly,  casting  eerie  shadows 
 383 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
across  rows  of  dusty  arcade  cabinets.  The  glass 
display  cases,  once  filled  with  pristine  game 
cartridges, now lie shattered—controllers and game 
boxes scattered across the floor like the remnants of 
a forgotten era. A low electronic hum still persists 
from  somewhere  in  the  back,  and  a  small  CRT 
television continues playing a distorted loop of an old 
gaming  commercial.  The  silence  is  broken  by  the 
occasional burst of static… or was that something 
moving in the storage room?
Description

Layout: A cramped shop packed with arcade 
machines, game posters, and shelves filled 
with collectible figurines and retro consoles. A 
counter at the back has a flickering computer 
screen, and a storage door behind it is slightly 
ajar.

Threats:
o
1d4 “Glitchers” (Zombies with erratic, 
twitching movements, as if responding 
to unseen button inputs).
o
1 “Insert Coin” Screamer (A zombie 
that lets out a garbled, staticky wail, 
drawing more undead from nearby).

Hazards:
o
Sparking Wires – Exposed electrical 
cables near the back room could be 
dangerous or useful.
o
Falling Shelves – A precariously 
balanced stack of old game boxes 
could topple if disturbed, making 
noise.
o
Malfunctioning Machines – A few 
arcade machines still power on, 
emitting bursts of sound at random 
intervals.
Interactables & Loot

Weapons & Tools:
o
Metal Fight Stick (Counts as a club, 
1d6 damage, reinforced for extra 
durability).
o
Game Console Power Cable (Can be 
used as a garrote or to set an 
electrical trap).
o
Display Katana (1d8 damage, fragile
—breaks on a natural 1-2 roll).

Supplies:
o
Unopened Energy Drinks (Grants a 
temporary +1 Dexterity bonus for 1 
hour, but increases dehydration).
o
Glow-in-the-Dark Arcade Tokens 
(Potential barter items with collectors 
or eccentric survivors).
o
Portable Battery Pack (Can recharge 
small electronics once).

Lore Clues:
A handwritten note in the back office: “I swear I saw 
something moving on the screen… and then it was 
here.”
A security feed looping on a CRT monitor shows a 
blurred humanoid figure standing in the shop just a 
few days ago, though the footage is glitchy and unclear.
Ambiguous Lore

The “Insert Coin” Screamer wears a 
shattered VR headset fused to its skull, as if it 
was testing some kind of experimental gaming 
device.

One arcade machine, “Zeta-X Resurrection”, 
displays a high score list with survivor 
names instead of initials. A single name 
flashes: YOU ARE NEXT.

A sticker on the shop’s storage room door 
reads: PROPERTY OF BIODYNE 
CORPORATION.
XP & Survival Value (SV)

Total SV: 400
36. Weapons & Tools: 150 SV
37. Supplies: 100 SV
 384 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
38. Lore Clues & Collectibles: 150 SV
Tension Impact

+5 Tension if the survivors activate or touch 
the wrong arcade machine (triggers loud 
music).

+10 Tension if the “Insert Coin” Screamer lets 
out a wail.

-5 Tension if survivors manage to cut the 
store’s power, making it safer to scavenge 
undetected.
Enemies
Glitcher Zombie (x1d4)

AC: 12

HP: 10

Attack: Slam (1d6)

Movement: 30 ft, but occasionally stops and 
twitches violently.

Special:
o
Erratic Movements – Attacks against 
it have disadvantage unless the 
attacker spends a turn observing its 
pattern.
o
“Reset” Effect – Upon dying, a 
Glitcher emits a burst of electronic 
noise, forcing nearby enemies (or 
allies) to make a Wisdom save (DC 
12) or become dazed for 1 round.
“Insert Coin” Screamer (x1)

AC: 10

HP: 15

Attack: Claw (1d4)

Movement: Slow (20 ft)

Special:
37. Sonic Wail (Recharge 5-6): Lets out a 
distorted scream that echoes through 
the mall. Any zombies in adjacent 
areas are drawn toward the store in 
1d4 rounds.
38. VR-Induced Frenzy – If an electrical 
device is within 10 ft, it powers on 
suddenly, creating additional 
distractions or hazards.
31)

sites.name: Panel Mania
sites.bookText:
Panel Mania – Comic 
Book Store
“The air smells of old paper and mildew. Tall racks of 
comic  books  lean  precariously,  their  bright  covers 
faded under layers of dust. A toppled display stand of 
action figures spills plastic superheroes across the 
tiled floor, their frozen expressions locked in eternal 
battle. The back of the shop is shrouded in gloom, a 
flickering emergency light barely illuminating a life-
size  cardboard  cutout  of  a  masked  vigilante. 
Something rustles in the aisles—something that was 
never meant to be part of the story.”
Description

Layout: A small comic book shop with tight 
aisles, colorful murals of superheroes in battle, 
and a glass counter filled with rare collectible 
issues. The cash register is still locked, and 
a door behind the counter leads to the 
manager’s office/storage room, where bulk 
comic boxes are stacked high. A “Back 
Issues” bin near the entrance is half-
rummaged through.

Threats:
o
1d3 “Collector” Stalkers – These 
stealthy zombies lurk between the 
shelves, ambushing intruders. They 
attack if startled or if valuable items 
are taken.
o
1d4 “Mannequin Mimics” – 
Cardboard cutouts and life-sized 
superhero statues stand eerily still… 
but one of them is not what it seems. 
If disturbed, it lunges suddenly.

Hazards:
 385 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
o
“Leaning Tower of Comics” – If a 
shelf is disturbed (or knocked over in a 
fight), it collapses, forcing a DEX save 
(DC 13) or causing 1d4 bludgeoning 
damage and creating loud noise 
(adds +5 Tension).
o
Glass Display Counter – A cracked 
but intact display of rare comics could 
be broken, making a loud crash and 
drawing more zombies.
o
Emergency Exit Alarm – A red 
“PUSH FOR EXIT” door in the back. If 
used, a siren blares, immediately 
increasing Tension by +15.
Interactables & Loot

“Power Sword” Replica – A steel prop 
sword (1d8 melee, fragile: breaks on a nat 1).

Rare Comic Books – Mint condition, worth 20 
SV per issue to the right collector.

Flashlight with Dead Batteries – Could be 
recharged or scavenged for parts.

Dice Bag of Holding – A small velvet pouch 
containing random tabletop RPG dice, oddly 
comforting.

Back Room Safe (Locked, DC 15 to crack or 
STR check to break open)
$200 in cash (useless unless bartering)
Antique Lighter (durable, does not run out of fuel 
easily—good for fire-based traps)
A Single Key Card (marked “BIODYNE 
CORPORATION - SECURITY CLEARANCE B”)
Ambiguous Lore Clues

A half-written inventory list suggests the 
owner had been collecting survival guides 
disguised as graphic novels. A note in the 
margins says:
“If it all goes south, the basement is the best 
bet. Stay away from the vents. Don’t listen to 
the whispers.”

A torn page from a newspaper under the 
counter reads:
“EXCLUSIVE: BioDyne CEO Addresses 
‘Unfounded’ Rumors of Military Contract”

A working radio in the back room emits faint 
static, but occasionally a garbled voice 
mutters:
“…not… heroes… gone… escape… island… 
the cure… beware…”
XP & Survival Value (SV)

Loot Total SV: ~75 SV
o
Rare Comics (20 SV each, up to 3 
copies)
o
Power Sword Replica (15 SV)
o
Antique Lighter (10 SV)
o
Key Card (30 SV, value depends on 
where it leads)
Tension Impact

Searching the store normally: +1 Tension 
(minor shuffling)

Knocking over shelves: +5 Tension (loud 
crash, attracts attention)

Breaking glass display case: +5 Tension 
(audible across the mall)

Triggering the Emergency Exit Alarm: +15 
Tension (guaranteed zombie swarm)
Monsters & Stat Blocks
“Collector” Stalker Zombie (Stealthy Ambusher)

AC: 12

HP: 14

MV: 30ft

ATK: Claw (1d6) or Bite (1d4, DC 12 Infection 
Save)
 386 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level

Abilities:
o
Silent Until Provoked – Stays hidden 
until it sees movement.
o
Uncanny Mimicry – Can blend with 
shadows or pretend to be dead until 
it attacks.
o
Lurking Horror – On a crit, it 
grapples and bites immediately.
“Mannequin Mimic” (Ambush Horror)

AC: 14

HP: 20

MV: 10ft (slow but relentless)

ATK: Slam (1d8) or Horrid Visage (DC 13 
WIS save or frightened for 1 round)

Abilities:
o
Perfectly Still Until Touched – 
Remains indistinguishable from real 
statues until moved.
o
Screeching Lunge – If it moves 
more than 5 feet toward a target, it 
lets out a bone-chilling shriek, 
adding +3 Tension.
o
Supernatural Durability – Immune to 
non-magical slashing damage, but 
vulnerable to blunt force (double 
damage).
Random Panel Mania Events 
(1d6)
Roll
Encounter/Event
1
A Zombie Crawls from the “Back 
Issues” Bin – A rotting corpse, 
buried under comics, suddenly 
stirs.
2
The Lights Flicker – A low hum of 
power stirs momentarily, 
illuminating a strange symbol 
scrawled in blood on the floor.
3
Radio Interference – The store’s 
old radio suddenly picks up a 
signal, repeating a cryptic phrase: 
“The island… it’s real… but it’s not 
safe.”
4
A Comic Fanatic Survivor – A 
half-starved survivor wearing a 
superhero cape hides in the 
backroom, armed with a 
sharpened ruler (improvised 
dagger). Will they help or betray 
the party?
5
The Collector Awakens – A 
seemingly lifeless zombie in a 
trench coat suddenly lunges, 
muttering something in an 
unknown language before 
attacking.
6
A Disturbing Sketchbook – A 
notebook filled with detailed 
drawings of people who died in 
the mall… but some pages show 
people still alive in horrifying 
situations.
Additional Notes
If players explore thoroughly, they may find hints 
about a hidden basement entrance somewhere in 
the mall.
The Key Card could unlock an important area 
(BioDyne Research Facility? A hidden security 
room?) elsewhere in the mall.
Escaping without making noise could lead to one of 
the most valuable loot spots in the mall, but 
carelessness could turn it into a death trap.
32)

sites.name: Craft & Creations
sites.bookText:
Craft & Creations – 
Artisan Craft Store
“The  glass  storefront  is  shattered,  leaving  jagged 
 387 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
edges like the teeth of a broken jaw. Inside, rows of 
wooden  shelves  and  display  tables  are  coated  in 
dust,  scattered  with  unfinished  pottery,  tangled 
embroidery threads, and beads spilled like a rainbow 
of tiny skulls across the floor. A mannequin dressed 
in a hand-knit sweater slumps in the corner, its head 
missing, and for a moment, it almost looks like a 
corpse at rest. The scent of dried paint and old wood 
glue lingers in the air, mingling with something sour—
perhaps mildew, perhaps something worse. A small 
wind  chime  dangles  near  the  entrance,  trembling 
slightly even though there’s no breeze.”
Room Description
Layout & Key Features

Located on the upper level of the mall, this 
artisan craft store specialized in handmade 
goods, with sections dedicated to pottery, 
painting, woodworking, and textiles.

The checkout counter is covered in old 
receipts, and an antique cash register 
remains closed.

A small worktable in the back has half-
finished crafts, including a partially sculpted 
clay face that eerily resembles one of the 
players (pure coincidence… or is it?).

A paint-splattered radio sits behind the 
counter, its last transmission frozen in static.
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps

Scattered Beads & Glass (Dexterity Save 
DC 12) – The floor is littered with small, round 
objects, making footing treacherous. Any 
sudden movement (running, dodging, or 
combat) requires a Dexterity Save or the 
character slips, falling prone.

