sites.name: Peak Gear
sites.bookText:
Peak Gear - 
Outdoor & Survivalist 
Shop
“The glass storefront of Peak Gear is shattered, its 
once-pristine outdoor displays now a jumbled mess of 
ripped  backpacks,  dented  camp  stoves,  and 
scattered hiking boots. A long-forgotten emergency 
lantern flickers weakly on a countertop, its battery 
barely clinging to life. The air smells of old canvas, 
spilled  propane,  and  something  foul—like  rotting 
meat. Dusty survival books and outdated trail maps 
are strewn across the floor, some marked with frantic 
red circles and cryptic notes. A soft drip…drip…drip 
comes  from  deeper  inside,  echoing  eerily  in  the 
darkness. Somewhere behind the collapsed shelves, 
something shuffles… and waits.”
 390 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Room Description:
Layout & Key Features:
Peak Gear is an outdoor and survivalist store, 
offering a range of camping, hiking, and hunting 
equipment.
Tents, sleeping bags, and camping stoves line the 
back walls, while display shelves in the front hold an 
assortment of multi-tools, knives, and flashlights.
The store’s checkout counter is still stocked with 
batteries and fire starters, though the register has 
been looted.
The storeroom door is locked, with a “EMPLOYEES 
ONLY” sign hanging crookedly—something is 
definitely inside.
A large, overturned shelving unit near the entrance 
blocks part of the space. Crawling over it could make 
noise (increasing Tension).
An emergency fire axe is embedded in the side of a 
headless mannequin dressed in a survivalist outfit
—clearly used in a desperate fight.
Creatures/Zombies Present:

1d3 “Camper Zombies” (Infected 
Survivalists)
These zombies were former preppers or campers, still 
carrying fragments of their survival gear.
One is tangled in a paracord trap, its undead fingers 
still twitching in futility.
Another lurks inside a tent, unmoving—until disturbed.
The third crawls slowly toward the noise if the 
players make loud actions.

1 “Stockroom Horror” (Mutated Corpse) – 
(Locked in the back room!)
o
The back storeroom contains 
something far worse than a normal 
zombie—a mutated survivor, bloated 
with fungal growths and extra limbs.
o
Opening the door without caution 
releases it, potentially spreading 
spores.
Hazards, Puzzles, or Traps:

Paracord Snare Trap: A previously set 
snare is still active, designed to hoist an 
infected survivor off the ground—but it could 
just as easily catch a player.
•
DC 12 Dexterity Save to avoid if triggered.
•
If caught, the player is suspended upside down 
for 1d3 rounds (granting zombies advantage on 
attacks).

Broken Propane Canisters: Several camp 
stove fuel canisters have leaked onto the 
floor, making the area volatile.
o
Firing a gun or using fire here could 
trigger an explosion (3d6 fire 
damage, 10ft radius).

Barricaded Storeroom Door: The back room 
is barricaded shut from the inside—opening 
it requires Strength (DC 15) or a successful 
lockpicking attempt.
o
If the door is opened without 
preparation, the Stockroom Horror 
attacks immediately.

sites.name: Gourmet Bites
sites.bookText:
Gourmet Bites (Shop #34)
“The scent of expired spices, dried herbs, and stale 
gourmet oils still lingers in the air of this dimly lit 
specialty  food  store.  A  faint  hum  comes  from  a 
malfunctioning fridge in the back, its contents long 
since spoiled, leaving behind a putrid stench. Tall 
wooden  shelves,  once  meticulously  stocked  with 
imported  goods,  now  stand  half-looted,  some 
collapsed  into  piles  of  shattered  glass  and  spilled 
pasta.  A  flickering”Fine  Imports”  neon  sign  barely 
clings to life, casting eerie green light over a floor 
littered  with  crushed  truffle  jars  and  broken  wine 
bottles. In the silence, something shifts near the far 
aisle—perhaps just a rat, or something much worse.”
Description

Layout:
Long, narrow aisles with stocked and half-looted 
shelves.
A collapsed display near the entrance (difficult terrain).
A locked employee backroom with a still-functioning 
freezer unit.
A glass deli counter in the center, cracked but mostly 
intact.
Threats: (Roll 1d6 on entry, unless already cleared)
| d6 Roll | Threat Present | |———|—————| 
| 1-2 | 1d4 Shamblers lazily swaying near the 
counters, tangled in fallen shelves. | 
| 3 | Spoiled Gasbag (Bloat zombie) lies bloated 
behind the counter—ruptures if disturbed. | 
| 4 | Rat Swarm feasting on spilled ingredients, 
scattering suddenly (can distract zombies). | 
| 5 | Cursed Mannequin standing near the storage 
door—doesn’t move until no one is looking. | 
| 6 | No immediate threats—but 1d4 zombies arrive 
if noise is made inside. |

Hazards:
o
Slippery Floor: (DEX Save DC 13) – 
Oil spill near the olive aisle creates a 
hazard for running or fighting.
o
Glass Shards: (Stealth checks at 
disadvantage) – Shattered bottles 
crunch underfoot if not avoided 
carefully.
o
Spoiled Goods: A foul miasma near 
the fridges triggers a CON Save DC 
12—failure causes nausea (-1 on all 
rolls for 1d4 rounds).

sites.name: Big Bite Express
sites.bookText:
Big Bite Express (Shop 
#35)
“Grease stains and the scent of long-rotted meat still 
linger in the air as you step inside Big Bite Express. 
Trays and paper wrappers lay scattered across the 
floor,  congealed  soda  pools  reflecting  the  dim 
emergency  lighting  overhead.  The  counter  is  half-
overturned, the register long looted, but behind the 
kitchen doors, something shifts—perhaps just a loose 
fryer basket… or something worse. The menu board 
still  flickers  with  old  combo  meal  deals,  now 
meaningless in a world without customers. A low, 
rhythmic  thump  echoes  from  inside  the  walk-in 
freezer, like something trapped… or waiting.”
Description

Layout:
o
A once-busy fast-food joint, now 
abandoned, with a front counter, 
seating area, kitchen, and a back 
freezer.
o
Booths and tables have been flipped 
for cover; a broken ketchup dispenser 
drips onto the floor like old blood.
o
A shattered drive-thru window at the 
back lets in the occasional cold breeze
—and maybe something else.

Threats: (Roll 1d6 on Entry)
| d6 Roll | Encounter |
 395 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
|———|———-|
| 1-2 | Shamblers (1d4+1) – Zombies still 
dressed in Big Bite uniforms shuffle behind 
the counter. |
| 3 | Feral Survivor – A starving human 
scavenger (wielding a cleaver) is desperate 
and paranoid. |
| 4 | The Frozen Horror – A grotesquely 
mutated zombie trapped in the freezer 
(emerges if opened). |
| 5-6 | Swarm of Rot-Rats – Disease-
carrying rats burst from a grease trap, biting 
and clawing. |

Hazards:
o
Grease Slick: The floor behind the 
counter is covered in old grease. 
(Dexterity DC 13 check or slip, falling 
prone.)
o
Unstable Freezer Door: If opened, it 
slams shut behind the player, trapping 
them inside (Constitution DC 14 check 
every round to resist freezing 
damage).
o
Leaking Propane Tank: A tipped fryer 
left open emits flammable gas. Any 
flame source causes a small 
explosion (3d6 fire damage, 10ft 
radius).
Interactables/Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Frozen Patties (10 SV) – Long-
expired but technically edible. 
Might cause food poisoning.
2
Deep Fryer Oil (15 SV) – Can be 
used to set traps (1d6 fire damage 
per round if ignited).
3
Cleaver (Melee Weapon, 1d8 
slashing, 20 SV) – Found near the 
register, stained but sharp.
4
Drive-Thru Headset – Picks up 
strange radio signals at random 
intervals. (Lore Clue)
5
Half-Full Propane Tank (30 SV) – 
Useful for power or makeshift 
d6 Roll Notable Items
explosives.
6
Employee Locker (Locked, DC 
14) – Contains a stash of cash 
(useless), a baseball bat (15 SV), 
and a half-eaten sandwich 
(inedible).
Ambiguous Lore (Roll 1d4 for 
Clue)
d4 Roll Strange Clue Found
1
Bloodstained Employee 
Schedule – Someone circled a 
date repeatedly with the words 
“They’re already inside.”
2
Fryer Instruction Manual – 
Scribbled in the margins: 
“Something’s wrong with Greg. His 
shift ended two days ago, but he 
won’t stop staring at the fryer…”
3
Corporate Memo (BioDyne Logo) 
– A receipt for a bulk meat 
shipment with an unlisted supplier.
4
Old Order Ticket (Still in 
Machine) – It just says: “ORDER 
#666 – SERVE IMMEDIATELY.”
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action
SV Earned
Clearing the area of 
threats
200 SV
Recovering useful 
supplies
50–100 SV 
(depending on items)
Unlocking the 
Employee Locker
50 SV
Discovering a Lore 
Clue
75 SV
 396 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Tension Impact
Action
Tension Increase
Making loud noise 
(slamming freezer, fryer 
explosion, etc.)
+2d6
Staying longer than 10 
minutes (whispers start in 
the drive-thru speaker)
+1d6
Opening the wrong locker 
(inside is a severed hand 
still clutching a meal 
receipt)
+1d4
Potential Enemies & 
Encounters
Shamblers (Fast-Food Crew)
AC: 10, HP: 12, Speed: Slow
Attack: Bite (1d6, infection chance 10%)
Special: Grease-Slicked – If hit, Dexterity DC 12 or 
attacker slips prone.
The Frozen Horror (If Freezer Opened)

AC: 12, HP: 20, Speed: Slow

Attack: Freezing Grasp (1d8 cold, CON DC 13 
or slowed for 1 turn)

Special: Icebound Flesh – Takes half 
damage from bullets and bludgeoning.
Feral Survivor (Scavenger with Cleaver)

AC: 13, HP: 18

Attack: Cleaver (1d8 slashing) or Throwing 
Utensils (1d4)

Special: Desperate – Will attempt to flee if 
below 5 HP, but may return later to ambush.
Survival Strategy & Potential 
Approaches
Stealth Approach

Avoiding the grease slick and staying low could 
allow players to loot without disturbing 
whatever is inside the freezer.
Combat Approach

If the enemies aren’t overwhelming, a smart 
survivor could use the grease and fryer oil to 
create a fire trap against zombies.
Investigative Approach

The Drive-Thru Headset might reveal radio 
transmissions hinting at a hidden survivor cell 
or another part of the mall still in operation.
Final Detail
Before leaving, a speaker crackles to life—even 
though the power is off. A garbled voice whispers:
“Thank you for choosing Big Bite Express… Please 
drive through for your order.”
A heavy knock echoes from the back freezer.

sites.name: Ink & Paper
sites.bookText:
Ink & Paper (Shop #36)
“A faint scent of old parchment and dried ink lingers in 
the  air  as  you  step  into  Ink  &  Paper.  Dust  coats 
elegant  calligraphy  sets  and  ornate  journals,  their 
once-pristine covers dulled by time. Tall shelves filled 
with forgotten stationery loom overhead, their labels 
now  meaningless  in  a  world  without  letters.  Torn 
greeting cards lie scattered across the floor, bearing 
messages  of  love,  hope,  and  birthdays  that  were 
never celebrated. In the dim light, a single mechanical 
pen still clicks open and closed on the counter, as if 
an unseen hand was fidgeting with it only moments 
ago…”
General Description

Layout: Ink & Paper is a compact stationery 
store with an upscale, minimalistic aesthetic.
o
Front Counter: A glass display case, 
cracked but still intact, holds luxury 
pens and fine paper.
o
Writing Desk Display: A showcase 
 397 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
table features old typewriters, an ink 
well, and sealed wax stamp kits.
o
Shelf Aisles: Lined with journals, 
blank greeting cards, calligraphy 
guides, and elegant writing sets.
o
Back Storage: A locked room where 
additional supplies are kept—papers, 
art supplies, and hidden valuables.

Threats:
o
1d4 Shamblers silently wander 
among the aisles, knocking over paper 
stacks as they move.
o
1 ‘Ink Dripper’ Zombie: A grotesque 
undead figure whose face is stained in 
black ink, leaking from its mouth like 
blood.
o
Optional Hostile NPC: A paranoid 
survivor who has barricaded 
themselves in the back room, 
convinced the ink itself is alive.

Hazards:
o
Paper Avalanche: A toppled shelf 
may bury a survivor under a cascade 
of books and papers (Dexterity DC 14 
to avoid, otherwise trapped).
o
Ink Spill: A large, dried ink puddle 
covers part of the floor, making 
movement slippery (Dexterity DC 12 to 
avoid slipping).
o
Unstable Shelving: Disturbing one 
section of the store may cause an 
entire bookcase to collapse (Dexterity 
DC 15 to avoid 1d6 damage).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Luxury Fountain Pen Set – High-
end writing tools, valuable to 
collectors. (50 SV)
2
Sealed Wax Stamp Kit – Complete 
with custom seals, ribbons, and 
scented wax. (25 SV)
d6 Roll Notable Items
3
Rare Leather Journal – Unused 
and pristine, could be used for 
logging survivor notes. (30 SV)
4
Antique Typewriter – Heavy but 
functional, could be bartered with 
NPCs. (75 SV)
5
Ink Bottle (Unusual Color) – A 
strange, deep purple ink; an oddity 
with unknown properties. 
(Ambiguous Lore)
6
Handwritten Letter (Sealed) – A 
heartfelt farewell, possibly 
containing cryptic clues about 
the mall’s past.

Secret Loot (Back Room - Locked, DC 15 to 
open):
1d4 Ink Bottles (usable as thrown blinding weapons, 
Dexterity save DC 12 or blinded for 1 round).
Hidden Key – Found taped to the underside of a desk, 
unlocks a storage safe elsewhere in the mall.
Gold-Plated Calligraphy Set – A collector’s item, 
worth 150 SV if traded with the right NPC.
Ambiguous Lore
Among the scattered pages, survivors might find cryptic 
hints about the nature of the apocalypse:
d4 
Roll
Ambiguous Clue
1
A half-written suicide note, its final 
lines scratched out violently. It 
mentions “the whispers in the ink.”
2
An old receipt from a “BioDyne 
Executive” purchase—why would a 
corporate scientist need a luxury 
pen?
3
A page from an ancient-looking 
book describing an old ritual 
involving ink as a medium for 
“binding forgotten names.”
 398 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
4
A child’s messy handwriting on a 
scrap of paper: “The Manager 
watches. He knows who writes 
things down.”
Tension Impact & Events

Knocking Over Shelves (+1d4 Tension): The 
sound echoes through the mall, attracting 
unwanted attention.

Ink Spill Struggle (+1d6 Tension): A survivor 
slipping noisily can alert nearby zombies.

Unsealing the Letter (+1d4 Tension): The 
letter mentions something disturbing enough to 
make the air feel heavier.
Encounters & Enemies
Ink Dripper (Special Zombie)

AC: 12

HP: 18

Speed: 20 ft

Attack: Ink Vomit (10 ft cone, Dexterity save 
DC 13 or blinded for 1 round)

Special Ability: Whispering Ink – Any 
character wounded by the Ink Dripper sees 
words appearing in their wounds, spelling out “I 
see you.”
Shamblers (1d4)

AC: 10

HP: 12

Speed: 15 ft

Attack: Bite (1d6 damage, infection check 
required)
Paranoid Survivor (Optional NPC)
1761.
HP: 22
1762.
Weapon: Pocket knife (1d4 damage) 
or Ink Bottle (blinding attack)
1763.
Mental State: Unstable, muttering 
about “words that can’t be erased.”
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action or Loot
SV Reward
Securing the store entirely
250 SV
Finding the Gold-Plated 
Calligraphy Set
150 SV
Recovering the Rare 
Journal
30 SV
Finding & unsealing the 
hidden letter
50 SV (Lore 
Bonus)
Bartering with the 
Paranoid Survivor
+100 SV if 
convinced to 
share resources
Final Notes:
Ink & Paper is a deceptively eerie encounter, offering 
deep lore clues, environmental hazards, and an 
optional NPC interaction. The Ink Dripper zombie 
introduces an unsettling twist—could the ink itself be 
alive? Or is this just another symptom of the 
apocalypse’s madness?
This room balances looting, lore discovery, and 
psychological horror, making it a memorable location 
within the Zombie Mall.

sites.name: Ride & Glide
sites.bookText:
Ride & Glide (Shop #37) – 
Bicycle Store
“Dust-covered bicycles hang from ceiling racks like 
forgotten relics, their tires deflated and chains rusting 
in silent decay. A shattered display case near the 
counter reveals the remnants of expensive cycling 
gear, now looted or broken. The faint scent of rubber 
and oil lingers in the air, mingling with a metallic tang 
that suggests something more sinister. A single bike, 
still  in  pristine  condition,  stands  upright  near  the 
entrance—as if someone placed it there on purpose. 
The silence here is almost too perfect, broken only by 
the occasional creak of metal shifting ever so slightly 
in the still air…”
 399 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
General Description
Ride & Glide was once a go-to destination for cycling 
enthusiasts, offering high-end bicycles, repair tools, and 
riding gear. Now, it’s a graveyard of deflated tires and 
discarded helmets. The store features:
- A showroom filled with tangled handlebars and half-
toppled bike racks.
- A repair station in the back with an overturned 
workbench and scattered tools.
- A storeroom, its door ajar, with crates of spare parts 
and a strange, guttural sound coming from within.
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (Roll 1d4 upon 
entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
“The Perfect Bike” – The pristine 
bike near the entrance is actually 
rigged with a tripwire alarm. 
Triggers a loud bike bell and chain 
reaction of falling metal racks 
(DEX Save DC 15 or take 1d6 
damage & alert zombies nearby).
2
Oil Slick – A large spill near the 
repair station. Any sudden 
movement (running, combat) 
requires a DEX Save DC 14 or slip 
and fall prone.
3
Ceiling Collapse – The weakened 
ceiling above the storage room 
crumbles if disturbed. CON Save 
DC 13 or take 1d6 bludgeoning 
damage and become temporarily 
trapped under debris.
4
Silent Stalker – The shadows 
shift near the back workbench. A 
hidden Stalker Zombie (see 
below) is watching and waiting to 
ambush.
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Notable Items
Roll
1
Mountain Bike (Functional) – One 
of the few bikes in rideable 
condition. Fast but noisy (Can be 
secured for 100 SV).
2
High-End Cycling Gear – 
Lightweight helmet, gloves, knee 
guards (25 SV, minor armor bonus).
3
Multi-Tool Repair Kit – Contains 
wrenches, screwdrivers, tire patches 
(Useful for fixing vehicles or crafting, 
15 SV).
4
Energy Gels & Protein Bars – Old 
but still edible, recovers 1d4 HP 
each (10 SV per pack).
5
Lockbox with Keys – A locked 
drawer near the register (DEX DC 
14 to pick, or found key in storage). 
Contains cash (useless), a 
flashlight (10 SV), and a revolver 
(25 SV, 5 bullets).
6
Survivor’s Note – A bloodstained 
message from a former survivor, 
warning: “DO NOT take the bike. 
It knows.”
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered throughout the store are eerie hints about the 
mall’s apocalypse origins, offering contradictory 
clues:
| d4 Roll | Ambiguous Clue |
| 1 | Military Supply List – A crumpled checklist 
referencing a “containment protocol for airborne 
agents”—suggesting a biological outbreak. | 
| 2 | Occult Symbols – Strange markings behind the 
register, possibly part of a ritual or a protection ward… 
but against what? | 
| 3 | Corporate Memo – A letter from BioDyne Corp, 
discussing “human motion studies” and potential side 
effects of prolonged exposure. | 
| 4 | Radio Log Entry – A scribbled note from an 
unknown survivor: “If you hear the wheels spin at night, 
don’t look outside.” |
 400 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level

50 SV
Tension Impact

Making Noise (Bike Bell, Loud Combat, 
Breaking Shelves): +1d6 Tension

Triggering Tripwire Alarm: +2d6 Tension

Sneaking Through Without Making Noise: 
No Tension increase
Potential Enemies
Roll 1d6 upon entry to determine the threat present: 
| d6 Roll | Zombie/Threat Type | 
| 1-2 | Shambler Pack (1d4+1) – Standard zombies 
lurking in the repair station. | 
| 3 | The Storage Room Surprise – A single “Half-
Turned” Survivor (a still-conscious infected person) 
begging for help. | 
| 4 | Stalker Zombie – A fast, intelligent zombie hiding 
behind the counter. It attacks when the players’ backs 
are turned. | 
| 5 | Corpse Puppeteer – A zombie tangled in bicycle 
chains, twitching unnaturally as if moved by unseen 
forces. | 
| 6 | No Zombies… Yet – The store is eerily empty, but 
noises from the vents suggest something is watching. |
Special Encounters
The Half-Turned Survivor (Optional Moral 
Dilemma)

A conscious but infected person is trapped 
in the storage room, chained to a shelf.

He pleads for help, claiming he knows a safe 
way out of the mall.

If the players rescue him, he offers a map 
with secret routes (150 SV value)—but he 
WILL turn within 24 hours.

Killing him now prevents the risk later, but 
costs morality points (if applicable in your 
system).
Monster Stats
Shamblers (1d4+1)

HP: 12 each

Attack: Bite (1d6, infection chance)

Slow-moving, weak but numerous.
Stalker Zombie (Fast & Silent)

HP: 18

AC: 14 (agile)

Attack: Claw (1d6 + grapple)

Special:
o
Ambush Strike: First attack 
automatically hits if unnoticed.
o
Silent Killer: Moves without sound 
unless spotted (WIS Perception DC 
15).
 401 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
Corpse Puppeteer

HP: 25

AC: 12

Attack: Chain Whip (1d8, 10ft reach)

Special:
o
Controlled Undead: Reanimates one 
fallen zombie every 3 rounds unless 
interrupted.
o
Eerie Movement: Immune to fear 
effects, moves unnaturally.
Survival XP Rewards
Action
XP / SV Reward
Securing store fully
250 SV
Securing the 
Mountain Bike
100 SV
Discovering the 
Survivor’s Note
50 SV
Defeating the 
Stalker Zombie
100 SV
Rescuing or Killing 
the Half-Turned 
Survivor
Varies (Ethical 
Decision Impact)
Summary:
- Ride & Glide is more than just a bike shop—it’s a 
potential fast-escape opportunity, a moral test, and a 
death trap depending on how players interact with it.
- The mysteries deepen with cryptic notes and 
contradictory lore, making it impossible to pin down 
what really happened.
- Players can either find loot, deal with threats, or 
uncover the eerie truth behind the pristine bike… if 
they dare to take it.

sites.name: Bright Beginnings
sites.bookText:
Bright Beginnings (Shop 
#38)
“A faded sign decorated with pastel-colored balloons 
and  smiling  cartoon  animals  hangs  above  the 
entrance, now peeling and covered in dust. Inside, 
rows of tiny mannequins dressed in outdated school 
uniforms stand eerily at attention, their glass eyes 
reflecting  the  dim  emergency  lights  flickering 
overhead. Clothing racks filled with miniature jackets 
and  dresses  sway  slightly  in  the  stale  air,  as  if 
something  unseen  just  passed  through.  The  faint, 
hollow sound of a child’s wind-up music box plays 
from somewhere deeper inside the store… but no 
one is there to wind it.”
General Description
Once a cheerful kids’ clothing boutique, Bright 
Beginnings is now an unsettling relic of pre-
apocalypse innocence. Its colorful walls are faded, the 
decorations peeling, and the floor is littered with tiny 
sneakers and abandoned strollers. The mannequins, 
positioned to look like happy schoolchildren, now stand 
as silent sentinels, their unsettling presence making the 
store feel like a frozen moment in time.

sites.name: The Grand Table
sites.bookText:
The Grand Table (Shop 
#39)
“Once a beacon of fine dining and elegance, The 
Grand Table now sits in eerie silence, its lavish décor 
draped in layers of dust. Crystal chandeliers hang 
precariously from the ceiling, some shattered on the 
floor  in  jagged  piles  of  glass.  The  long,  ornate 
banquet tables remain set as if awaiting guests, their 
plates covered in mold and forgotten feasts turned to 
rot. A grand piano rests in the corner, its ivory keys 
chipped and stained. A faint scraping noise echoes 
from the kitchen, where something—or someone—
still lingers.”
General Description

Layout: The Grand Table is an upscale fine 
dining restaurant with an open floor plan. The 
dining area is filled with long banquet tables, 
decorative chairs, and a stage where 
musicians once played. The bar area remains 
stocked with aged liquors, and the kitchen is a 
maze of stainless-steel counters, ovens, and 
freezers—some still sealed.

Threats: Several Hollow Gourmands 
(mutated zombies that gorge themselves 
endlessly) sit slumped over tables, seemingly 
dormant. A Butcher Revenant stalks the 
kitchen, wielding a massive meat cleaver.

Hazards: The chandeliers are unstable and 
could fall (1d6 damage in a 10ft radius if 
disturbed). The floor near the kitchen is slick 
with congealed grease, making movement 
treacherous (Dexterity DC 13 or prone).
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (roll 1d4 on entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Falling Chandelier: Any loud noise 
(combat, breaking glass, shouting) 
has a 50% chance of causing a 
chandelier to fall. 10ft radius, 2d6 
damage.
2
Rancid Buffet Table: The air near 
the long banquet tables is so putrid 
that it forces a Constitution DC 14 
save or causes nausea 
(disadvantage on attacks for 1 
minute).
3
Bloodied Kitchen Floor: Stealth 
checks are at disadvantage in the 
kitchen due to sticky, blood-slicked 
surfaces.
4
Hidden Larder Corpse: A freezer 
door swings open suddenly, 
revealing a pile of half-eaten 
bodies. Willpower (Wisdom) DC 
12 or suffer -2 morale for the next 
hour.
Interactables/Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Aged Wine (Fine Vintage) – A 
rare, untouched bottle worth 100 SV 
to the right buyer.
2
Butcher’s Cleaver (Heavy Blade, 
1d8 damage) – Found in the 
kitchen, still sharp.
3
Cigar Box with Hidden Stash – 
Contains $1,000 in pre-collapse 
cash (Trade Value 50 SV) and an 
old key labeled “Manager’s Office”.
4
Undisturbed Walk-In Freezer – 
Holding 50 SV worth of preserved 
food, but opening it releases an 
ice-covered Shambler.
5
Gold-Plated Dinnerware – A set of 
extravagant forks and knives, worth 
75 SV if sold.
 405 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
6
Rare Canned Goods – A hidden 
supply of high-quality canned 
meats and vegetables (75 SV in 
food value).
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered throughout the restaurant are cryptic signs of 
what happened before the mall fell:
d4 Roll Lore Clue
1
A wine-stained napkin with a

sites.name: Hero’s Haven
sites.bookText:
Hero’s Haven (Shop #40)
“The air inside Hero’s Haven is thick with the scent of 
dust and old paper. Shelves of graphic novels stand 
untouched, their colorful covers faded under flickering 
fluorescent lights. A massive, shattered display case 
at the center of the shop once held a prized collection 
of rare action figures—now scattered across the floor 
like fallen warriors. Rows of costumed mannequins 
line the walls, their capes and masks frozen mid-
motion, some missing heads or limbs. In the back, the 
glow of a still-active arcade cabinet flickers, its screen 
displaying  an  endless  ‘GAME  OVER.’  The  silence 
here  feels  unnatural,  as  if  the  heroes  of  old  are 
watching… waiting.”
General Description
Hero’s Haven was once the mall’s premier comic and 
collectibles store, featuring everything from rare graphic 
novels to high-end replica swords and superhero 
figurines. Now, it is a graveyard of fandom, with 
overturned shelves, broken glass, and eerie superhero 
mannequins that seem to shift positions when no one is 
looking.

Layout: Narrow aisles lined with comics, action 
figures, and novelty merchandise. A ruined 
central display case. A back storeroom filled 
with locked stock boxes.

Threats:
o
“Collector’s Revenge” Zombie (1) – 
A former store manager in a tattered 
superhero hoodie, now an intelligent 
hunter zombie that stalks survivors 
through the shop, waiting for the 
perfect moment to strike.
o
Shambler Horde (2d4) – Slow-moving 
zombies tangled in capes and hero-
themed apparel, shambling between 
aisles.

Hazards:
o
Unstable Shelves – Any sudden 
movements (Strength check DC 13) 
can cause a shelf to topple, crushing a 
character (1d8 bludgeoning) and 
creating loud noise (+2d6 Tension).
o
Motion-Triggered Hero Display – A 
loud recording of a superhero 
monologue may suddenly play when 
the sensor is tripped (+1d4 Tension).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Replica Katana (1d8 slashing, 
counts as a short sword but with a 
+1 to intimidation checks due to 
its ornate design).
2
Mysterious Locked Box – A 
reinforced stock crate (Lockpicking 
DC 16) containing a signed first-
edition graphic novel (worth 200 
SV to collectors).
3
Limited Edition Action Figure – 
Pristine condition, still sealed 
(Trade value: 100 SV)
4
Collector’s Backpack – A sturdy 
backpack featuring comic-themed 
patches, increasing carrying 
 407 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
d6 Roll Notable Items
capacity by +10 slots.
5
Superhero-Themed Motorcycle 
Helmet – Provides +1 AC, protects 
against headshots, and has a one-
way tinted visor.
6
Arcade Token Cache – A hidden 
box of old arcade tokens that can 
be used to activate a still-
functional “Superhero 
Beatdown” arcade machine 
(grants +1 temporary morale if 
played).
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered notes and collectibles hint at strange pre-
apocalypse occurrences related to the mall’s downfall:
d4 Roll
Ambiguous Clue
1
Handwritten Notebook – A 
former store employee’s journal, 
ranting about “seeing things 
move when the store was 
closed” and hearing “voices in 
the static of the arcade 
machine.”
2
Cracked Glass Trophy Case – A 
plaque from BioDyne 
Corporation thanking Hero’s 
Haven for its contribution to a 
“classified marketing study 
involving psychological 
imprinting in young minds.”
3
Defaced Captain Valor Statue – 
Someone has carved occult 
symbols into the chest of a once-
proud superhero statue.
4
Old Security Footage (found in 
the back room) – A VHS tape 
showing the last shift before the 
outbreak, where mannequins 
visibly move on their own in the 
security feed.

Tension Impact

Knocking over a shelf: +2d6 Tension

Motion-triggered hero monologue: +1d4 
Tension

Fighting the Collector’s Revenge zombie: 
+3d6 Tension
Potential Enemies
Collector’s Revenge (Hunter Zombie)
AC: 14 | HP: 25 | Speed: 40 ft
Atk: Leaping Claw Strike (1d8 slashing) OR Lunging 
Bite (1d6 + grapple)
Special:
o
Ambush Predator – The Collector 
moves silently among the aisles, 
gaining Advantage on stealth 
checks to remain undetected.
o
Heroic Last Words – When reduced 
 408 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
to 0 HP, the zombie lets out a loud 
final scream that increases Tension 
by +2d6.
o
Superhuman Reflexes – Can dodge 
ranged attacks (Disadvantage to hit 
unless within 10 ft).
Shambler Horde (2d4)

AC: 8 | HP: 12 each | Speed: 20 ft

Atk: Flailing Hands (1d4 bludgeoning) or Bite 
(1d6, Infection chance 25%)

Special:
o
Costume Snags – These zombies 
wear long superhero capes and 
masks, occasionally tripping over 
their own attire (10% chance they fall 
prone).
Optional Event: “Arcade of the 
Damned”
If a player interacts with the old arcade machine 
(Superhero Beatdown II: Galactic Showdown), 
strange occurrences begin:

The screen flickers and plays out events that 
have happened inside the store—before 
they actually happen.

The machine’s final boss battle features a 
hero with the exact likeness of the 
Collector’s Revenge zombie.

If the player completes the arcade game, 
they receive a +2 morale boost for 24 hours 
and may unlock a hidden drawer containing 
a crowbar (15 SV) and canned food (10 SV).
Final Thoughts & Gameplay 
Uses

Hero’s Haven is a prime location for 
scavenging rare collectibles, makeshift 
weapons, and lore clues.

The Collector’s Revenge is a formidable 
stalker enemy, perfect for a suspenseful 
encounter.

The arcade machine adds a surreal, cosmic 
horror twist to the otherwise mundane setting.

Tension effects ensure players must be 
careful with their movements and actions.

sites.name: QuickTalk Wireless
sites.bookText:
QuickTalk Wireless (Shop 
#41)
“The  once-bustling  phone  store  now  stands  eerily 
silent.  The  walls  are  lined  with  shattered  display 
cases, their glass crunching softly underfoot. Rows of 
useless smartphones sit lifeless, screens cracked and 
batteries long drained. Promotional posters still hang 
from the ceiling, offering ‘Unlimited Plans for Life!’—a 
cruel joke now. A flickering neon ‘Open’ sign buzzes 
intermittently,  casting  brief  pulses  of  sickly  light 
across  the  darkened  interior.  In  the  back,  the 
employee  door  hangs  slightly  ajar,  revealing  a 
darkened storage room. Something shifts inside, just 
at the edge of hearing…”
Description

Layout:
o
Small storefront with a central 
checkout counter, shattered glass 
display cases, and walls lined with 
dead smartphones and accessories.
o
A back storage room contains boxed 
inventory and a small break area with 
lockers.
o
The ceiling security cameras still 
turn occasionally, seemingly 
powered by something unknown.

Threats:
o
1d4 Crawler Zombies hiding behind 
the counter or within the back storage 
room.
o
Shambling Sales Rep (Unique 
Zombie): A former employee still 
dressed in his QuickTalk uniform, 
holding a broken tablet.

Hazards:
•
Surprise Sparks: Exposed wiring near the 
counter causes random electrical arcs. Contact 
 409 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
deals 1d6 lightning damage and makes a loud 
noise.
•
Security Alarm Glitch: Attempting to access the 
register without caution (Dex DC 14) may trigger a 
sudden burst of recorded sales pitches, 
increasing Tension.
•
Unstable Shelving (Backroom): A collapsed 
phone rack is precariously balanced; disturbing it 
(Dex DC 12) could bury a survivor in 1d6 
bludgeoning damage and alert zombies.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Item Found
1
Dead Cellphones (Useless) – 
Could be used for makeshift 
distractions.
2
Bluetooth Speaker (Functional) – 
Plays sounds remotely if powered 
(useful for zombie luring).
3
Power Bank (Low Charge) – Holds 
1d4 charges for small electronics 
(flashlights, radios).
4
Walkie-Talkies (1d4 found) – 
Range of a few miles, could be 
useful for survivor 
communication.
5
Hidden Safe (Locked, DC 15 to 
Pick/Open) – Contains $1,000 in 
cash (useless) and BioDyne 
Corporation Flash Drive (Lore 
Item).
6
Emergency Backup Battery 
(Heavy, 50 SV) – Could be used 
to restore power to another small 
section of the mall.
Ambiguous Lore
d4 Roll Lore Clue Found
1
A distorted voicemail recording 
still plays on one of the office 
phones: “They locked us in here… 
I don’t think help is coming. If 
anyone finds this, DO NOT TRUST
—” (static).
2
A customer complaint receipt 
about strange frequencies 
interfering with phone calls: “I keep 
hearing a voice on the other end, 
but it’s not my daughter… It just 
keeps whispering my name.”
3
Corporate Memo referencing a 
“Government Surveillance 
Initiative” that QuickTalk was 
involved in—suggesting they were 
tracking something BEFORE the 
outbreak.
4
A phone is still receiving texts 
despite no power: The most 
recent message simply reads: 
“You can’t run forever.”

sites.name: Curio Cove
sites.bookText:
Curio Cove (Shop #42)
“The scent of stale popcorn and artificial lavender still 
lingers in the air. Rows of dusty shelves are crammed 
with  novelty  gifts—stuffed  animals  with  oversized 
eyes,  mugs  with  corny  slogans,  and  racks  of 
mismatched socks patterned with llamas and UFOs. 
A spinning display of keychains creaks with every 
movement, as if watching you. Something feels… off. 
The air is thick with unease, and a low, rhythmic 
rustling  echoes  from  the  back  storage  room—like 
something shifting among the plushies.”
 411 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
Description:

Layout: Small and cluttered, with narrow aisles 
packed with whimsical trinkets. A checkout 
counter at the front has an old, still-functioning 
cash register. The back storage room is half-
blocked by fallen shelves.

Threats: 1d4 Plushlings—small, stuffed 
animal-like zombies that animate when 
disturbed. One Ambush Crawler is hidden 
behind the counter.

Hazards: Some of the plush toys have been 
rigged with noisemakers. Stepping on them 
(Dexterity DC 12 to avoid) triggers high-pitched 
sounds, increasing Tension by +1d4 and 
alerting zombies in nearby rooms.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
“Best Dad Ever” Mug – Sturdy 
enough to be a blunt weapon (1d4 
damage).
2
Limited Edition Plush (Sealed) – 
Worth 75 SV if sold or traded.
3
Mystery Box (Locked, DC 14 to 
open) – Contains a pocket knife 
(1d4 damage) and an old concert 
ticket stub (Lore clue).
4
“Emergency Clown Horn” – Can 
be used as a distraction, but raises 
Tension by +1d6 when sounded.
5
Keychain Stun Gun – Weak (1d4 
non-lethal damage, 3 uses), but can 
shock zombies for an escape 
chance (DC 13).
6
Gift Card Cache – Useless for 
spending, but could be burned 
for a morale boost (+5 SV).
Ambiguous Lore Clues
Scattered around Curio Cove are cryptic hints about the 
apocalypse’s origins:
d4 Roll Lore Clue
1
Handwritten note on a greeting 
card: “It’s not a virus. They wake 
up if you listen too long.”
2
Mall flyer: “BIG SALE: Free plush 
with every purchase! Limit one per 
customer… no refunds.”
3
Bloodstained receipt: 
“Transaction declined. Customer 
refused to leave.”
4
Security Memo: “Reports of 
missing stock in Curio Cove. 
Store manager swears plushies 
are moving overnight. Hysterics. 
Reprimanded.”
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action/Loot
SV Reward
Securing Curio Cove
200 SV
Finding Limited 
Edition Plush
75 SV
Discovering Storage 
Room Cache
50 SV
Mystery Box 
Contents
Varied SV
Tension Impact:

Triggering plush noisemakers: +1d4 Tension

Breaking glass display cases: +1d6 Tension

Setting off Clown Horn: +1d6 Tension

Killing a Plushling without alerting others: 
No Tension Increase
 412 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Enemies
Plushlings (1d4) – Sentient 
Stuffed Animals
Small, animated stuffed creatures with exposed teeth 
where stitching has torn away. They move awkwardly 
but fast.

HP: 8

AC: 12 (soft body, but agile)

Attack: Claw Rake (1d6 damage) or Latch-On 
Bite (1d4, grapple DC 12 to remove).

Special Ability: If destroyed loudly, nearby 
zombies gain +10ft movement speed for 1d4 
rounds (their “screams” agitate the horde).
Ambush Crawler – Half-Buried 
Under the Counter
One of the original store clerks, now missing its lower 
half. It drags itself toward prey with unnatural 
persistence.

HP: 15

AC: 11

Attack: Grab & Bite (1d6+Grapple, DC 14 to 
escape).

Special Ability: Silent Stalker – It remains 
motionless until approached, then attacks 
with advantage on its first turn.
Survival Summary

Danger Level: Moderate (high if Plushlings 
trigger Tension)

Resource Value: Medium (some useful 
trinkets, valuable limited-edition plush)

Lore & Mystery: Strange hints about 
animated objects, odd disappearances.

sites.name: Fine Cuts Deli
sites.bookText:
Fine Cuts Deli (Shop #43)
“The air in Fine Cuts Deli is thick with the scent of old 
spices and something far less appetizing. The faded 
black-and-white  checkerboard  tiles  are  slick  with 
unknown  stains,  and  the  long  deli  counter  stands 
abandoned, its glass case smeared and cracked. A 
massive, old-fashioned meat slicer sits at the center, 
its blade still glistening as if recently used. Hanging 
from the ceiling, desiccated sausages and hunks of 
cured meat sway slightly in an unseen breeze. The 
flickering neon ‘Fresh Cuts Daily’ sign hums above 
the empty register, casting eerie shadows. A rhythmic 
drip…drip…drip echoes from somewhere in the back. 
Something—or someone—has been here recently.”
General Description
Fine Cuts Deli was once a bustling butcher shop, 
specializing in premium cured meats, fresh sandwiches, 
and gourmet cheeses. Now, it is a chilling relic of what 
was, its neatly arranged trays of cold cuts long since 
turned to rot.

Layout:
o
A long deli counter with a shattered 
display case, smeared with dried 
blood.
o
A storage freezer in the back, its 
metal door slightly ajar.
o
Hanging sausages and meats, some 
still looking… suspiciously fresh.
o
A rusty meat slicer, the blade 
appearing too clean.
Threats: (Roll 1d6 on entry)
| d6 Roll | Encounter | 
| 1-2 | 2d4 Shamblers – Rotting former customers 
stumble out of the back room. | 
| 3 | The Butcher – A hulking, apron-wearing zombie 
with a cleaver embedded in its arm (mini-boss). | 
| 4 | Hanging Meat Crawlers – Limbless zombies 
strung up with hooks, still twitching. | 
| 5 | Ambush! Crawler Swarm – Hidden under 
tables, 1d6 zombies grab at ankles. | 
| 6 | Human Survivor (Trapped) – A paranoid, knife-
wielding survivor barricaded in the freezer. |
Hazards: (Roll 1d4 to add an environmental 
 413 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
challenge)
| d4 Roll | Hazard |
| 1 | Slick Floors – Greasy tiles make movement 
treacherous (DEX save DC 14 or fall prone). | 
| 2 | Live Wires – Exposed electrical cords spark 
dangerously (touching deals 1d8 shock damage). | 
| 3 | Gas Leak – The air is filled with an unlit but 
dangerous gas (any flame weapon ignites an 
explosion for 3d6 damage). | 
| 4 | Locked Freezer Door – Something bangs from 
inside, but should it be opened? |
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Butcher’s Cleaver – A hefty 
weapon (1d8 slashing, +1 vs 
zombies due to weight).
2
Sealed Meat Rations – Vacuum-
packed salami, still safe to eat (10 
SV per pack, 1d6 packs found).
3
Rusty Meat Slicer (Weapon Trap) 
– Can be rigged to create a deadly 
ambush (1d10 damage on first 
use).
4
Blood-Stained Ledger – A book 
detailing late-night shipments 
labeled “Special Meat Deliveries”. 
(Lore Clue)
5
Preserved Sausages – Non-
perishable, can be traded or eaten 
(worth 20 SV).
6
Hidden Cash Register Drawer – 
Contains $200 in old cash 
(worthless) and a fully loaded 
.38 Revolver (25 SV) with six 
rounds.
Ambiguous Lore:
Scattered throughout Fine Cuts Deli, players may find 
unsettling hints about what went wrong here. Each clue 
contradicts the others, adding to the mall’s apocalyptic 
mystery.
d4 Roll Lore Clue
1
Bloodied Military Dog Tag – 
Belonged to a soldier from 
Containment Protocol Zulu. Why 
was he here?
2
Handwritten Note (Crumpled in a 
Locker) – Reads: “The Butcher 
feeds them at night. Don’t let him 
see you.”
3
Strange Black Sausage with 
Alien Symbols – A grotesque, 
unidentifiable meat product that 
pulsates slightly when touched.
4
Cultist Graffiti Scrawled on the 
Wall – Reads: “The feast never 
ends. The flesh will rise.”
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action or Loot
SV Reward
Securing Fine Cuts 
Deli
250 SV
Butcher’s Cleaver 
(weapon)
30 SV
Sealed Meat Rations 
(per pack)
10 SV each (1d6 
packs)
Hidden Cash Register 
Revolver
25 SV
Preserved Sausages
20 SV
Rusty Meat Slicer 
(Trap Use)
15 SV
Tension Impact:

Foraging & Searching – +1d4 Tension per 
minute spent looting.

Triggering a Noise-Based Hazard (meat 
slicer, freezer, live wires) – +2d6 Tension.

Killing The Butcher (mini-boss fight) – No 
immediate Tension, but +1d4 from echoes of 
 414 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
the fight.

Exploding Gas Leak – +3d6 Tension mall-
wide.
Enemies & Stats
Shamblers (2d4)

HP: 12 each

AC: 8

Attacks: Bite (1d6, 5% infection chance)

Speed: Slow

Special: Groaning attracts more zombies if the 
fight drags on.
The Butcher (Mini-Boss)

HP: 30

AC: 12

Attacks:
o
Cleave (1d10 slashing, hits two 
targets if within range).
o
Meat Hook Grab (Grapple, DC 14 to 
escape, takes 1d6 bleeding damage 
per round).

Special Ability:
o
The Feast Never Ends – If The 
Butcher lands a killing blow, he gains 
10 HP by feeding.
o
Horror Aura – Anyone who fails a DC 
12 Wisdom save hesitates in fear 
(loses next attack).

Tension Increase: +2d6 if The Butcher is 
encountered.
Survivor (Trapped in the 
Freezer)

HP: 18

Weapon: Rusty Fillet Knife (1d6 damage)

Disposition:
o
Paranoid: May attack if startled.
o
Grateful: If convinced to join, provides 
survival knowledge (rolls with 
advantage on scavenging checks).

Tension Impact:
o
Rescuing him lowers mall-wide 
Tension by -1d4 (new ally improves 
morale).
o
Killing him raises Tension by +2d4 
(others may hear or find out).
Survival XP & Bonuses
Action
XP Bonus
Securing the deli 
without alerting 
zombies
250 SV
Defeating The 
Butcher
+150 SV
Finding the revolver 
in the cash register
+50 SV
Successfully setting 
up the Meat Slicer 
as a trap
+75 SV
Rescuing the 
Survivor from the 
freezer
+200 SV
Learning the full 
ambiguous lore 
clues
+100 SV
Fine Cuts Deli is a creepy, tense encounter filled with 
valuable resources, a terrifying boss, and multiple 
layers of lore to deepen the mystery of the mall’s 
 415 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
fall. Players can brute force their way through, sneak 
around carefully, or uncover disturbing truths while 
trying to stay alive.

sites.name: Value Grocers
sites.bookText:
Value Grocers (Shop #44)
“The smell of rotting produce and stale air hangs 
heavy as you step into Value Grocers. Metal shelves 
stand half-empty, their remaining contents coated in 
dust or gnawed by rodents. Flickering overhead lights 
cast  long  shadows,  making  it  difficult  to  tell  if 
something is shuffling in the next aisle or if it’s just 
your imagination. A freezer door slowly creaks open 
and closed as if someone—or something—left it ajar. 
Broken glass crunches underfoot near the checkout 
counters, where an abandoned register screen still 
flickers  with  a  transaction  that  will  never  be 
completed. Somewhere in the distance, a soft thud 
echoes, followed by an unsettling silence…”
Description:

Layout:
o
A large, open supermarket with long 
aisles, partially looted shelves, and 
flickering fluorescent lights.
o
A checkout counter with broken 
registers, loose receipts, and scattered 
dollar bills.
o
Deli & Butcher Counter: Blood-
stained tiles and an overturned meat 
slicer.
o
Storage Room: A locked door with 
“AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY” 
in faded lettering.
o
Freezer Section: Cold mist leaks from 
a half-broken freezer door.
Threats: (Roll 1d6 for enemy presence on entry)
| d6 Roll | Encounter | 
| 1-2 | 4 Shamblers – Slowly wandering between

sites.name: Mini Mode
sites.bookText:
Mini Mode (Shop #45)
“A faded pastel sign with cartoon animals welcomes 
you  to  Mini  Mode,  a  boutique  once  filled  with 
laughter and the hum of parents browsing for their  
children. Now, the air is thick with dust, and the tiny 
mannequins  dressed  in  miniature  suits  and  frilly 
dresses stand eerily still, their plastic eyes reflecting 
the  dim  light.  A  lone  stroller,  overturned  near  the 
entrance, rests beside scattered plush toys—one of 
which inexplicably rocks slightly as if something just 
nudged it. The store is deathly silent… except for the 
faint creak of something moving in the stockroom at  
the back.”
Description

Layout:
o
Mini Mode is a mid-sized children’s 
boutique with narrow aisles filled with 
racks of tiny outfits, formalwear, and 
colorful onesies.
o
The checkout counter still has a 
functioning cash register with receipts 
from what may have been the final day 
of sales.
o
A changing room area sits in the 
back, its curtains swaying gently 
despite the absence of wind.
o
A small play area with a plastic slide 
and a rocking horse is near the back—
one of the ride-on toys sways ever so 
slightly.
o
A storage room door in the back is 
partially ajar, revealing shadows 
moving inside.

Threats:
o
“Lost Children” Zombies (1d4+1) – 
These were once children but have 
become something… else. They hide 
among the racks and dart out 
suddenly, fast and erratic. (See enemy 
stats below.)
o
Silent Stalker (1) – A former store 
employee, now turned zombie, lurks in 
the storage room. It moves eerily quiet 
and only attacks when backs are 
turned.

Hazards:
o
Toppling Mannequins – The first time 
a player moves too fast in an aisle, 
1d4 mannequins fall loudly, raising 
Mall Tension by +1d4.
o
Cradle Alarm Trap – An old 
mechanical baby cradle alarm is still 
active in the play area. If bumped, it 
plays a tinny lullaby at full volume, 
attracting zombies from neighboring 
stores within 2d6 rounds.
o
Narrow Aisles – Movement is halved 
in the clothing racks unless players 
deliberately push through (STR check 
DC 12).
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Item Found
1
Tiny Tuxedo (Trade Value 30 SV) 
– A pristine, high-end child’s tuxedo 
that could be valuable to a collector.
2
Walkie-Talkie (Functional) – A 
child’s toy walkie-talkie set, but 
oddly, static crackles when turned 
on, hinting at possible 
transmissions. (Range: 500 ft, 
intermittent.)
3
Mom’s Emergency Bag (Medical 
 418 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Kit, 50 SV) – Found near the 
stroller. Contains 1x bandage, 1x 
painkiller, and 1x child’s inhaler 
(removes breathing penalties).
4
Old Teddy Bear (Morale Boost, 20 
SV) – This bear was clearly loved. If 
kept, it reduces Stress for NPC 
survivors or can be traded for 
comfort.
5
Backroom Supply Box – If the 
storage room is searched (DC 14 
Investigation), contains 1d4 snack 
packs (Food, 5 SV each) and a 
rusty box cutter (1d4 damage, 
concealable weapon).
6
Creepy Doll (Lore Clue) – A 
child’s doll with an eerie stitched-
on smile. When pressed, it utters, 
“Mommy says the monsters 
aren’t real.”
Ambiguous Lore:
Hidden clues suggest something strange happened 
before the outbreak:
d4 
Roll
Lore Fragment Found
1
Bloodstained Employee Memo – A 
note from the manager about “odd 
sickness spreading among the kids 
in the daycare section.”
2
Forgotten Shopping List – A 
crumpled receipt with a note on the 
back: “Stay in the play area! The 
bad people can’t see you there!”
3
Mall Surveillance Photo (Stained) 
– A black-and-white image showing 
a woman pushing an empty 
stroller, yet shadows suggest 
something inside.
4
Creepy Child’s Drawing – Depicts 
a child holding hands with 
something huge and faceless, 
with the words “My new friend” 
scrawled in red crayon.

+50 SV

(Tuxedo, Teddy Bear, 
etc.)
Varies (20-50 SV)
Discovering Lore 
(each clue found)
+25 SV each
Tension Impact
Action
Tension Increase
Loud Mannequin Fall
+1d4
Baby Cradle Alarm 
Triggered
+2d6
Gunfire Used in Store
+1d6 per shot
Leaving the Store 
Unchecked
Zombies may spread 
to nearby locations
Enemy Encounters
Lost Children (Fast Zombie 
Pack)

HP: 10 each

AC: 12

Movement: 40 ft. (faster than standard 
zombies)

Attacks: Claw (1d6), Bite (1d4 + chance of 
infection)
 419 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall

Special:
o
Erratic Speed: Must be attacked with 
Disadvantage unless the player 
predicts their movement pattern 
(Insight DC 14).
o
Hide Among Racks: On a turn, can 
attempt to disappear into clothing 
aisles (Stealth DC 15 to detect).
o
Creepy Giggle: Once per encounter, 
they all laugh in unison, causing Fear 
(DC 13 Will Save) for 1 round.
Silent Stalker (Lurking 
Zombie)

HP: 20

AC: 13

Movement: 30 ft. (completely silent)

Attacks: Chokehold (Grapple DC 14, 1d8 
damage per turn)

Special:
o
Ambush Predator: Remains 
completely still until players turn 
their backs or check the storage 
room.
o
No Moans, No Growls: Unlike normal 
zombies, it makes zero noise when 
moving, requiring a Perception 
check (DC 16) to notice.
o
Head-Tilt Mimicry: If detected before 
attacking, it tilts its head and slowly 
mimics the players’ movements for 
several seconds before lunging.
Survival XP & Rewards

Successfully clearing the store without 
triggering Cradle Alarm: +200 SV

Defeating the Lost Children Pack: +50 SV

Defeating the Silent Stalker: +75 SV

Discovering hidden Lore Clues: +25 SV each

Securing valuable trade items (Tuxedo, Teddy 
Bear, etc.): 20-50 SV each
Final Notes & Optional 
Encounter Hooks

A Survivor’s Fate: The back storage room has 
bloody handprints on the wall, but no body. 
A survivor may have escaped—or something 
worse happened.

Strange Transmission: If the toy walkie-
talkie is turned on, it randomly picks up a 
child’s voice whispering, “They’re still 
here… hiding in the dark.”

The Unused Register: The checkout cash 
register beeps once, despite no power. The 
receipt roll prints a final message: “Thank you 
for shopping. You should leave now.”

sites.name: Bloomscape
sites.bookText:
Bloomscape (Shop #46 - 
Upper Level)
“Thick vines spill over shattered pots, curling around 
toppled shelves and cracked ceramic planters. The 
air here is damp, heavy with the scent of soil, decay, 
and something faintly floral—something wrong. Dim 
skylights filter in an eerie green light, illuminating the 
tangle of overgrown ferns and ivy that have reclaimed 
the  shop.  A  rusted  sprinkler  system  drips  steadily 
from  the  ceiling,  creating  a  soft  pattering  sound 
against the floor. Somewhere beneath the foliage, 
something shifts.”
General Description
Bloomscape was once a thriving indoor garden 
center, selling houseplants, gardening tools, and exotic 
flora. Now, it is an overgrown ruin, partially reclaimed 
by nature. The sprinklers appear to have malfunctioned 
long ago, keeping the soil damp and accelerating the 
growth of its now-wild inhabitants.

Layout: Overgrown display shelves, broken 
ceramic pots, scattered gardening supplies. 
The shop extends deeper into a dark storage 
area, where the plants grow even thicker.
 420 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level

Threats: Certain plants seem… off. Strange 
pulsing spores drift lazily in the air. The 
“roots” in the back move occasionally, as if 
something is nesting within.

Hazards: Low visibility, damp floors (Dex DC 
12 to avoid slipping). Any loud noise dislodges 
pollen clouds (CON save DC 13 or suffer mild 
hallucinations for 1 minute).
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (Roll 1d4 upon 
entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Pollen Spores Release: A 
disturbance causes a cloud of 
bioluminescent spores to erupt. 
(CON save DC 13 or suffer mild 
hallucinations for 1 minute—
disadvantage on Perception and 
Investigation.)
2
Hidden Vine Trap: A creeping vine 
grapples the first survivor to step 
into the back storage area (STR DC 
14 to break free).
3
Rotten Floorboard Collapse: A 
section of floor gives way (DEX 
save DC 12). On failure, the 
character falls into a crawlspace 
beneath the shop, where something 
is waiting (2 Crawler Zombies).
4
Fungus Growths Burst: Stepping 
in the wrong place releases toxic 
spores (CON save DC 14 or take 
1d6 poison damage and suffer 
nausea for 1d4 rounds).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Rusty Garden Shears – Heavy-
duty, still sharp. Can be used as a 
makeshift weapon (1d6 slashing).
2
Packets of Untouched Seeds – 
May be useful for long-term food 
sustainability (Trade Value: 20 SV 
per packet).
3
Old Gas-Powered Hedge 
Trimmer – Loud, but deals 2d6 
slashing damage (must refuel with 
gasoline).
4
Fertilizer Bags – Can be turned 
into improvised explosives with 
the right materials (Crafting DC 15).
5
Rainwater Collection Barrels 
(Half-Full) – Usable for long-term 
water storage (+2 Days of Water 
per barrel).
6
“Experimental BioDyne Growth 
Compound” – A sealed vial 
labeled with corporate branding 
and a biohazard warning. Could 
be valuable—or incredibly 
dangerous.
Ambiguous Lore (Roll 1d4 
upon searching the shop)
d4 Roll Hidden Clue
1
Handwritten note (water-
stained): “I don’t think this place 
was just a garden store… The 
plants don’t die like they should.”
2
Old BioDyne Memo: “Test Site C 
contamination observed—
recommend immediate quarantine 
of all organic materials.”
3
Cultist Symbol Carved into 
Wood: The roots seem to grow 
towards it, as if responding to its 
presence.
4
Half-buried Military Gas Mask: 
Issued by a government 
response team. The filter is 
clogged with strange spores.
 421 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
Potential Enemies (1d6 
Encounter Table)
d6 Roll Zombie/Threat Type
1-2
Shamblers (1d4) – Entangled in 
vines, these zombies move 
sluggishly through the overgrowth.
3
Rootbound Corpse – A body 
fused with the vines. It struggles to 
move but can still attack (grapple-
based attacks).
4
Crawler Zombies (2-3) – Hidden 
beneath soil, grab ankles and 
attempt to pull survivors under 
(STR DC 14 to resist).
5
Fungal Walker – A zombie 
covered in fungal growths. When 
killed, it releases a cloud of 
spores (CON save DC 14 or suffer 
mild poisoning).
6
Something Else… – Deep in the 
back of the shop, roots pulse like 
veins. Something ancient is 
buried here. (GM’s choice—
Lovecraftian horror, mutated 
creature, or boss encounter).
Monster Stats
Fungal Walker (Infected Variant)

HP: 18

AC: 12

Attacks: Claw (1d6) / Bite (1d6, Infection 
Chance)

Special:
o
Death Burst: On death, releases 
spores in a 10-ft radius (CON save 
DC 14 or take 1d6 poison damage 
and suffer disadvantage on attack rolls 
for 1 minute).
Rootbound Corpse

HP: 20

AC: 14

Attacks: Grasping Vines (1d6 bludgeoning + 
Grapple)

Special:
o
Stationary Horror: Cannot move, but 
can grapple and pull victims into the 
plant mass (STR DC 14 to resist).
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action or Loot
SV Reward
Securing 
Bloomscape 
completely
300 SV
Experimental 
BioDyne Compound 
(Lore Item)
100 SV
Water Collection 
Barrels (Each, +2 
Days Water)
50 SV
Functional Hedge 
Trimmer (Loud, 
High Damage)
75 SV
Fertilizer Bags 
(Improvised 
Explosives)
60 SV
Untouched Seed 
Packets (Per Packet)
20 SV
Tension Impact

Any loud noises (breaking pots, chainsaws, 
or gunfire) instantly increase Tension by 
1d4+2.

If players disturb the “Something Else” in 
the back, roll 1d6 Tension immediately.

Using fire (Molotovs, torches, etc.) in this 
room will cause a runaway blaze—escalating 
Tension by 2d6** but clearing the infestation.**
 422 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Additional GM Hooks & 
Weird Events
(Optional, roll 1d6 at any point for a weird event!)
d6 Roll Unusual Event
1
Something Moves in the Soil – A 
root shifts unnaturally beneath a 
player’s feet.
2
A Whisper on the Wind – 
Someone hears their name 
whispered from deeper in the 
store.
3
Strange Blooms – A flower opens 
up, revealing something fleshy 
inside.
4
The Plants React – A dead 
zombie’s veins begin to turn 
green, as if being absorbed.
5
Visions – For a moment, the room 
looks pristine and alive, as if 
before the outbreak. Then it fades.
6
A Low Hum Begins… – 
Something underneath is waking 
up.

sites.name: Write Away
sites.bookText:
Write Away (Shop #47) – 
Stationery Store
“The shelves of ‘Write Away’ are packed with colorful 
journals,  novelty  pens,  and  planners  promising 
productivity in a world that no longer functions. A thin 
layer of dust coats everything, except for a single 
counter  where  it  looks  like  someone  was  recently 
scribbling in a notebook. The faint scent of old paper 
and dried ink lingers in the air, mixing with something 
else… something faintly metallic. A few overturned 
racks have spilled greeting cards onto the floor, their 
cheerful messages now eerily out of place. A neon 
‘SALE’ sign still flickers weakly above the register, 
casting strange shadows on the far wall. And then, 
just  as  you  step  forward—was  that  the  rustle  of 
paper, or something moving behind the counter?”
General Description

Layout: A tidy, compact store with well-
organized shelves of journals, greeting cards, 
and office supplies. A long counter at the back 
contains an old register, and behind it is a 
storage area with more inventory. The 
overhead lights flicker intermittently, creating 
unsettling movements in the reflection of glass-
covered display cases.

Threats: Something rustles near the back of 
the shop, either a lone scavenger or something 
worse.

Hazards:
o
Unstable Shelves – An entire display 
could collapse if bumped, causing 
+1d6 Tension and blocking 
movement.
o
Ink Spill – A large stain of leaked ink 
makes the floor dangerously slippery 
(Dexterity DC 12 or fall prone).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll
Notable Items
1
High-Quality Fountain Pen – Still 
functional, oddly pristine. Can be 
used to sign documents, trade for 
10 SV, or as a very unsatisfying 
shiv (1 damage).
2
Planners & Journals – Useless in 
terms of productivity but could be 
sold to certain NPCs or hoarders 
for 5 SV each (up to 3 available).
3
Sharp Letter Opener – Hidden in 
the register drawer, functions as a 
1d4 piercing weapon.
4
Box of Permanent Markers – 
Can be used to create signs, mark 
paths, or graffiti warnings for 
others (5 SV).
5
Locked Notebook – The last few 
pages are ripped out, but there are 
 423 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
frantic notes about “THEY 
WATCH FROM THE PAPER, 
DON’T WRITE TOO MUCH.” 
Unlocking it (Dex DC 14) reveals 
indecipherable scribbles and a 
single, cryptic note: “The ink is 
alive.”
6
Scavenger’s Cache (Hidden in 
Storage Closet) – Someone’s 
stash of 2 ration packs (10 SV 
each), a Swiss Army knife (15 
SV), and a half-filled bottle of 
painkillers (25 SV).
Ambiguous Lore: Strange 
Writing
Scattered throughout the shop, players may find 
strange written messages—whether warnings, mad 
scribbles, or something else entirely.
d6 Roll Mysterious Note Found
1
A sticky note on the register reads: 
“Don’t use the red pens. The red 
ones are his.”
2
A journal left open on the counter 
contains repeated phrases: “I see 
them. I see them. I see them.”
3
A greeting card has been altered—
crossed-out words now read: “They 
know when you are sleeping. They 
know when you’re awake.”
4
A child’s handwriting on the back of 
a receipt: “Mommy went into the 
paper. She’s still in there.”
5
A receipt from “BioDyne Corp.” for 
“bulk ink shipments,” with a strange 
note: “Lot #66 - DO NOT 
DISTRIBUTE TO PUBLIC”
6
A crude map of the mall with a 
section circled in red ink labeled: 
“DO NOT GO HERE.”
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action or Loot
SV Reward
Securing ‘Write 
Away’ entirely
150 SV
Finding & 
deciphering the 
notebook
50 SV
Discovering the 
hidden scavenger 
cache
75 SV
Salvaging sellable 
items (planners, 
markers, etc.)
10-25 SV
Tension Impact

Disturbing Shelves – Knocking over a shelf 
increases Tension by +1d6.

Reading the Wrong Note – Certain writings 
(like the child’s note) might cause a strange 
paranoia effect, increasing Tension for the 
character who reads it.

Ink Spill Mishap – If someone slips, they must 
roll Stealth DC 14 to avoid alerting nearby 
zombies.
Potential Enemies
Upon entry, roll a d6 to determine if something is lurking 
in the store.
d6 Roll Encounter
1-2
Paper Scraper (1) – A skeletal 
zombie with shredded, ink-stained 
skin. Seems drawn to writing 
materials.
3
Scared Scavenger – A lone 
survivor hiding behind the counter. 
Will react based on the party’s 
actions.
4
Shambler (1d4) – Mindless 
undead, sluggishly pushing over 
 424 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
bookshelves as they wander.
5
Inkspawn Horror – A faceless 
humanoid-shaped entity dripping 
black ink, trying to write something 
with its clawed fingers.
6
Nothing – For now…
New Monster: Paper Scraper
A bizarre zombie that seems partially composed of 
shredded paper and ink-stained flesh. It moves 
erratically, scratching at walls, dragging its hands 
across surfaces as if trying to write something…

HP: 14

AC: 12


must roll Wisdom DC 13 or suffer Paranoia (-1 
to Perception & Insight for 1 hour).

o

symbols that increase Tension by +1 
every 10 minutes if not destroyed.
o
Weakness to Fire – Takes double 
damage from fire-based attacks.
o

to writing materials, it will momentarily 
ignore combat to scrawl symbols on 
nearby walls.

Mini-Boss)
A writhing humanoid figure composed of black ink, 
constantly shifting between liquid and solid states. Its 
movements are jerky, as if being erased and redrawn at 
the same time.

disorientation (-1 to attack rolls for 1 
round).

target for 1d4 rounds (Dex DC 14 to 
avoid).

o
Weakness to Light – Any direct light 
source reduces its AC to 12.
o
Shadow Meld – Can vanish into pools 
of ink and reappear elsewhere.

Write Away may seem like just a simple stationery 
shop, but the presence of strange writings, eerie 
messages, and unnatural creatures make it a disturbing 
location. If the players choose to investigate the odd 
ink-related events further, they might uncover a deeper, 
more sinister mystery behind the mall’s apocalypse… or 
they might wish they had never started reading.

sites.name: The Comfort Zone
sites.bookText:
The Comfort Zone (Shop 
#48)
“This furniture outlet was once a showroom of plush 
recliners,  overstuffed  sectionals,  and  glass  coffee 
tables. Now, the fake leather on the couches has 
started  peeling,  dust  covers  everything,  and  the 
silence  is  broken  only  by  the  occasional  creak  of 
settling furniture. Some of the recliners are still in a 
reclined position—though whether someone left them 
that way or something else did remains unclear. A 
single  ceiling  fan  rotates  lazily  above,  making  a 
rhythmic clicking noise. The air carries the faint scent 
of  mildew,  wood  polish,  and  something  else—
something rotten.”
General Description

Layout:
The Comfort Zone was once a mid-range 
furniture outlet, showcasing sofas, recliners, 
and dining sets arranged in mock living room 
displays. Several fake “show apartments” 
were set up, complete with coffee tables, 
bookshelves, and decorative items. A staff-
only storeroom in the back contains boxed 
 425 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
furniture, assembly kits, and possibly, hidden 
supplies.

Threats:
o
Couch Crawlers (1d3) – Half-
mummified zombies wedged between 
cushions or slumped within recliners, 
waiting to strike if disturbed.
o
Display Mannequins (1d2) – Human-
shaped mannequins positioned in 
“relaxed poses” on the furniture. Upon 
closer inspection, some appear to 
have been gnawed on.
o
Something Under the Rugs – The 
carpet near the back of the store is 
slightly raised, as if covering 
something…

Hazards:
o
Unstable Shelving: Bookshelves and 
entertainment centers can be knocked 
over (Intelligence DC 12 to notice 
before it collapses). If a survivor leans 
on one or bumps into it, make a 
Dexterity DC 14 save or take 1d6 
bludgeoning damage and add +2d4 
Tension due to the noise.
o
The “Trap Recliner” – One of the 
recliners near the middle of the store is 
damaged; sitting in it locks it into a 
reclined position (Strength DC 15 to 
break free). If occupied when zombies 
attack, the survivor is Restrained for 1 
round.
Loot & Interactables
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Heavy-Duty Flashlight (Still works, 
lasts for 1d6 hours – 15 SV).
2
Luxury Throw Blanket (Can be 
used for warmth or camouflage – 10 
SV).
3
Leather Couch Cushion (Can 
function as a crude shield – +1 AC 
in melee, 20 SV).
4
Decorative Fireplace Poker 
(Counts as a 1d6 melee weapon, 
metal, sturdy – 15 SV).
5
Safe Behind Picture Frame 
(Locked, Dexterity DC 15 to open; 
contains $500 in old cash (5 SV) 
and 1d4 handgun bullets (5 SV 
each)).
6
Back Room Tool Kit (Contains 
screwdriver, hammer, nails; used 
for barricades, 25 SV).
Hidden Loot:
- Survival Manual: A copy of “Home Defense & 
Improvised Barricades”—grants Advantage on checks 
related to fortification (Intelligence-based). Found 
behind a fallen bookshelf.
- Emergency Rations (2) – Found inside a staff locker 
in the back; expired but still edible (15 SV each).
- Secret Stash: Under one of the recliners, an old 
backpack contains a working Walkman with 
batteries, one cassette tape, and a bloodstained 
note (lore clue).
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered throughout The Comfort Zone are unsettling 
hints about what might have happened here before the 
mall fell. These clues deliberately contradict one 
another, keeping the cause of the apocalypse 
mysterious.
d4 
Roll
Ambiguous Clue
1
Security Camera (Still 
Functioning?) – A small blinking 
red light suggests at least one 
camera is still operational. But 
where is it transmitting to?
2
Blood-Stained Employee Roster – 
A list of employees, with some 
names crossed out in red ink and 
“Sent Below” written next to them.
3
Customer Complaint Forms (Half-
Filled Out) – One mentions strange 
mold growing on the furniture before 
the outbreak. Another describes “an 
unbearable rotting smell” from the 
 426 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
backroom.
4
Hidden Radio Transmission – The 
Walkman tape, when played, 
contains a muffled voice 
recording: “They locked us in… 
they said it was for our safety… 
but we heard them screaming 
inside the walls.”

Possible Enemy

1-2

concealed in the furniture, lunging 
at anyone searching too deeply.
3
Lurking Shambler (1) – A single, 
slow-moving undead near the 
backroom.
4
Recliner Corpse (1) – A zombie 
wedged into a motorized recliner. 
It only activates if disturbed.
5
“Customer Service 
Representative” (Unique 
Zombie) – A former employee, still 
wearing a name tag, that 
whispers hoarsely instead of 
groaning.
6
Mannequin Horror (1) – A store 
display figure that looks human 
from afar, but closer inspection 
reveals its “flesh” is covered in 
hard, fungal-like growths.
Monster Stat Blocks
Couch Crawler (Zombie Variant)

HP: 10

AC: 12

Atk: Slam (1d6 damage, DC 12 STR to escape 
if grappled)

Special: Concealed Ambush – Automatically 
surprises anyone searching furniture unless 
Perception (DC 14) is passed.
“Customer Service Representative” (Unique 
Zombie)

HP: 18

AC: 13

Atk: Whispered Lullaby (1d4 Psychic, DC 12 
WIS save or become Disoriented for 1 round)

Special: Instead of groaning, it whispers 
apologies and repeats customer service 
scripts in a breathy, unnatural voice.
 427 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
Mannequin Horror

HP: 22

AC: 14 (Hardened fungal plating)

Atk: Claw Swipe (1d8 damage)

Special: Silent Stalker – It does not move 
while being directly watched, but advances 
rapidly when unobserved.
Final Notes & Strategy

This shop is ideal for scavenging, offering 
survival gear and clues.

Smart survivors can avoid combat by 
carefully searching the furniture before 
touching anything.

Triggering loud events (like the safe or 
bookshelves) could turn this from a loot spot 
into a desperate fight for survival.

sites.name: Signal Boost
sites.bookText:
Signal Boost (Shop #49 - 
Wireless Store)
“The flickering glow of still-active LED signs casts a 
sickly  blue  light  over  the  trashed  interior.  Phone 
cases, tangled chargers, and shattered screens litter 
the floor. A toppled display stand crackles weakly as 
a half-dead tablet loops an old advertisement for an 
‘Unlimited Plan.’ The air is stale, tinged with the acrid 
scent of burnt plastic. Amidst the wreckage, a single 
phone vibrates on the counter—despite there being 
no working networks left.”
Description:

Layout: A small, cramped tech store with 
broken glass counters and overturned shelves. 
A display wall still holds an array of mobile 
accessories, and a few locked cabinets house 
premium products. The backroom, partially 
barricaded, holds old stock and maintenance 
equipment.

Threats:
o
1d3 Crawler Zombies hidden behind 
the service counter, waiting for 
movement.
o
1d6 Shamblers outside the store—if 
noise is made, they may attempt to 
push in.

Hazards:
o
Glass Shards: Moving carelessly 
risks stepping on broken glass (DEX 
Save DC 12 or take 1 piercing 
damage, +1d4 Tension).
o
Exposed Wires: A severed cable near 
the counter still sparks. Contact 
causes 1d4 electric damage.
o
Ghost Signal: A few devices still 
connect to a mysterious, encrypted 
network broadcasting eerie messages.

loaded Glock 19 (Pistol, 9mm, 25 SV, 10 rounds).
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered among the store’s digital records and 
lingering transmissions are conflicting hints about the 
nature of the apocalypse. Survivors may piece together 
various clues, none of which tell the full story:
d4 Roll Ambiguous Clue
1

Caller: “You don’t understand… 
this wasn’t supposed to happen. 
The signal is spreading. Destroy 
the towers. Stop listening.”

trapped in the food court. Mall WiFi 
still works. Someone, anyone, if 
you see this… help.”

“Urgent: The waveform interference 
is accelerating subject reanimation. 
We need to shut down all 5G relays 
immediately—before THEY adapt.”
4
Weird Signal Broadcast: A 
looping transmission in a 
language no one recognizes, 
punctuated by bursts of static 
and what sounds like chanting.
Tension Impact:


increase.

aware of movement.)

zombies react.)


Player must make a Wisdom Save (DC 14) 
or suffer mild paranoia.

the backroom, scribbling symbols onto phone cases. 
His skin is covered in self-inflicted circuit-like carvings. 
He grips a screwdriver like a weapon and speaks in 
cryptic warnings:
“It’s in the waves. It’s in the air. You hear it too, don’t 
you? The ones who listen too long… they change.”






Signal Boost offers more than just standard looting—it 
presents a unique digital horror aspect to the mall’s 
apocalypse. The ghost signal, encrypted messages, 
and deranged survivor make for an unsettling, 
paranoia-inducing encounter that leaves players 
questioning whether the apocalypse was purely 
biological… or something more.

sites.name: Paw Prints
sites.bookText:
Paw Prints (Shop #50)
“The  faint  scent  of  pet  shampoo  and  stale  kibble 
lingers in the air as you step into what was once a 
boutique  for  spoiled  pets.  Plush  dog  beds  are 
scattered across the floor, some clawed and torn. 
Racks of tiny outfits—dog tuxedos, cat hoodies, and 
bunny  bowties—hang  limply  from  their  displays, 
coated  in  a  thin  layer  of  dust.  Squeaky  toys  and 
rubber bones lay abandoned on the floor, some of 
them grotesquely chewed. In the far corner, a display 
of luxury pet food sits untouched, the labels promising 
‘Gourmet  Organic  Lamb  &  Rice’  for  pets  that  no 
longer exist. Somewhere in the distance, you hear a 
soft scratching sound… but is it just the wind against 
the glass, or something lurking inside?”
General Description

Layout: A small boutique filled with pet 
apparel, toys, and high-end animal care 
products. Shelves stocked with overpriced 
organic pet food, chew toys, and grooming kits. 
A caged-off grooming area in the back holds 
overturned crates and a still-running water 
basin dripping eerily into the drain. The store’s 
mascot—a giant, fluffy plush dog—sits in the 
corner, its glassy eyes reflecting the dim light.

Threats: Something is alive in here, but it’s not 
clear whether it’s human, zombie… or 
something else.

Hazards: Possible trapped or mutated animals, 
unstable shelving, and noise-sensitive hazards.
 430 

Zombie Mall
 
Upper Level
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps (Roll 1d4 on Entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Loose Cage Door – One of the 
backroom kennels swings open 
suddenly. It makes a sharp clang, 
potentially attracting nearby 
zombies (+1d4 Tension).
2
Rabid Survivor’s Trap – A 
previous occupant rigged a tripwire 
connected to dog leashes. Anyone 
who steps on it will be tangled 
(Dexterity DC 14 to avoid), creating 
loud noise if failed.
3
Knock Over Display – A 
precarious shelf filled with ceramic 
dog bowls and metal food 
containers teeters dangerously. Any 
major movement causes it to 
collapse, creating loud noise (+1d6 
Tension, 25% chance to summon 
1d4 zombies).
4
Toxic Pet Shampoo Spill – A 
bottle of industrial-strength flea 
shampoo has leaked, creating a 
slippery hazard (Dexterity DC 13 
to avoid falling, failure results in 
1d6 damage).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Luxury Pet Food (Sealed) – Can 
be used as rations (equivalent to 
5 food portions, 10 SV) or traded 
with desperate survivors.
2
Heavy-Duty Leash (Improvised 
Weapon) – Functions as a garrote 
(1d6 damage, grapples on 
successful hit, 15 SV).
3
Canine First Aid Kit – Contains 
d6 Roll Notable Items
antibiotics, bandages, and an anti-
bacterial spray. Equivalent to a 
medkit (20 SV).
4
Pet Carrier (Useful for 
Transporting Small Items) – Can 
be reinforced as an improvised 
storage container (15 SV).
5
Rubber Chew Toy (Silent 
Distraction Device) – Can be 
thrown to create a silent diversion, 
useful for stealth situations (10 SV).
6
Dog Whistle (Summons Nearby 
Dogs/Zombies?) – May attract 
feral animals or zombies within 
hearing range. Its usefulness is 
questionable… (10 SV).
Ambiguous Lore Clues (Roll 
1d4 when searching the store)
d4 Roll Ambiguous Clue
1
Bloody Paw Prints Leading Out 
the Back – They belong to 
something large. But… the door is 
still locked from the inside.
2
An Open Notebook Left on the 
Counter – The last entry is 
scribbled in shaky handwriting: 
“They’re still in here. They’re still in 
here. THEY’RE STILL IN HERE.”
3
A Missing Pet Poster – Someone 
was looking for their dog, but the 
date on it is from before the 
outbreak… and the ink looks fresh.
4
Security Camera Monitor (Still 
Functioning?) – The screen 
flickers, showing static-filled 
footage of something moving in 
the store just moments ago. But 
you’re the only ones inside… 
right?
 431 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall

on Entry or When Exploring 
Backroom)
d6 
Roll
Threat Type
1-2
Rabid Dogs (1d4 Feral Mutts) – 
Once loyal pets, these creatures 
have been driven mad by starvation. 
They are fast, aggressive, and will 
not hesitate to attack.
3
Caged Horror (Mutated Pet 
Experiment) – A large rotting 
mastiff with exposed ribs and 
unnatural growths. It has 
enhanced strength and resistance 
to damage. It lunges at the first 
person to enter the back room.
4
Lost Survivor (Delusional, 
Believes They Are a Dog Trainer) 
– This survivor barks orders at 
imaginary pets and may become 
violent if their “dogs” are threatened.
5
Puppy Swarm (1d6 Zombie 
Puppies) – Tiny, reanimated 
creatures silent until they strike, 
attempting to bite at ankles and drag 
survivors down.
6
Alpha Stray (Feral Pack Leader, 
Undead or Not?) – A massive 
wolfhound, scarred and starving, 
standing unnervingly still as it 
watches you from the shadows… 
before it decides whether you’re 
prey.






