sites.name: Golden Crust Bakery
sites.bookText:
Golden Crust Bakery (Shop 
#51)
“The scent of stale bread and mildew lingers in the 
air,  mixing  with  the  faint,  acrid  odor  of  something 
rotting. Dust covers the glass display cases, once 
filled  with  golden-brown  loaves  and  flaky  pastries. 
Long-dried dough is caked onto the industrial mixers 
behind the counter, and an overturned tray of half-
eaten  baguettes  sits  abandoned  on  the  floor.  Rat 
droppings  dot  the  wooden  shelves,  and  the 
occasional rustling hints at unseen scavengers. The 
large oven stands eerily cold, its door slightly ajar, as 
if  something—or  someone—was  interrupted  mid-
preparation. A faint, rhythmic tapping echoes from the 
storage room in the back…”
Description:

Layout:
A main storefront with shattered display 
cases, a kitchen and baking area lined with 
rusting industrial equipment, and a rear 
storage room with flour-covered shelves and 
large, rodent-infested sacks of grain.

Threats:
o
Shambler Bakers (1d3 zombies) – 
Wearing torn aprons, they mindlessly 
repeat old motions, kneading invisible 
dough and placing nothing into cold 
ovens.
o
The Dough Thing (Mutant, Large) – 
A grotesque mass of infected, 
fermenting dough mixed with human 
remains, still “rising” in the walk-in 
freezer.

Hazards:
o
Flour Dust Explosion – Any open 
flames (gunfire, torches, etc.) risk 
igniting airborne flour (Dexterity Save 
DC 14 to avoid 3d6 fire damage).
o
Slick Floors – Rotten butter and 
spilled oil cause slipping hazards 
(Dexterity Save DC 12 or fall Prone).
o
Rats in the Walls – Disturbing the 
wrong shelf (Wisdom Perception DC 
15) triggers a swarm of diseased rats 
to flood the room (inflicts 1d4 damage 
& minor infection risk).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Chef’s Butcher Knife (Counts as 
Machete, 1d8 Slashing, Silent) – 
Razor-sharp, still lodged in a cutting 
board.
2
Sealed Jars of Honey & Peanut 
Butter (Food, 10 SV each) – High-
calorie, long-lasting sustenance.
3
Old Recipe Book (Lore Clue, 25 
SV for morale boost) – Notes 
written in the margins hint at “The 
Sixth Meal Ritual.”
 433 

Upper Level
 
Zombie Mall
d6 Roll Notable Items
4
Industrial Flour Sacks (Trade 
Item, 15 SV each) – Still usable for 
making basic food, or setting traps.
5
Rusted Rolling Pin (Improvised 
Weapon, 1d6 Bludgeoning) – 
Sticky with dried blood, suggesting 
previous use.
6
Hidden Cache Behind Oven (Roll 
1d3 items from below) – A 
survivor’s stash tucked away 
from raiders.
Hidden Cache Loot (if found 
behind oven, roll 1d3 times)
d6 Roll Secret Items
1
Fire Axe (1d10 Slashing, Loud, 
+1d6 Tension if used) – A last 
resort weapon hidden in a flour 
sack.
2
Canned Goods (3x, 10 SV each) – 
Expired but still edible.
3
Antibiotics (Medical Item, 30 SV) 
– A rare bottle of infection-fighting 
pills.
4
Small Fuel Canister (5 Uses, 50 
SV) – Could be used for fire or 
generator fuel.
5
Cryptic Employee Memo (Lore 
Clue) – Notes about a “Manager’s 
Final Order” with symbols that 
match occult writings elsewhere in 
the mall.
6
Old Survivor’s Backpack 
(Randomly rolled survival gear) – 
A forgotten stash with useful 
odds and ends.
Ambiguous Lore (Roll 1d4 
upon investigating notes, 
backroom, or strange 
carvings)
d4 Roll Lore Discovery
1
Torn Employee Note: “Don’t use 
the yeast from shipment #66. I 
swear it moves…”
2
Security Camera Log (Still 
Flickering): Timestamped footage 
shows zombies entering the 
bakery before the outbreak 
happened.
3
Strange Symbols on Freezer 
Door: These marks match those 
found in the occult bookstore, 
hinting at supernatural origins.
4
Survivor’s Scratchings on Wall: 
“The dough still RISES. The flesh 
still FEEDS.”

dressed in aprons, mechanically 
trying to knead rotten dough.
3-4

Hidden in walls, disturbed if 
players fail Stealth.
5
The Dough Thing (Boss) – A 
massive, gelatinous, semi-
conscious mass of infected flesh 
and flour, still growing.
6
Survivor Ghoul (One Prior 
Employee, Semi-Sentient) – 
Mutters about “feeding the 
hunger,” attacks if threatened.
Special Enemy: The Dough 
Thing (Mutant, Large Creature, 
Optional Boss)
A horrifying, rising mass of infected dough, blood, and 
human remains. Its body constantly shifts, spewing out 
acidic yeast and rotten flesh.

AC: 12

HP: 40

Speed: 10 ft (oozing movement)

Attacks:
o
Engulf (Melee, Reach 5 ft) – +5 to hit, 
2d6 bludgeoning + restrained (Escape 
DC 14)
o
Rotten Yeast Spray (Ranged, 10 ft 
Cone) – 3d6 Acid, causes 
Disadvantage on next roll (blinded by 
fumes).

Special Traits:
o
Fermenting Flesh: Each round, The 
Dough Thing grows in size, gaining 
+5 HP.
o
Flammable: Takes double damage 
from fire (gasoline, flamethrower, or 
flour dust explosion).
o
Unnerving Motion: Any survivor who 
watches The Dough Thing move must 
make a Sanity Save (DC 12) or 
become unsettled for 1d4 rounds 
(Disadvantage on Perception checks).
Survival XP Rewards

Defeating Shambler Bakers: 25 XP each

Defeating The Dough Thing: 200 XP

Looting all remaining food: +100 XP bonus

Discovering Occult Clue on Freezer: 50 XP
Final Notes:
Golden Crust Bakery is a high-risk, high-reward 
location filled with valuable food, mysteries, and 
horrific surprises. Whether the players come out with 
full stomachs or screaming nightmares is entirely up 
to their choices.

sites.name: Victory Athletics
sites.bookText:
Victory Athletics (Shop 
#52)
“The glass storefront of Victory Athletics is shattered,  
with bits of safety glass crunching underfoot as you 
step inside. Racks of jerseys and sports gear hang 
askew,  some  stained  with  old  blood.  A  toppled 
display  of  baseball  bats  lies  scattered  across  the 
floor,  some  still  gripped  by  skeletal  hands.  The 
overhead  lights  flicker  intermittently,  casting  eerie 
shadows  over  mannequins  frozen  mid-stride  in 
running  gear.  An  old  security  monitor  behind  the 
counter crackles with static—then, just for a moment, 
a flickering image of movement deeper inside the 
store. Was that a trick of the light… or something 
else?”
General Description
Victory Athletics was once a premium sporting goods 
store, catering to athletes and fitness enthusiasts. Now, 
it is a looter’s jackpot—if they can get past whatever 
lurks inside.

Layout: The store is split into distinct sections: 
an athletic shoe display in the front, a clothing 
area in the middle, and a weapons-relevant 
sporting gear section (bats, hockey sticks, 
bows) toward the back. A fitting room area and 
a manager’s office sit in the rear, with a 
malfunctioning security camera monitor 
blinking weakly behind the counter.

Threats: Something fast has nested in the 
back storeroom. Occasional scratching noises 
suggest something lurking in the ventilation 
ducts above.

Hazards: Broken glass, unstable shelving, and 
motion-sensitive security alarms (if powered) 
that could attract zombies if triggered.
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps (roll 1d4 on entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Shattered Glass Trap: Stepping in 
the wrong spot creates a loud 
crunch, increasing Tension by 1d4 
d4 Roll Hazard
and alerting enemies.
2
Falling Display Rack: An unsteady 
metal rack (Dex DC 14 to avoid) 
collapses, pinning anyone 
underneath (1d6 damage, action 
required to escape).
3
Motion-Sensitive Alarm: A 
forgotten security system still has 
power. Movement in the wrong 
area (Perception DC 15 to notice) 
triggers a loud alarm, adding +2d6 
Tension and summoning 1d6 
zombies within 3 rounds.
4
Duct Crawler Attack: A Stalker 
Zombie drops from a ventilation 
duct onto the first person 
passing beneath it, initiating an 
immediate grapple (Str DC 13 to 
resist).

Ambiguous Lore:
Victory Athletics contains remnants of clues about the 
apocalypse, but none of them provide definitive 
answers. Survivors may uncover:
d4 Roll Ambiguous Clue
1
Security Footage (If Powered): A 
corrupted recording from the day 
the outbreak started, showing 
something inhuman moving at 
impossible speed just before the 
camera feed cuts to static.
2
Bloodied Memo: A note from the 
store manager detailing “corporate 
orders to distribute select 
merchandise to the BioDyne 
research team.” The list of 
requested items includes high-
performance energy drinks and 
experimental muscle 
supplements.
3
Survivor’s Graffiti: Scribbled on a 
dressing room mirror: “Speed kills. I 
saw it. If it looks human, RUN.”
4
BioDyne Packaging: A broken 
crate with labels for prototype 
exo-performance gear, now 
empty—implying that something 
or someone used them.

 437

Speed Demon (Mutant Zombie, 
Unique Encounter)

AC: 14

HP: 35

Attack: Clawed Strike (1d8 slashing) or 
Leaping Pounce (contested Strength check; if 
failed, target is knocked prone and takes 1d6 
damage)

Speed: 50ft (can outrun almost anything)

Special Abilities:
o
Blurred Motion – Disadvantage on 
attacks against it unless the attacker 
has heightened reflexes (Dex 16+).
o
Adrenaline Surge – Once per turn, it 
can take an additional movement 
action.
o
Feeding Frenzy – If it lands a critical 
hit, it restores 5 HP as it consumes 
flesh.

Weakness: Fire-based attacks or well-aimed 
ranged shots (disadvantage on saving throws 
against burning effects).
Survival XP

Securing the store fully: 300 SV

Finding the Security Footage: 100 SV

Defeating the Speed Demon: 150 SV

Discovering BioDyne memo: 50 SV
Victory Athletics is more than just a sporting goods 
store—it hints at BioDyne’s experiments, provides 
useful survival gear, and introduces a new type of 
zombie threat in the form of speed-based infected 
creatures. Survivors who rush in expecting a simple 
looting opportunity may find themselves outmatched 
and outpaced if they’re not careful.

sites.name: Maker’s Market
sites.bookText:
Maker’s Market (Shop #53)
“A soft, flickering glow from dim LED fairy lights still 
clings to the walls of this abandoned artisan shop, 
casting eerie shadows across shelves of handcrafted 
trinkets.  Shelves  are  filled  with  intricately  woven 
scarves,  carved  wooden  figurines,  and  delicate 
blown-glass ornaments—many shattered on the tile 
floor,  crunching  underfoot.  The  scent  of  dried 
lavender  and  beeswax  lingers  in  the  air,  but 
something else is present, too—a faint, acrid burn, as 
if something had been scorched here recently. A lone 
mannequin  stands  behind  the  checkout  counter, 
draped in an unfinished quilt, its missing head giving 
it an unsettling presence. The door leading to the 
back storage room is slightly ajar, and from within, 
something shifts in the darkness…”
General Description
Once a haven for artists and crafters, Maker’s Market 
specialized in unique, handmade goods—woven 
fabrics, wooden carvings, pottery, and metalwork. Now, 
the store is half-looted, its delicate creations left to 
decay amidst shattered glass and broken displays. The 
walls still bear hand-painted murals of pastoral 
landscapes, though claw marks and scorch marks 
suggest something violent happened here.







Final Notes:

Maker’s Market is a psychologically tense 
area—the mannequins, artisan sculptures, and 
scorched remains hint at something deeper.

The “Woven Husk” and “Scorched Horror” 
are optional but terrifying encounters, 
rewarding players who investigate cautiously.

Multiple hidden lore clues deepen the 
apocalyptic mystery, suggesting ties to cult 
activity or BioDyne Corporation.

Loot is valuable, but high risk—firebombs, 
body armor materials, and a reinforced melee 
weapon make this a worthwhile, dangerous 
scavenging point.

sites.name: Modern Living
sites.bookText:
Modern Living (Shop #54)
“The once-pristine showroom of Modern Living now 
lies  in  ruin.  Designer  couches  are  upturned,  their 
sleek  upholstery  slashed  by  desperate  hands.  A 
massive display bed sits in the center, its expensive 
mattress sagging and stained. Shattered glass from 
decorative  mirrors  litters  the  floor,  reflecting  the 
flickering emergency lights above. The faint scent of 
mildew and stale air mingles with something sour—
like  spilled  cleaning  chemicals  mixed  with  decay. 
Somewhere in the distance, a rhythmic thunk-thunk 
echoes, as if something is tapping against a wall… or  
trying to get in.”
General Description
Modern Living was once an upscale home décor store 
known for its minimalist furniture and overpriced 
aesthetic pieces. Now, the showroom is a chaotic 
landscape of wrecked displays and abandoned 
purchases. The showroom floor is divided into model 
rooms—each meant to showcase a different style of 
living: an elegant “City Loft”, a “Modern Farmhouse”, 
a “Cozy Cottage”, and an “Industrial Urban” theme. 
Each section has its own unique hazards and hidden 
loot.

Layout: Multiple mock “rooms,” each with 
different furniture and potential hiding spots.

Threats: A lurking predator (see below) and 
potential environmental dangers.

Hazards: Glass shards, unstable shelving, 
hidden enemies.
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (Roll 1d4 upon entry)

mirrors make perception difficult; 
enemies gain advantage on stealth 
rolls.

A Home AI Hub (Offline)—could 
once control security cameras, 
but its last log entry simply says: 
“They are here. Goodbye.”
Tension Impact
Actions that Increase Tension:
- Moving furniture too loudly (+1d6 Tension).
- Breaking a glass display case (+2d6 Tension).
- Interacting with the Home AI Hub (+1d4 Tension, 
but may provide critical information).
Actions that Reduce Tension:
- Using the barricade materials to reinforce the 
entrance (-1d6 Tension).
- Carefully sneaking through the showroom without 
making noise (-2 Tension per successful Dexterity 
check, DC 14).
Potential Enemies
Showroom Lurker (Special Threat, Hidden Until 
Triggered)
“Something is here with you. It doesn’t moan like the 
others. It doesn’t shuffle. Instead, it watches… waiting. 
You catch a glimpse of something slipping behind a 
wardrobe—too fast to be a normal zombie. And then… 
silence.”

AC: 15

HP: 30

Speed: 40 ft. (can climb furniture effortlessly)

Attacks: Claw (1d8 + Grapple) or Bite (1d6, 
Infection Chance)

Special:
o
Ambush Predator: If unnoticed, it 
deals double damage on its first 
attack.

detected unless players specifically 
search for it (Perception DC 16).
o
Artificial Intelligence? It seems to 
avoid attacking mannequins or 
electronic devices.

- Moving furniture.
- Breaking a mirror.
- Interacting with the AI Hub.

Final Notes:
Modern Living is not just another looting spot—it 
introduces psychological tension, environmental 
puzzles, and an intelligent enemy that requires 
stealth or strategy to survive. The cryptic USB drive 
could be a major campaign clue, while the AI system 
hints at the mall’s deeper secrets.
Would you fight the Lurker or try to evade it? Would 
you dare turn on the AI system, knowing it could alert 
something else?

sites.name: Mall Security Office
sites.bookText:
Mall Security Office
“Dim emergency lighting flickers weakly across rows 
of dead security monitors, their screens reflecting the 
ghostly glow of a static-filled display. The air is thick 
with the scent of mildew, gun oil, and something acrid
—like old sweat and fear. A thick steel door, dented 
and scratched, stands ajar, leading to a reinforced 
weapons locker that has already been looted. An old 
radio crackles faintly with white noise, and a control 
panel  labeled  ‘EMERGENCY  LOCKDOWN’  blinks 
with a faint red warning light. On the desk, a dusty 
coffee mug sits beside a half-written incident report 
detailing something… unexplainable.”
General Description

Layout: A small but heavily reinforced 
room, previously used as a control center for 
mall security. Banks of surveillance monitors 
line the walls, mostly shattered or inactive. A 
security desk is covered in scattered 
paperwork, spent bullet casings, and an old 
cup of moldy coffee. A reinforced gun locker 
is propped open, its contents mostly gone. A 
control panel with emergency lockdown 
options and alarm systems sits partially 
powered, flickering erratically.

Threats:
o
1d4 Crawler Zombies hidden beneath 
desks (remains of security officers who 
tried to make a last stand).
o
If the players activate the 
EMERGENCY LOCKDOWN PANEL, 
a malfunction causes the mall-wide 
alarm system to activate, attracting 
zombies.

Hazards:
o
Unstable Electronics: Random short 
circuits can shock players if 
tampered with improperly (1d4 
electric damage, DC 13 Dexterity 
check to avoid).
o
Decayed Floor Panels: A section of 
the floor near the breaker box has 
rotted through due to water damage
—falling in causes 1d6 damage and 
leaves a player vulnerable to attacks.
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps (Roll 1d4 on Entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Glitched Alarm System: The 
moment the players interact with 
the control panel, an ear-splitting 
siren echoes through the mall. 
(+2d6 Tension immediately; 
attracts zombies from adjacent 
locations in 1d4 rounds.)
2
Crumbling Ceiling: A section of 
the ceiling collapses when 
disturbed, crushing furniture and 
trapping a player (DC 14 Strength 
to escape).
3
Misdirected Sprinkler Activation: 
The old fire suppression system 
activates incorrectly, spraying the 
room in murky, stagnant water. If 
a player is bitten later, they have a 
higher infection risk (+5% 
chance).
4
Security Desk Trap: A dead 
security officer’s body slumps 
forward, pressing a silent panic 
button under the desk. The 
nearby mechanical security gate 
SLAMS shut behind the players, 
trapping them inside unless 
manually disabled. (DC 15 
Mechanics check to bypass.)
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Half-Filled Firearm Permit Form: An 
unfinished form signed by a mall 
executive referencing a missing 
 445 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
cache of guns. (Lore clue.)
2
Partially Functional Surveillance 
System: Restores partial mall 
camera access (players can see 
three random store feeds, 
potentially spotting danger ahead).
3
Security Officer’s Sidearm 
(Empty): A 9mm pistol (25 SV) with 
no ammo—but the officer’s nearby 
desk drawer contains 1d4 bullets.
4
Mall Master Keycard (Partial 
Access): Unlocks most employee-
only doors but doesn’t work on 
secure areas like the Emergency 
Shelter or Armory.
5
Emergency Backup Radio (Still 
Active): Can receive strange 
broadcasts but cannot transmit. Roll 
1d4 for the latest transmission (see 
Ambiguous Lore).
6
Last-Ditch Safe (Locked, DC 15 to 
Open): Contains one remaining 
flashbang grenade (Single-Use, 
Blinds Targets in 15ft, 50 SV).
Ambiguous Lore
Players can discover conflicting clues about the mall’s 
fall, adding layers to the mystery of the apocalypse’s 
cause. If they activate the radio, they hear one of the 
following (roll 1d4):
d4 
Roll
Strange Broadcast
1
A robotic voice repeats: “Zeta 
Protocol compromised. 
Containment breach detected. 
Evacuation terminated.”

sites.name: Manager’s Office & Safe Room
sites.bookText:
Manager’s Office & Safe 
Room
“The polished mahogany desk sits untouched, a relic 
of corporate authority, now coated in a thin layer of 
dust. The leather chair behind it is overturned, one 
armrest torn as if someone was dragged from it in a 
struggle.  Filing  cabinets  lie  rifled  through,  their 
contents scattered in frantic disarray. A digital safe, 
still locked, is embedded in the wall beneath a portrait 
of the mall’s original owner—a man with a too-wide 
smile, his eyes seeming to follow you. A half-written 
resignation letter, stained with something brown and 
flaking, rests on the desk beside a security keycard. 
The air smells of old cologne, ink, and something 
sickly sweet, like meat left out too long.”
General Description

Layout: A large office with a plush carpet, 
expensive but ruined furniture, and floor-to-
ceiling windows overlooking the mall atrium. 
A security terminal, now inactive, sits next to 
the reinforced safe embedded in the wall. The 
back door leads to a small “panic room”, 
still locked from the inside.

Threats: 1 locked door leading to the panic 
room; unknown occupant inside (either alive 
or undead). Scratched bloodstains lead from 
the entrance to the back door, where someone 
desperately tried to enter.

Hazards: Safe requires code entry or brute 
 447

force to open (STR DC 18 or INT DC 15 to 
hack). The security system flickers back to 
life if tampered with, potentially drawing 
unwanted attention (Tension +2d4).

players to kill him before he fully 
loses control.

looks like a dead man in a suit, but 
the “corpse” suddenly gasps, 
lunging at the nearest player. A 
parasitic mass erupts from its 
throat.
6
Something Worse – A humanoid 
figure stands in the dark, facing 
the corner. It doesn’t react to 
light. If approached, it tilts its 
head slowly—but makes no 
sound. If touched, roll 1d20: on a 
10 or lower, it vanishes. On an 
11+, it attacks violently.
 449

Zombie Mall
Special Enemy: “R. Howarth, 
The Last Manager”
(If the infected manager is still alive)

AC: 12

HP: 30

ATK: Unarmed Slam (1d6+1) or “Lurking 
Horror” (1d10 psychic damage, CON save 
DC 14 or Disadvantage on next attack roll).

Special Ability – “Residual Humanity”: If a 
player talks to him instead of attacking, he 
whispers something important (a secret 
about the mall’s disaster).
Final Notes & Usage Ideas

This office is a critical story hub, filled with 
clues, gear, and tension-building choices.

The Safe Room encounter can escalate the 
horror or serve as a major puzzle.

If the players make too much noise, a 
roaming zombie pack might arrive before 
they can escape.

The Mall Blueprints can help navigate the 
rest of the mall, making this a key 
exploration reward.

sites.bookText:
Power Control Room
“The air here is thick with the scent of burning plastic 
and ozone. Rows of towering electrical panels flicker 
dimly, their ancient, dust-choked fans barely spinning. 
A  deep  hum  resonates  from  the  remaining  active 
circuits,  punctuated  by  occasional  sparks  and  the 
ominous clicking of failing relays. Thick power cables 
coil across the floor like dead snakes, some of them 
still live with residual energy. The room should be 
silent…  yet  something  scuttles  within  the  vents 
above,  unseen  but  uncomfortably  close.  Then,  a 
sudden,  high-pitched  whirring  echoes  through  the 
room—the sound of an emergency system struggling 
to reboot on its own…”
General Description
The Power Control Room is the central hub of the 
mall’s electrical grid, located in a secured utility sector 
on the second level near the loading docks. It was 
used by maintenance crews to monitor power 
distribution, reroute circuits, and restore backup 
generators.
Layout:
- Central Control Panel: A wall-sized breaker system 
with flickering indicator lights, manual levers, and a half-
melted main control interface.
- Sub-Panels: Large, locked power relays for specific 
mall sections.
- Circuit Boxes: Some remain active, while others are 
fused or overloaded.
- Overhead Vents: The ducts are disturbingly large, 
and occasional scurrying noises suggest something is 
lurking within.
- Back Room: A tiny technician’s break room filled 
with scattered paperwork, moldy sandwiches, and an 
overturned tool cabinet.

sites.name: Mechanical & HVAC Maintenance Rooms
sites.bookText:
Mechanical & HVAC Maintenance Rooms serve 
as the backbone of the mall’s utilities, a network of 
narrow industrial corridors, boiler rooms, and 
ventilation shafts. The space is filled with heavy 
machinery, metal catwalks, and dangerous 
industrial hazards, making it a perfect hideout—but 
also a potential death trap.

Layout:
o
A boiler room filled with leaking pipes, 
rusted tools, and dangerously 
pressurized steam valves.
o
A ventilation chamber, where 
massive air filters and fan turbines 
still whirr in half-functioning agony.
o
A power relay station, controlling the 
mall’s emergency backup power—if 
anyone dares to fix it.
o
Narrow crawlspaces within the HVAC 
system, perfect for ambushes—or 
escape.
o
Service tunnels leading to deeper, 
uncharted maintenance corridors 
beneath the mall.

Threats:
o
1d6 Crawlers (limbless zombies stuck 
in tight spaces).
o
1d4 Shamblers (slow zombies 
wandering between machinery).
o
1 “Vent Stalker” (a grotesque zombie 
twisted by duct travel, extremely 
mobile).

Hazards:
o
Overheated Steam Pipes (DC 13 
DEX Save or take 2d6 scalding 
damage if burst open).
o
Collapsing Catwalk (DEX DC 14 to 
avoid fall; 2d6 damage, prone for 1 
turn).
o
Electrified Panel (If power is restored 
improperly, DC 15 CON Save or take 
3d6 shock damage).
o
Vent Obstructions (Large creatures 
must crawl through at half-speed; 
sudden drops possible.)
Interactables/Loot

Industrial Tool Kit (15 SV, allows makeshift 
repairs or lockpicking attempts.)

it attacks, it strikes **fast, vanishing into the walls before 
you can react.”*

(1d10 bite, pulls into vents)
Speed: 40 ft (in vents), 20 ft outside
Special:

Ambush Predator: Can attack from 
hidden vent openings with advantage.
o
Shadow Step: After attacking, can 
use Bonus Action to retreat into 
vents (Disengage effect).
o
Hearing-Based Lurker: Loud noises 
(gunfire, shouting) attract it 
immediately.
Special Encounters 
(Optional)
d6 Roll Random Event
1
Steam Pipe Explosion: A failing 
valve bursts open, scalding anyone 
nearby (2d6 damage, loud).
2

has been hiding, but they’re injured 
and paranoid.
3

If players attempt repairs, sparks 
fly—potential fire hazard!
4

is moving… but where?

body inside a locker twitches 
suddenly…
6

echo through the ducts… but 
there’s no one there.

The Mechanical & HVAC Maintenance Rooms offer a 
tense mix of tight-quarters horror, environmental 
hazards, and hidden threats. It’s a key strategic 
location—players must decide whether to:
- Restore power (attracting zombies but unlocking 
mall systems)
- Seal vents (stopping Vent Stalkers but requiring 
resources)
- Scavenge for vital tools at the risk of enemy 
ambushes
5)

sites.name: Emergency Water Tanks & Filtration System
sites.bookText:
Emergency Water Tanks 
& Filtration System
“The rooftop hums with the sound of a distant wind,  
whipping  through  metal  grates  and  rusting  pipes. 
Before you, a series of  massive steel water tanks 
sit elevated on thick iron supports, looming like silent 
sentinels.  Dark  streaks  stain  the  riveted  surfaces 
where  the  rain  has  long  mixed  with  something 
 455 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
unnatural. A series of large, industrial filtration units 
stand between the tanks and the mall’s main water  
lines, their gauges flickering erratically. The air smells 
of mildew, rusted iron, and something foul—a rotten, 
chemical tang that clings to the back of your throat. 
Below  the  tanks,  the  rooftop  is  damp,  slick  with 
black, oily sludge, as if something in the water had 
started to… change.”
Description:

Layout: A network of five industrial-sized 
water tanks, each holding up to thousands of 
gallons of collected rainwater. Connected by a 
series of pipes and catwalks, with a narrow 
maintenance shed nearby filled with tools and 
old inspection reports.

Threats: 1d4 “Drowned” Zombies (see 
below). These creatures, bloated and dripping, 
lurk inside the filtration system, emerging 
when disturbed. A mutated bio-organism may 
also be inside one of the tanks…

Hazards:
o
Slick Rooftop: The sludge-covered 
ground requires a DC 13 Dexterity 
check to avoid slipping (falling prone).
o
Structural Instability: One of the 
tanks has corroded supports—too 
much force could collapse it (potential 
flood hazard).
o
Contaminated Water Supply: If 
connected to the mall’s plumbing 
without purification, anyone drinking 
it must pass a Constitution save 
(DC 14) or suffer infection (1d4 
Constitution damage over 1d6 
days).
Environmental Hazards & 
Random Events (roll 1d4 when 
players enter)
d4 Roll Hazard/Event
1
Water Tank Collapse: The most 
rusted tank partially collapses, 
d4 Roll Hazard/Event
spilling a wave of fetid water and 
1d6 zombies onto the rooftop.
2
Pipe Bursts: A sudden pressure 
change causes a filtration pipe to 
explode, spraying the area with 
black sludge (DC 12 Dex save or 
blinded for 1d6 rounds).
3
Drowned Crawler: A bloated 
zombie, stuck inside a pipe, 
breaks free and grabs the nearest 
character’s leg (DC 14 Strength 
save to resist being pulled down).
4
Eerie Reflection: Looking into 
the dark water, a character sees 
their own reflection speaking to 
them—but the lips don’t match 
their words… (Purely 
atmospheric… or is it?)
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Purification Tablets (5 doses) – 
Can make contaminated water 
safe to drink (10 SV each).
2
Hand Pump Filtration Unit – Can 
be detached and used to purify 
small amounts of water manually 
(25 SV).
3
Engineer’s Logbook – Notes about 
water contamination, mentions 
strange “growths” inside the 
tanks (Ambiguous Lore).
4
Industrial Wrench – Can be used 
as an improvised melee weapon 
(1d6 bludgeoning, +1 
vs. mechanical objects, 10 SV).
5
Generator Fuel Can (Half-Full) – 
Usable for mall power systems or 
 456 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
vehicles (50 SV).
6
Survivor’s Stash – A hidden 
toolbox with lockpicks, flashlight, 
and a revolver with 3 bullets (75 
SV total).
Ambiguous Lore Clues (Roll 
1d4 or scatter throughout the 
area)
d4 Roll Mysterious Clue
1
BioDyne Corp. memo: 
“Unidentified foreign biomaterial 
detected in filtration system. DO 
NOT DRINK.”
2
Faded CDC Warning Sticker: 
Reads: “Do not let them drink the 
water. It spreads.”
3
A Child’s Diary Page, tucked 
inside the maintenance shed: “The 
water made Daddy sick. Then the 
black stuff started crawling…”
4
Graffiti on a rusted tank: “We are 
still in the water.” The words 
shift slightly when looked at from 
different angles.
Tension Impact
Action
Tension Increase
Loud noises (gunfire, 
collapsing tank)
+2d6 Tension
Water contamination 
spreads to mall
+1d6 Tension per 
day
Zombies emerge from 
tanks/pipes
+1d4 Tension
Purifying the water
-1d4 Tension (mall 
becomes safer)
Potential Enemies & 
Encounters
Drowned Zombies (1d4)
(These zombies have absorbed the contaminated water 
and are bloated, half-dissolved, and drippy.)

AC: 11

HP: 18

Attack: Claw Swipe (1d6 slashing) or 
Drowning Grapple (DC 14 STR to escape, 1d4 
damage per round)

Special: If killed with slashing/piercing 
damage, they burst, covering attackers in 
toxic sludge (DC 13 Constitution save or 
suffer nausea, -2 to rolls for 1 hour).
The Thing in the Water (Optional Mini-Boss)
(A pulsating, shifting mass inside the last intact tank. It 
hasn’t been fully born… yet.)

AC: 14

HP: 45

Attacks:
1.
Tentacle Lash (10-ft reach, 1d8 
bludgeoning, DC 13 Strength save 
or restrained)
2.
Acidic Vomit (10-ft cone, 2d6 acid 
damage, DC 14 Dex save for half)

Weakness: Fire and electricity deal double 
damage.
XP & Survival Value (SV) 
Rewards
Action
SV Reward
Securing the entire 
rooftop area
300 SV
Clearing all threats 
(Drowned Zombies & 
Mutant Entity)
+200 SV
 457 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
Action
SV Reward
Repairing filtration 
system (requires 
proper tools)
+150 SV
Recovering loot
Varies (50-100 SV 
per useful item)
Survival Strategy Hooks

Base Potential? – If purified, the tanks could 
supply water indefinitely, making the mall a 
viable long-term shelter.

Poison or Cure? – The contaminated water 
could be used against enemies if bottled as 
biological weapons.

Mystery Hooks – What really caused the 
contamination? The players might need to go 
deeper into the mall’s dark past to find out.
Final Notes:
This area can serve as:
- A high-risk but high-reward location (clean water is 
crucial for survival).
- An environmental hazard & puzzle (do they repair 
the system or avoid it?).
- A boss fight encounter (if the mutant entity is 
included).
- A key piece of the apocalypse mystery (was this 
contamination part of the zombie outbreak, or 
something worse?).
6)

sites.name: Generator & Fuel Storage
sites.bookText:
Generator & Fuel 
Storage
“The rooftop air hums with a low, electrical thrum as 
you  approach  the  generator  enclosure.  The  metal 
structure is surrounded by chain-link fencing topped 
with rusted barbed wire, its gate left hanging open. 
Inside,  massive  industrial  generators  sit  dormant, 
their fuel lines chewed through and leaking the sharp 
scent  of  gasoline  into  the  night  air.  Dozens  of 
jerrycans lie scattered across the concrete, some still 
full, others punctured and seeping dark stains onto 
the ground. Amidst the tangle of electrical cables and 
steel  casings,  the  sound  of  skittering  movement 
echoes through the vents. The rats should have been 
a  minor  nuisance—until  you  notice  the  gnawed 
human bones piled behind one of the machines…”
Description

Layout: A fenced-off rooftop structure 
housing several large industrial generators, 
a small fuel storage shed, and maintenance 
lockers with tools and spare parts. The area 
smells strongly of gasoline and ozone, and 
many fuel drums appear rummaged through 
or tipped over.

Threats: A pack of oversized rats—bloated, 
twitching, their flesh splitting in unnatural ways. 
Something worse lurks in the fuel shed, where 
a pile of half-eaten bodies suggests these 
rodents aren’t the biggest danger here.

Hazards:
1.
Flammable Environment: Any 
firearms or explosives used in 
combat risk igniting the fuel (roll 1d20; 
on 1-5, a massive fireball engulfs the 
area for 4d6 damage to everyone 
inside).
2.
Leaking Gasoline: Dexterity DC 13 
or risk slipping on the oil-slick ground 
during movement.
3.
Exposed Electrical Wiring: Damaged 
generator cables spark wildly—
anyone stepping on them must 
make a DC 12 Constitution save or 
take 1d6 electrical damage and be 
stunned for 1 round.
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Full Jerrycan (Gasoline, 10 SV 
each) – Three intact cans remain 
among the wreckage.
2

Heavy but operational. Can be used 
to power one section of the mall.
3
Mechanic’s Toolbox (25 SV) – 
Contains wrenches, screwdrivers, 
wire cutters, useful for repair tasks.
4

6

survivor’s last entry, describing a 
lurking “shadow thing” that 
emerged from the vents before 
they died.
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered throughout the area, players can find 
contradictory clues about the outbreak’s origins:
d4 Roll Lore Clue
1
Military Labeling: The fuel cans 
are stamped with “PROPERTY OF 
FORT REDACTED - OPERATION 
BLACKOUT.”
2

the generator panels, sigils 
resembling ritualistic markings 
pulse faintly under blacklight.
3
BioDyne Experiment Logs: A 
clipboard from a “Project Rebirth” 
field study, referencing energy 
anomalies during zombie 
encounters.
4
Doomsday Prepper Notes: An 
old ham radio transmission 
printout, warning that the “power 
grid failure” was a deliberate 
test.

Survival Strategy & Player 
Decisions

Fix the Generator? Requires proper tools 
(from Maintenance Room) and 1 hour of 
work.

Loot Fuel or Hold Back? Risk exposing more 
zombies by moving large supplies.

Avoid Combat or Engage? Firearms & 
explosions are risky here. Melee preferred.

Investigate the Shed? Risk disturbing 
whatever killed the security team.
Final Notes
The Generator & Fuel Storage area is a high-value 
but high-risk location. If secured, it provides power to 
the mall—but players must balance stealth, combat, 
and resource management. This encounter tests 
player decision-making, forcing them to prioritize 
repairs, supplies, or survival.

sites.name: Emergency Disaster Shelter
sites.bookText:
Emergency Disaster 
Shelter
“The steel-reinforced blast doors are dented but still 
intact,  their  surface  scarred  by  failed  attempts  to 
break in. A faded Civil Defense emblem is stenciled 
near the entry, its edges peeling like old skin. Beyond 
the threshold, the air is thick with a musty, metallic 
 460 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
scent—long-sealed and untouched for years. Rows of 
metal shelves line the walls, stocked with cans of 
government-issued rations, first aid kits, and sealed 
water barrels. Cots, still made with scratchy military 
blankets, sit in eerie order, as if waiting for occupants 
who never arrived. A small emergency radio crackles 
softly, stuck between stations. But something feels 
off. The space isn’t entirely abandoned…”
General Description
Layout: Hidden beneath the mall’s roof level, this 
fallout shelter was built as an emergency survival 
bunker during the Cold War. The shelter is reinforced 
with steel walls, ventilation systems, and self-
contained water & power sources, though many are 
failing or damaged. It contains sleeping quarters, a 
supply depot, a communications terminal, and a 
locked storage vault.
Threats: Something got inside before it was fully 
sealed. The previous survivors who took refuge 
here are no longer human.
Hazards: Limited oxygen, unstable power, hidden traps 
from previous occupants.
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & 
Puzzles (Roll 1d4 upon entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Failing Air Filtration System – 
Players have 20 minutes before 
oxygen depletes unless repaired 
(Intelligence DC 14). Failure results 
in exhaustion for everyone inside.
2
Malfunctioning Blast Doors – 
They slam shut after 1 minute. If 
not disabled (Intelligence DC 15), 
they will lock permanently until 
power is restored elsewhere.
3
Hidden Tripwire – Survivors who 
occupied this place booby-trapped 
the shelves before dying. 
d4 Roll Hazard
Perception DC 16 to notice, 
otherwise, triggers tear gas 
grenade (CON DC 13 or blinded 
for 1d6 rounds).
4
Rats in the Walls – Mutant rats 
have burrowed into the structure. 
Players hear scratching from 
behind metal panels. In 2d6 
minutes, they will break through 
in a swarm.
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
MRE Crates (6 total) – Military 
rations (3 days of food per crate, 18 
SV each).
2
Emergency Medkits (3 total) – First 
aid kits with antibiotics (10 SV each).
3
Old Service Rifle (Locked in Gun 
Cabinet) – A semi-auto rifle (2d6 
damage, 40 SV). Cabinet is locked 
(Dexterity DC 15 to pick or 
Strength DC 18 to break).
4
Government-Issue Survival 
Manual – Contains fortification tips 
and defense plans. If studied, 
grants +1 to Base Defense rolls for 
the mall.
5
Shortwave Radio (Partially 
Functional) – Can receive signals, 
possibly from another survivor 
faction.
6
Vault Door (Locked, Requires 
Special Key) – Stamped “For 
Military Personnel Only.” What’s 
inside? (GM’s choice: Advanced 
weapons, classified documents, or 
something worse.)
 461 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
Ambiguous Lore: How Did This 
Shelter Fail? (Roll 1d4 when 
searching logs or 
investigating remains.)
d4 Roll Cryptic Clue
1
Survivor Log Entry – “We thought 
we’d be safe here. It was already 
inside. We heard it whispering 
through the vents. It said it wasn’t 
alone.”
2
Blood-Stained Clipboard – 
Military documents reference 
‘Containment Protocol Theta’—
no further explanation.
3
Strange Symbols Scratched into 
the Walls – Unrecognizable script, 
but it matches the markings 
found elsewhere in the mall.
4
Newsprint from the Day of the 
Outbreak – Front-page headline: 
“Biodyne Corporation Denies 
Allegations of Bio-Weapons 
Testing.”
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action/Loot
SV Reward
Securing the Shelter
500 SV
Recovering all food 
rations
108 SV (18 per crate)
Unlocking the 
Military Vault
150 SV (or more, 
depending on 
contents)
Repairing the 
Shortwave Radio
75 SV
Discovering a major 
lore clue
100 SV bonus
Tension Impact

Low Noise Actions (Searching, Reading 
Logs): +0 Tension

Triggering Traps or Breaking Down Doors: 
+2d6 Tension

Firing Guns Inside Shelter: Instantly attracts 
nearby zombies (+3d6 Tension)

Activating the Radio on Speaker: +1d6 
Tension per broadcast attempt
Potential Enemies (Roll 
1d6 upon entry or after 10 
minutes inside)
d6 Roll Enemy Encounter
1-2
Shambler Pack (1d4+2) – The 
previous occupants turned into 
slow, relentless undead.
3
Mutant Rat Swarm – Gnaws 
through the air ducts, attacking in 
waves (DEX Save DC 13 or 
swarmed, 1d4 damage per round).
4
Something in the Vault – If 
opened, releases an “Elder Thing 
Spawn” (AC 15, HP 30, Psychic 
Scream attack).
5
Echoing Whispers – Players start 
hearing a voice in their heads. It 
tells them they are not alone. 
(SANITY CHECK DC 12: Failure = 
mild paranoia, Success = ignore.)
6
The Last Survivor (Madman with 
a Shotgun) – “No one gets in. No 
one gets out.” (Negotiation DC 16 
or combat.)
 462 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
Stat Blocks
Shamblers (1d4+2)

HP: 12

AC: 10

Attack: Claw (1d6), Bite (1d8, infection 
chance)

Slow-moving but relentless
Mutant Rat Swarm

HP: 15

AC: 12

Attack: Swarm (1d4 damage per round, 
cumulative effect)

Special: Attacks as a single entity; if reduced 
to half HP, it scatters.
The Last Survivor

HP: 25

AC: 14

Weapon: Shotgun (2d8, reload every 2 shots)

Special: Will barricade doors and use the 
shelter defensively. If persuaded (DC 16), he 
may join the party—or turn on them later.
Final Notes
The Emergency Disaster Shelter is one of the best 
possible safehouses, but comes with serious risks. 
Whether due to traps, hostile survivors, or 
something worse lurking inside, the players must 
earn the safety of this place. If they fully secure it, it 
offers a major advantage in long-term survival.
But… was it ever truly abandoned?
8)

sites.name: Security Armory
sites.bookText:
Security Armory 
(Locked & Abandoned)
“A thick steel door, reinforced with heavy-duty locks 
and long-dried bloodstains, stands at the end of the 
dimly lit hallway. A flickering emergency light buzzes 
weakly  above,  casting  long,  erratic  shadows.  The 
faint scent of gun oil, sweat, and something rotten 
seeps  through  the  seams.  A  hastily  spray-painted 
message in black across the door reads: ‘STAY OUT. 
WE TRIED.’ The door is still locked, but from the 
scratching  and  low  groans  inside,  you  can  tell… 
something is still in there.”
General Description
The Security Armory was once the last stronghold of 
the mall’s security team. As the outbreak spiraled out of 
control, the guards retreated here, locking themselves 
in with their weapons, ammunition, and riot gear. The 
room was meant to be a stronghold—but something 
went wrong.
Now, the door is locked from the inside. The security 
staff is still here… but they aren’t alive anymore.
Layout:

The Exterior: The armory door is thick steel 
with a digital keypad (which is broken). A 
ventilation shaft above leads inside, though 
only a small or nimble character (DEX DC 
16) can squeeze through.

The Interior: Racks of riot gear, shotguns, 
ammunition, and tactical vests line the walls. 
The security logs are still in their terminals, 
but power is unstable.

The Final Stand: Desperate barricades of 
desks, lockers, and metal shelving failed to 
keep the infected at bay. The guards turned 
inside the room, leaving a small, confined kill 
zone filled with undead.

An Active Threat: The locked-in zombies are 
docile until disturbed. Breaking in releases 
the undead and escalates the Tension 
meter dramatically.

Zombie Mall

(The confined space amplifies the sound.)

 465

o
Fearful & Armed: If startled, he fires 
first unless a CHA (Persuasion) DC 
15 check calms him down.
Conclusion
The Security Armory is a high-risk, high-reward 
encounter that can play out in multiple ways:
- Stealth Infiltration (through vents, careful unlocking)
- Loud Assault (break down the door, causing a 
Tension spike)
- Diplomacy & Mystery (dealing with the trapped 
guard, gathering lost intel)
The gear inside makes it worth the risk, but reckless 
players could easily turn this into a full mall-wide 
panic. The lore hints further deepen the mystery of 
what actually happened in Zombie Mall.
9)

sites.name: Rooftop Greenhouse & Hydroponics Garden
sites.bookText:
Rooftop Greenhouse & 
Hydroponics Garden
“A humid wave of overgrowth and decay greets you 
as  you  step  onto  the  rooftop  garden.  Thick  vines 
creep across shattered glass panes, filtering dim light 
through a canopy of tangled leaves and broken steel 
framework. Rusted irrigation pipes drip stale water 
into algae-covered troughs, their pumps sputtering 
with the last dregs of power. Rows of once-cultivated  
crops have grown wild, stretching toward the sky in 
defiance  of  their  long-dead  caretakers.  And  yet, 
something has disturbed the tangled foliage—great 
clawed furrows rip through the dirt, as if something* 
massive has made this place its home. The air is 
thick with the scent of damp earth and something 
rotten, something hungry.*”
General Description

Layout: The greenhouse structure is 
partially collapsed, leaving half the area 
exposed to the elements.

A central irrigation system runs along the 
floor, pools of murky water forming between 
cracked tiles.

Rows of hydroponic growing trays contain 
rotting or overgrown plants, though some 
food is salvageable.

The glass ceiling is broken in many places, 
making it dangerous to climb and allowing 
birds, wind, and the occasional infected 
creature to get inside.

A shadowy nest of tangled vines and 
disturbed soil sits in the farthest corner, 
hidden among the overgrowth…

sites.name: Secret Panic Room
sites.bookText:
Secret Panic Room 
(Hidden in a Store Office)
“A nondescript office door sits ajar at the back of the 
jewelry store, its keypad lock flickering weakly with 
half-dead power. Inside, the air is stale but not rank—
this place was sealed, but not abandoned. A steel-
reinforced safe room, lined with faux-wood paneling 
and faded luxury furniture, feels more like an upscale 
bunker than an office. A dusty cot rests in one corner, 
next  to  a  long-dead  laptop  and  an  open  can  of 
preserved meat. The emergency radio hums faintly, 
its red light blinking intermittently. A half-eaten protein 
bar and a bottle of water sit on the desk, still fresh. 
Someone was here. Maybe they still are…”
Description:
2196.
Layout:
o
Hidden in the back office of Sterling 
Lux Jewelers, disguised as a 
standard storage room.
o
Steel-reinforced walls and an 
electronically locked door (can be 
hacked or forced open).
o
Small cot, stocked shelves, 
emergency radio, dead laptop, 
bloodstained notes.
o
A small air filtration unit still hums 
weakly, powered by a backup 
battery.
o
A bullet-riddled body slumped in a 
chair—one gunshot to the head, 
pistol still in hand.
Threats:
o
Uncertain—who locked the door 
from the inside?
o
The emergency radio still flickers on 
and off, broadcasting… something.
o
If the players linger, there’s a 30% 
 468 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
chance that something outside 
heard them enter.
Hazards:
o
Door Lock System (Electronic, 
Malfunctioning) – Hacking or picking 
(DC 16) required to enter.
o
Hidden Panic Button – Can be 
pressed, but does it send for help or 
summon more danger?
o
Radiation-Laced Food Cans – 1d4 
random canned goods are spoiled 
and mildly irradiated.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Emergency Ration Packs (4 Days 
of Food, 20 SV) – Some are still 
good.
2
9mm Pistol (30 SV) with 10 
Rounds (10 SV each) – Gun held 
by the dead man.
3
Mysterious Laptop (Locked, 
Battery Dead) – Requires power 
source to access potential 
encrypted files.
4
Handwritten Notes – Rambling 
thoughts of a corporate employee 
trapped inside. Mentions “The 
Protocol” and someone named K. 
(Lore)
5
Emergency Radio (Functional but 
Unstable, 50 SV) – Occasionally 
picks up military broadcasts… or 
something else.
6
Air Filtration Unit (Can Be 
Salvaged, 75 SV) – If relocated, 
can provide contaminant-free air 
for the base.
Ambiguous Lore:

The laptop (if powered) contains encrypted 
files marked BIO-RESEARCH 
CONTINGENCY. It references “Project 
Lazarus” and classified emergency 
lockdown protocols.

The dead man’s ID badge reveals his name: 
Derek Holloway, Security Consultant, 
BioDyne Corporation.

The radio picks up distorted transmissions 
at odd intervals. Sometimes military code, 
other times… something whispering.
Random Events (Roll 1d4 
When Exploring)
d4 Roll Event
1
The Radio Signal Clears – The 
emergency radio suddenly picks up 
a military broadcast. It’s dated 
three weeks ago, warning about 
“failed containment in Zone B-6.”
2
The Lock Fails – After 10 minutes, 
the door locks again 
automatically. If inside, players 
need to force it open (Strength DC 
14) or bypass it (Tech DC 16).
3
The Laptop Powers On – If 
powered, the laptop briefly works 
before blue-screening. The last 
visible file is labeled “Subject 32 
Awakening.”
4
Footsteps on the Roof – A soft 
thudding above. Could be wind… 
or something walking overhead.

100 SV

(Reclaimed)
75 SV
Tension Impact:

If the players use the emergency radio, roll 
1d6:
o
1-3: Nothing but static.
o
4: Picks up a garbled military 
transmission (+1d4 Tension).
o
5: A voice whispers something 
unintelligible (+1d6 Tension).
o
6: The signal attracts something 
outside the room (+2d6 Tension).

Forcing the Door Open: Increases Tension 
by +1d6 (loud noise).
Possible Enemies (Roll 1d6 if 
the Players Linger Too Long)
d6 Roll Enemy Encounter
1-2
No immediate danger… yet.
3
Crawlers (1d4) – Zombies that 
squeeze under the reinforced door 
when it’s pried open.
4
Panic Room Survivor (Hostile) – 
A malnourished, paranoid survivor 
returns and mistakes the players 
for thieves. He’s armed with a 
rusty revolver (1d6+2 damage).
5
BioDyne Experiment (Feral 
Human, 1) – Something that used 
to be human finds its way inside. It 
has glowing eyes, elongated 
fingers, and speaks in echoes of 
past conversations.
6
The Door Slams Shut – A 
system lockdown triggers, 
sealing the players inside. They 
now need to find another way 
out…
Enemy Stat Blocks (For 
Common Threats in the Room)
Crawlers (1d4)
- HP: 8
- AC: 12
- Attack: Bite (1d6, Grapple DC 13)
- Special: Hidden in shadows, ambushes first player 
through the door.
Panic Room Survivor (Paranoid Armed NPC)
- HP: 15
- AC: 11 (Improvised Kevlar)
- Attack: Revolver (1d6+2 damage, 6 shots)
- Special: “Desperate Shot” – If reduced below 5 HP, 
takes one last reckless shot (automatic hit, max 
damage).
BioDyne Experiment (“Failed Subject”)
- HP: 30
- AC: 14
- Attack: Clawed Swipe (2d6), Mutated Bite (1d8 
Infection Chance)
- Special:
- “Psychic Echo” – Randomly repeats something the 
players have said in the last minute.
- “Phase Instability” – At 10 HP or less, flickers in 
and out of existence. Harder to hit (AC +2).
Survival Summary
The Secret Panic Room is an excellent short-term 
safe zone, but the mystery, resources, and danger 
escalate quickly. Players might secure valuable 
supplies, lore, or an escape plan, but lingering too 
long could lead to something discovering them… or 
locking them inside.
11)

sites.name: Helicopter Pad
sites.bookText:
Helicopter Pad 
(Abandoned News 
Chopper)
“A cold wind whips across the open rooftop, rattling 
 470 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
the skeletal remains of metal scaffolding and half-
finished billboard repairs. At the center of the landing 
pad, an old news helicopter sits motionless, its faded 
blue and yellow paint peeling under years of neglect. 
The  windshield  is  shattered,  glass  fragments 
crunching underfoot as you approach. Dried blood 
splatters  across  the  cockpit,  and  an  old  radio 
transmitter  inside  crackles  weakly  with  static.  The 
helicopter’s  rotors  creak  in  the  wind,  almost  as  if 
they’re  whispering  some  long-forgotten  warning. 
Something doesn’t feel right… and you’re not alone 
up here.”
General Description

Layout:
o
The helicopter pad is located on the 
highest point of the mall rooftop, 
surrounded by chain-link fencing 
(some sections broken) and 
maintenance walkways leading back 
inside.
o
A news station chopper (call sign 
“SkyEye 7”) sits rusting in the middle, 
cockpit doors ajar, its tail slightly 
bent from a rough landing.
o
A small metal storage locker nearby 
contains spare aviation tools and 
supplies, but the lock is broken.
o
Several abandoned fuel drums lay 
nearby, some empty, some leaking.

Threats:
o
1d4 “Rooftop Stalkers” (Stealthy 
Zombies) hide near ventilation ducts, 
waiting for prey.
o
If noise is made (e.g., checking the 
helicopter, firing a gun), roll 1d6:
1-3: Distant moans echo from below. No immediate 
response.
4-5: A zombie climber is attracted to the noise, scaling 
up the side of the mall.
6: A screamer zombie on the opposite rooftop spots 
the players and lets out a horrifying shriek (+2d6 
Tension instantly).

Hazards:
o
Unstable Walkways: Some metal 
panels near the pad are loose or 
rusted through (DEX DC 13 to avoid 
falling 10 feet).
o
Fuel Leak: A slow diesel leak from 
the helicopter’s broken engine casing 
could ignite if exposed to fire or 
gunfire.
o
High Winds: Any ranged attack 
beyond 30 feet suffers disadvantage 
due to rooftop gusts.
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Emergency Parachute – One-time 
use for a desperate rooftop escape. 
(30 SV)
2
First Aid Kit (High-Grade) – 
Contains antibiotics, painkillers, 
bandages. (50 SV)
3

weathered SD card in the cockpit. 
Contains a news anchor’s final 
moments before the outbreak. (Lore 
Clue)
4
Aviation Tools – Includes a wrench 
set and fuel siphon, needed for 
helicopter repair. (75 SV if intact)
5
Partially Full Fuel Drum – 1d4 
gallons of usable aviation fuel, but 
leaks if moved carelessly. (50 SV 
per gallon)
6
Emergency Flare Gun – Usable as 
a weapon (1d8 fire, sets targets 
ablaze) or distress signal. (40 SV)

files labeled “Project Lazarus”,



Dragging Grab: Instead of biting, it can grapple a 
target (DC 13 STR to escape). If successful, it 
attempts to pull victims off the rooftop.


as normal terrain.



within 60 feet must make a DC 15 
CON save or be stunned for 1

+2d6 instantly.

Special Encounter: The 
Pilot (Optional)

The pilot’s body is slumped in the cockpit, 
seatbelt still latched.

If the players disturb him (move body, loot, 
or try to start the chopper)…
The pilot is still alive.
He has been bitten and is in the final stages of turning.
If revived, he can share critical lore information, but 
within 1d6 minutes, he turns into a runner zombie 
and attacks.
Final Thoughts
The Helicopter Pad is a major endgame location, 
offering a possible escape route, high-value loot, 
and deep lore clues. However, players must manage 
noise and tension carefully, as the open-air nature 
of the rooftop makes them highly vulnerable to zombie 
swarms.

sites.name: Skylight Catwalks & Glass Domes
sites.bookText:
Skylight Catwalks & 
Glass Domes
“High  above  the  shattered  remains  of  the  mall’s 
central concourse, a network of rusting maintenance 
catwalks  stretches  between  massive,  grime-coated 
skylights. Dim sunlight filters through the fractured 
glass, casting eerie beams across the ruined stores 
below. Patches of old blood stain the walkways, and 
long-dried  handprints  smear  the  support  railings—
evidence  of  a  final,  desperate  struggle.  The  faint 
creak of shifting metal echoes through the silence, 
hinting  that  not  all  of  these  catwalks  are  entirely 
stable.  Below,  half  a  dozen  zombies  shamble 
aimlessly,  their  milky  eyes  occasionally  flicking 
upward, as if drawn to movement they can no longer 
reach… or understand.”
General Description
The Skylight Catwalks were once used by 
maintenance crews to access the massive glass-
domed skylights overhead. Some walkways still hold, 
while others have collapsed entirely, leaving only 
twisted metal beams and shattered glass below. 
Suspended over the mall’s largest atrium, these 
catwalks offer a stealthy way to traverse the 
concourse, but the risk of falling, breaking through a 
weakened platform, or drawing unwanted attention 
is high.
 473 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (Roll 1d6 on 
entry)
d6 Roll Hazard
1
Loose Panel: A rusted section 
gives way beneath a survivor’s 
weight (Dex DC 14 to grab the 
railing or fall 30 ft).
2
Shattered Skylight: A broken 
glass section threatens collapse. 
Moving across requires a Dexterity 
check (DC 13) or the glass gives 
way (fall + glass shards = 2d6 
damage).
3
Hanging Corpse: A dead security 
guard dangles from a cable, 
swaying gently. His radio crackles 
on randomly, drawing 1d4 
zombies below.
4
Nest of Crows: Startled birds burst 
into the air when disturbed, 
causing a loud noise that 
increases Tension by +2d6.
5
Collapsed Walkway Section: A 
gap in the catwalk requires a jump 
(DC 12 Strength or Dex) or players 
must find another way across.
6
Shambler on the Railing: One 
zombie impaled on a metal bar 
suddenly comes to life, grabbing 
at the nearest player (Grapple DC 
14 to avoid being pulled down).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Maintenance Locker – Contains 
rope (50 ft), wrench (melee 
weapon, 1d6), duct tape, and 
flashlight (Tool Kit, 15 SV).

Could be used as a ranged weapon

(Worth 10 SV.)

stash in a store below. (Lore 
Clue.)

handgun with 4 bullets (25 SV). 
The gun is jammed (requires a 
Smart Survivor to repair).
6
Zipped-up Toolbag – Contains 
wire cutters, screwdriver, pliers, 
and a pack of old cigarettes 
(Trade Value: 20 SV).
Ambiguous Lore
Players may discover clues suggesting different 
causes for the apocalypse. These are scattered 
among maintenance logs, bloodied notes, and 
strange graffiti.

1

access should remain restricted 
during testing. We don’t want

(Testing? What kind?)
2

Revelation 6:12 into the skylight:

sackcloth, and the moon like blood.”
3
Old Security Logs – Mentions a 
team sent to “clean up the VIP 
lounge” before “The Surge.”
4
Distorted Radio Signal – If the

sites.name: Mall Billboards & Rooftop Signage
sites.bookText:
Mall Billboards & 
Rooftop Signage
“Towering over the mall’s rooftop, enormous neon 
billboards flicker with dying electricity, their cracked 
and weather-worn surfaces advertising long-forgotten 
brands. Some panels are missing, revealing rusted 
steel  frames  and  frayed  wiring  that  sparks 
intermittently.  The  hum  of  faulty  transformers 
competes with the eerie silence of the ruined world 
beyond. From here, the entire city stretches out—a 
skyline of broken windows, distant fires, and the slow 
movement of shambling figures in the streets below. 
But most unsettling is the fresh graffiti scrawled on 
one billboard in thick red paint: ‘WE SEE YOU.’”
Description

Layout:
The billboards are arranged along the 
eastern side of the rooftop, supported by 
massive steel scaffolding and 
maintenance walkways. Some are tilted 
dangerously, their bolts loosened by years of 
exposure. A small control station sits at the 
base of the largest sign, its old panel still 
powered, though flickering erratically. A 
broken ladder leads up to the tallest sign, 
its rungs rusted through.

Threats:
o
1d4+1 Crawler Zombies are tangled 
in the scaffolding, their legs crushed 
but their torsos still very much alive.
o
1d3 Stalkers (Stealth Zombies) lurk 
in the shadowed maintenance 
walkways, waiting for movement.
o
The graffiti is fresh—someone (or 
something) was recently here.

Hazards:
o
Loose Signage – A powerful wind 
could cause one of the billboards to 
collapse (Dexterity Save DC 14 or 
take 2d6 bludgeoning).
o
Electrified Wires – Several cables still 
have active current. Contact deals 
1d8 lightning damage and sparks 
loudly.
o
Compromised Walkways – Stepping 
on the wrong section (Dexterity 
Check DC 12) could cause rusted 
grating to give way, resulting in a 20 ft. 
drop onto solid concrete.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items

Flare Gun (3 shots) – Can be used 
for signaling, combat, or distracting 
zombies. (+10 Tension if fired.) (25 
SV)
2

locked doors or breaking chains. 
Heavy but valuable. (20 SV)
3
Makeshift Rooftop Camp – 
Remains of a survivor’s hideout, 
complete with a backpack 
containing canned food (5 meals, 
10 SV) and an old handwritten 
note.
4
Handheld Radio – Tuned to a

emits faint whispering voices that 
aren’t quite human. (Ambiguous

used to repair a generator or jerry-
rig electronics. (Tool Kit, 20 SV)
6
Sniper’s Nest – Someone left an 
old bolt-action hunting rifle (1d8 
damage, 30 SV) and 6 bullets (10 
SV each) hidden under a tarp. 
Blood stains the ground nearby.

We shouldn’t have answered

do not trust the light… repeat, do

grinning face that was never 
part of the original design. The 
moment players look away and 
back, it’s gone.

Special Encounter: “The Ad 
Man” (Optional)
A biomutant zombie somehow fused into one of the 
giant billboards. It speaks in distorted radio ads, 
repeating corporate slogans in an unnerving, garbled 
voice.

HP: 30

AC: 13

Attacks:
o
“Buy More!” Sonic Scream – 15 ft. 
cone (1d8 psychic damage, CON 
Save DC 13 to resist)
o
Tangled Wires (Whip Attack) – 1d6 
electrical damage, restrains on hit 
(Strength DC 14 to escape)
o
Neon Burst (Recharge 5-6) – Sparks 
fly, temporarily blinding players in a 
10 ft. radius

Special:
o
If killed, its final words will be a 
distorted radio broadcast: “Thank you 
for shopping with us. Your transaction 
is… incomplete.”
o
Loot: The “Ad Man’s” remains include 
a cracked USB drive containing 
garbled but decipherable audio files 
from before the outbreak.

Summary

Mall Billboards & Rooftop Signage provide 
both opportunity and danger—a potential 
escape signal, but also a zombie magnet.

Survivors’ remnants suggest that someone 
else was here recently, but whether they’re 
friend or foe remains unknown.

The flickering lights, radio interference, and 
cryptic graffiti add psychological horror 
elements.

A powerful mutant “Billboard Zombie” 
introduces a unique boss fight with an eerie 
corporate horror twist.

Multiple interactables and hazards allow 
players to engage creatively, whether it’s 
using flare guns, scavenging hidden 
stashes, or repairing power lines.

14) Drainage Gutters & 
Water Collection System
“The  rooftop  stretches  out  before  you,  a  maze  of 
rusting  gutters,  cracked  water  tanks,  and  sloshing 
pools of stagnant rainwater. The air smells of mildew 
and decay. Some of the gutters are clogged with 
rotting  leaves,  others  with  decomposed  corpses 
bloated  from  endless  downpours.  Here  and  there, 
makeshift rain barrels stand overflowing, catching the 
last clean water in the city—if you dare to drink it. A 
steady drip… drip… drip echoes from the drainage 
pipes, a rhythm broken only by the distant moans of 
something shifting in the shadows.”

Zombie Horde (1d6+2 
Shamblers) – Slowly climbing 
the mall exterior, drawn to 
activity.
Special Encounter: “The Ad 
Man” (Optional)
A biomutant zombie somehow fused into one of the 
giant billboards. It speaks in distorted radio ads, 
repeating corporate slogans in an unnerving, garbled 
voice.

HP: 30

AC: 13

Attacks:
o
“Buy More!” Sonic Scream – 15 ft. 
cone (1d8 psychic damage, CON 
Save DC 13 to resist)
o
Tangled Wires (Whip Attack) – 1d6 
electrical damage, restrains on hit 
(Strength DC 14 to escape)
o
Neon Burst (Recharge 5-6) – Sparks 
fly, temporarily blinding players in a 
10 ft. radius

Special:
o
If killed, its final words will be a 
distorted radio broadcast: “Thank you 
for shopping with us. Your transaction 
is… incomplete.”
o
Loot: The “Ad Man’s” remains include 
a cracked USB drive containing 
garbled but decipherable audio files 
from before the outbreak.

Summary

Mall Billboards & Rooftop Signage provide 
both opportunity and danger—a potential 
escape signal, but also a zombie magnet.

Survivors’ remnants suggest that someone 
else was here recently, but whether they’re 
friend or foe remains unknown.

The flickering lights, radio interference, and 
cryptic graffiti add psychological horror 
elements.

A powerful mutant “Billboard Zombie” 
introduces a unique boss fight with an eerie 
corporate horror twist.

Multiple interactables and hazards allow 
players to engage creatively, whether it’s 
using flare guns, scavenging hidden 
stashes, or repairing power lines.

14) Drainage Gutters & 
Water Collection System
“The  rooftop  stretches  out  before  you,  a  maze  of 
rusting  gutters,  cracked  water  tanks,  and  sloshing 
pools of stagnant rainwater. The air smells of mildew 
and decay. Some of the gutters are clogged with 
rotting  leaves,  others  with  decomposed  corpses 
bloated  from  endless  downpours.  Here  and  there, 
makeshift rain barrels stand overflowing, catching the 
last clean water in the city—if you dare to drink it. A 
steady drip… drip… drip echoes from the drainage 
pipes, a rhythm broken only by the distant moans of 
something shifting in the shadows.”

sites.name: Drainage Gutters & Water Collection System
sites.bookText:
Drainage Gutters & Water Collection System 
was designed to recycle rainwater for the mall’s internal 
plumbing, fountains, and rooftop greenhouse. Now, it’s 
a clogged, filth-ridden mess—a mix of valuable 
drinking water, dangerous contamination, and places 
where something unnatural might be lurking.
Layout:
o
Narrow walkways between large 
industrial water tanks (some 
leaking).
o
Deep, clogged drainage pools filled 
with debris, bodies, and who-knows-
what else.
o
Rain barrels, some clean, some 
contaminated, others hiding 
something beneath the surface.
o
Metal catwalks run across certain 
sections, though some are rusted 
and unstable.
Threats:
o
1d4 Shambler Zombies trapped in 
knee-high water, dormant until 
disturbed.
o
1d3 “Drowned Ones”—waterlogged 
corpses that rise up if players step into 
deep water.
o
Something inside a storm drain 
keeps whispering…
Hazards:
o
Collapsing Walkways: Roll Dexterity 
(DC 14) to avoid falling into a water-
filled pit.
o
Contaminated Water: Drinking from 
the wrong barrel? Roll Constitution 
(DC 12) or risk infection or 
hallucinations.
o
Slippery Surfaces: Running may 
cause a Dexterity check (DC 10) to 
avoid slipping into hazards.
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps (Roll 1d4 on Entry)
d4 
Roll
Hazard
1
Waterlogged Bodies: A floating 
corpse suddenly moves, grabbing 
the nearest survivor (Dex DC 14 or 
grappled).
2
Rusting Walkway: The metal 
groans underfoot—first heavy step 
triggers collapse (Dex DC 15 or 
fall 10 ft. into filth below).
3
Boiling Rain Barrel: A barrel looks 
normal, but inside, something 
writhes in the water—a parasitic 
infection (Constitution DC 13 to 
resist illness).
4
Whispering Drain Pipe: A sound 
echoes from a dark storm drain—
listening closely (Wisdom DC 12) 
might reveal a cryptic warning… 
or a growing madness.

NOT LISTEN TO THE DRAIN. IT 
LIES.” The ink looks fresh.
4
Military Markings: Old, faded 
stencils on a rain barrel read 
“QUARANTINE SITE Z-06. DO

sites.name: Construction Scaffolding & Maintenance Ladder
sites.bookText:
Construction 
Scaffolding & 
Maintenance Ladder
“The towering scaffolding clings precariously to the 
side of the mall like a skeletal metal ribcage, rusting 
where the elements have begun to eat away at it. 
Wind whistles through loose panels, rattling them with 
unsettling irregularity. A frayed construction banner, 
still barely clinging to the frame, flaps like a wounded 
bird.  Below,  the  cracked  pavement  is  littered  with 
shattered  glass,  old  safety  helmets,  and  an 
abandoned tool belt—proof that someone attempted 
this climb before… and didn’t finish. The maintenance 
ladder ascends alongside the scaffolding, bolted to 
the building’s side but wobbling with every gust of 
wind. Something… skitters above, unseen.”
Description:

Layout: The scaffolding is a five-story 
structure of rusted metal beams and 
loose planks, providing a dangerous but 
viable alternative route to the rooftop. A 
rickety maintenance ladder is bolted into 
the concrete wall beside it, leading directly 
to an access hatch on the roof. A partially 
collapsed platform about halfway up forces 
climbers to leap or navigate a precarious 
plank (DEX save to avoid falling).

Threats:
o
“The Clinger” – A half-dead 
construction worker-turned-zombie 
hanging from a harness, groaning 
softly in the wind. It will attack only if 
disturbed or if the ladder shakes 
too much.
o
Flying Carrion Beasts – Large, 
mutant crows peck at corpses 
tangled in the upper scaffolding. They 
don’t attack outright, but will scatter 
loudly (increasing Tension) if 
startled.

Hazards:
o
Loose Beams & Weak Planks – 
Stepping on the wrong section 
triggers a DEX (DC 13) save or a 
1d6 ft fall.
 481 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
o
Gale-Force Winds – Sudden wind 
gusts may force climbers to make a 
Strength (DC 12) check or lose their 
grip.
o
Entangled Ropes & Gear – The 
construction site is littered with 
abandoned tools and safety lines. A 
survivor who fails a climbing check 
might tangle in old harnesses 
instead of falling outright.
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps (Roll 1d4 on Entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1

way! DEX save (DC 14) to jump to 
safety, or fall 10 feet (1d6 
bludgeoning).
2

construction worker dangles by a 
safety line. Disturbing it causes 
the body to drop noisily, adding 
+2d6 Tension.
3
Swarm of Rats – Nesting in a 
supply bag, they scatter across 
the scaffolding, causing survivors 
to make a DEX save (DC 13) or 
slip.
4
Ladder Failure – One rung 
snaps! The climber must make a 
STR save (DC 12) or fall 15 feet 
(or catch a hanging rope at 
disadvantage).

won’t open from outside. God 
help us.”

sites.name: Rooftop Garden Lounge
sites.bookText:
Rooftop Garden 
Lounge
“The shattered remains of a once-charming open-air 
café stretch before you, framed by rusted patio chairs 
and overturned tables. String lights, long burned out, 
sway gently in the wind, their bulbs clinking together 
like eerie wind chimes. A small, circular bar sits in the 
corner, its countertop still sticky with dried cocktails 
and  dust.  Scattered  wine  glasses—some  upright, 
some  toppled—dot  the  scene,  many  held  in  the 
skeletal grips of their former owners. Their slumped 
bodies rest in patio loungers, heads tilted back as if 
gazing at the sky one last time. The scent of decayed 
roses lingers in the air, mixing with the unmistakable 
stench  of  death.  A  faded  sign  by  the  bar  reads: 
‘Sunset Special: Half-Off All Drinks!’”
Description

Layout: The lounge sits on the highest 
accessible part of the mall’s rooftop, offering a 
clear vantage point of the surrounding 
cityscape. The bar and seating area form a 
semi-circle around a small stage where a 
forgotten karaoke machine stands, its screen 
cracked and flashing garbled lyrics. A garden 
trellis, now overgrown with dead vines, creates 
partial cover along one side, while metal patio 
tables and chairs are scattered around. The 
roof’s edge is dangerously close, with a 
waist-high railing that looks unreliable.

Threats:
1d4+1 Corpse Drinkers – Zombies still clutching their 
glasses, eerily still until disturbed.
1 ‘Last Toast’ Shambler – A bloated corpse that 
suddenly vomits acidic bile if approached.
Unstable Roof Section – The area near the bar has 
softened with water damage (DEX save DC 14 to 
avoid falling through).

Hazards:
o
Glass Shards Everywhere – Stealth 
attempts suffer disadvantage due to 
crunching glass.
o
Flammable Alcohol Stains – Spilled 
booze on the bar and ground can be 
set alight (fire spreads 5ft per round).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Old Bartender’s Revolver (One 
Bullet Left) – Found under the 
bar, a rusty but functional .38 
revolver (25 SV). Six notches are 
scratched into the handle.
2
Half-Drained Liquor Bottles – 
Useful as Molotov cocktails (each 
deals 2d6 fire damage, 5ft radius). 
(15 SV each)
3
Wind-Up Music Box – Sitting on 
the bar, it still plays a tune… a 
familiar tune. (50 SV if traded)
4
Crumpled Letter from a Survivor 
– Signed ‘To My Love—Hope You 
Made It,’ tucked into a dusty wine 
bottle. A hidden safe code is 
scrawled on the back.
5
Emergency Stash in a Wine 
Crate – Behind the bar, a hidden 
emergency ration pack (5 days’ 
worth of food & water). (50 SV)
6
Luxury Cigar Box (Mostly Intact) 
– A collectible worth 75 SV, but 
smoking one reduces Stress by 
1d4 at the cost of attracting 
zombies with the smell.

sites.name: Loading Dock Roof Access
sites.bookText:
Loading Dock Roof Access serves as a 
secondary entry point into the mall, connecting the 
rooftop to the warehouse and receiving areas. It’s a 
key escape route but also a prime ambush zone—
any noise will echo down into the cavernous loading 
docks below, potentially drawing a horde.
Layout:
o
A steep metal stairwell leads down to 
the loading dock entrance.
o
A chain-link fence with barbed wire 
surrounds the stairwell’s landing.
o
Scattered crates and pallets provide 
half-cover but also block easy 
movement.
o
A weathered security checkpoint 
booth stands nearby, its window 
cracked.
Threats:
o
1d4+1 Shamblers inside the 
stairwell, attracted by movement or 
noise.
 486 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
o
1 security guard corpse—it might get 
up.
o
Unknown noises drifting from below
—something lurks in the loading dock.
Hazards:
o
Slippery Stairs: DC 12 Dexterity 
check to avoid slipping (falling deals 
1d6 damage & makes noise).
o
Collapsing Stair Section: On a roll of 
1 on a D20 while crossing, a stair 
gives way, forcing a DC 14 Dexterity 
save or falling into the dark.
o
Alarms in the Security Booth: If 
triggered, +2d6 Tension from the 
blaring klaxon.

in the dead guard’s hands. (1d8+1

3

access to locked storage areas in 
the warehouse below. (Critical for 
looting supplies!)
4

military rations, still good. (SV 20 
per meal, 80 total SV)
5
Survivor’s Bloodstained 
Notebook – Entries hint at an 
escape attempt gone wrong. 
(Ambiguous Lore Clue)
6

but might be useful for disguises 
or trade. (SV 10)

and the corpse, players can find cryptic hints about 
what really happened here:

the outbreak.

3

security officer mentioning “strange

unloading sealed containers before 
everything went to hell.

sites.name: Old Staff Break Room & Lockers
sites.bookText:
Old Staff Break Room 
& Lockers
“A stale, musty scent fills the dimly lit break room. A 
half-eaten sandwich, now covered in mold, sits atop a 
long-forgotten lunch tray. Rows of battered lockers 
line the back wall, their doors hanging open or dented 
from  frantic  hands.  The  vending  machines  are 
cracked—one appears to have been shattered with a 
fire  extinguisher,  its  contents  long  looted.  A 
microwave beeps in short, irregular bursts, as if trying 
to finish a meal that never got made. On the far wall,  
smeared in dark, dried blood, someone scrawled a 
single warning in shaky, desperate letters: ‘DON’T 
GO DOWNSTAIRS.’”
Description:

Layout: A standard break room with a 
microwave station, vending machines, a 
coffee corner, and a long communal table 
littered with forgotten magazines and crumpled 
fast food wrappers. A row of rusting lockers 
stands along one wall, some closed, others 
forced open.

Threats: 1d4+1 Crawler Zombies (hiding 
under furniture, lockers, and behind vending 
machines).

Hazards:
o
Collapsing Ceiling Panels – Loose 
panels overhead may fall (1d6 
damage, DC 12 Dex save to avoid).
o
Sparking Electrical Panel – Frayed 
wires from a broken vending machine 
may cause a shock hazard (1d6 
lightning damage if tampered with).
o
Rotten Floor Section – The tiles near 
the lockers sag slightly. Too much 
pressure (or a failed Investigation 
check) will cause a survivor to fall 
into the vent system below (1d6 
falling damage, separated from party).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Finds
1
Keyring (Contains 3 Unlabeled 
Keys) – One key unlocks a 
janitor’s closet, another a storage 
room, and one is a mystery.
2
Energy Drinks (2x, Expired) – 
Drinking restores 1 HP but imposes 
disadvantage on Dex saves for 
10 minutes (jitters).
3
Abandoned Wallets (3x) – 
Contains IDs of former employees 
and $37 in small bills (worth 10 
SV if bartered).
4
Locked Locker (DC 15 Strength 
or Lockpicking) – Inside is a 9mm 
Handgun (1d6 damage, 15 SV) 
with 3 rounds (5 SV each).
5
Waterlogged Employee Logbook 
– Names, schedules, and strange 
redacted notes about after-hours 
meetings.
6
Coffee Can (Hidden in Fridge) – 
A rolled-up security map and 
partially melted keycard are 
inside (important for lore).
Ambiguous Lore:
d4 Roll Cryptic Clue
1
Journal Page (Bloodstained, 
Torn) – “They told us to keep 
quiet, but the night crew saw 
something down there. I’m not 
going back.”
2
Memo from BioDyne 
Corporation – “Effective 
immediately, all deliveries to Sub-
Basement 2 require Level 5 
authorization.”
3
Strange Employee Pass (Worn & 
 489 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
Cracked) – On the back, written in 
faded Sharpie: “Ask Marcus 
about the blueprints. It’s not just 
a mall.”
4
Graffiti Inside a Locker – “The 
Corpse Man comes when you 
sleep. Don’t close your eyes.”

(echoes through vents).


hazards and reinforce doors.

Crawlers - “Locker Corpses”)

AC
11

10

Claw (1d4) or Bite (1d6, DC

10 ft (Crawling)

without Investigation 15+)

- When lockers or vending machines are moved, one

- If a survivor falls through the rotten floor, another

after spending 5+ minutes 
inside)
d6 Roll
Event

3

touched it. Something inside just 
shifted.
4

Vents – A hushed, unintelligible 
voice seems to be speaking from 
inside the walls.
5
Radio Interference – If anyone 
has a radio, static bursts

through it, repeating a single

high-mystery area with hidden dangers, light lore 
clues, and solid scavenging rewards. It’s a great 
place for players to gather early resources but also 
plants seeds of unease about the mall’s deeper 
horrors.

sites.name: Rooftop Air Conditioning & Ventilation Ducts
sites.bookText:
Rooftop Air 
Conditioning & Ventilation 
Ducts
“A low mechanical hum vibrates through the rooftop 
as the mall’s massive ventilation system chugs along, 
half-functional despite years of neglect. The industrial 
fans  rattle  in  their  rusted  housings,  their  motors 
occasionally  sputtering  as  if  gasping  for  breath. 
Jagged metal grates line the enormous ducts, some 
bent or pried open—too large for just rats. The stale 
air carries a mixture of mildew, ozone, and something 
rotten, like meat left out in the sun. A gust of wind 
kicks up loose debris, sending a faded security badge 
skittering across the rooftop. Something deep inside 
the vents makes a faint, rhythmic scratching noise—
too slow to be a rat, too erratic to be the wind…”
General Description
The mall’s air conditioning and ventilation system 
spans the entire rooftop, connecting to maintenance 
shafts, storage rooms, and even some stores below. 
Large, boxy AC units stand in long rows, some still 
humming faintly while others have been pried open—
either for scrap metal, shelter, or something worse. The 
ducts themselves are big enough to crawl through, 
but the tight spaces limit movement and visibility.
Some maintenance hatch doors remain locked, while 
others hang open, their hinges rusted and twisted. 
There are signs that someone—or something—has 
been using the vents as a hidden passageway. The 
deeper the players investigate, the clearer it becomes: 
they are not alone up here.
