sites.name: Communications Tower & Satellite Dishes
sites.bookText:
Communications 
Tower & Satellite Dishes
“A skeletal radio tower juts into the overcast sky, its 
rusted  frame  groaning  in  the  wind.  The  array  of 
satellite dishes, once pristine, are now caked with 
grime and riddled with bullet holes. A tangled mess of 
cables drapes across the rooftop, some severed and 
sparking with dying energy. A control terminal flickers 
weakly,  its  screen  displaying  garbled  text  and 
distorted  maps.  Nearby,  a  toppled  emergency 
broadcast speaker lies half-submerged in a pool of 
rainwater,  still  whispering  faint  static.  Something 
about  the  distorted  signal  doesn’t  sound  quite… 
human.”
General Description

Layout:
o
A large rooftop section dedicated to 
communications infrastructure.
o
A 20-foot radio tower, climbable but 
rusted (DEX DC 12 to climb safely, 
failure results in a fall for 2d6 
damage).
o
Three large satellite dishes, all 
misaligned, one of which has 
something strange stuck in it.
o
A locked communications shed 
housing the radio terminal, 
broadcast controls, and some 
emergency supplies.
o
Several loose cables, tangled in 
places—could be used as tripwires, 
restraints, or jury-rigged traps.
 493 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall

Threats:
o
1d4+1 Stalker Zombies (hiding 
among the wreckage, highly stealthy, 
don’t groan until they strike).
o
1 “Repeater Zombie” (a former 
technician fused into the tower by 
unknown means, still clutching a radio 
headset, mindlessly muttering into the 
static).

Hazards:
o
Tangled Wires: Loose, dangerous trip 
hazards. Running without caution 
(DEX DC 13) results in falling prone 
and possibly electrocution (1d4 
lightning damage).
o
Structural Decay: The tower and 
dishes are unstable. Sudden 
movements (jumping, climbing, 
combat) have a 20% chance to 
loosen metal debris, causing falling 
objects (1d6 damage, DEX save to 
avoid).
o
Radio Interference (Weird Signal): 
Strange broadcast frequencies bleed 
into the static. Listening for too long 
(more than 1 minute) may cause a 
Willpower Save (WIS DC 14) or 
induce paranoia, hallucinations, or 
cryptic whispers from an unknown 
entity.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Working Ham Radio – Can send 
distress signals, but who will 
answer? (50 SV)
2
Encrypted Hard Drive – Requires 
hacking (INT DC 16); contains 
unsettling classified data. (75 SV)
3
Emergency Generator (Partially 
Functional) – Can be repaired with 
parts (100 SV if fully restored).
4
Old Military Transmission Logs – 
Pages detailing emergency 
d6 Roll Notable Items
evacuations, some mentioning the 
mall by name.
5
Survivor’s Notes (Bloodstained) – 
Scattered journal entries detailing 
failed radio contacts. Mentions “the 
whispers in the static.”
6
Torn BioDyne Memo – A half-
burned document describing 
experimental “resonance 
frequencies” and their effect on 
the undead.
Ambiguous Lore (Roll d4)
These clues create uncertainty about the apocalypse’s 
origins:
d4 Roll Clue Found on the Rooftop
1
Repeating Emergency 
Broadcast: “THIS IS NOT A TEST. 
DO NOT RESPOND TO 
UNKNOWN SIGNALS. TRUST NO 
RADIO CONTACT.”
2
Scrawled in Blood on the Tower: 
“THEY CAN HEAR US.”
3
Handwritten Note Taped to the 
Terminal: “The signal called them. 
We thought we were getting help. 
We were wrong.”
4
Fragment of a Military Memo: 
“Station 37 confirmed 
anomalous auditory feedback. 
Immediate shutdown ordered. 
Personnel missing.”
Tension Impact

Tension Change

Tower
+1d6 Tension (noise, 
unstable metal creaks)

Radio
+1d4 Tension (potentially 
alerts zombies)

= Help, 4-6 = Something 
else hears)


HP: 15





Special: Stealthy (DC 14 Perception to detect 
before attack), silent movement, can climb 
walls.
Repeater Zombie (1 Unique)

HP: 20

AC: 13

Attack: Static Discharge (1d8 lightning 
damage, 10ft radius, CON DC 13 for half).

Special: Muttering in Static (Anyone within 
10ft must make a WIS DC 14 save or 
experience auditory hallucinations for 1d4 
minutes).

violently, forcing a CON save (DC 
12) or suffer temporary deafness.
2
Distant Helicopter Sound: A 
shadow briefly passes over the 
rooftop… then vanishes.
3
Zombie Howl Below: A distant 
screech echoes, followed by the 
sound of something climbing…
4
Mysterious Signal: A voice 
comes through the static—“Is 
anyone alive out there?” (It 
sounds… wrong.)
5
Dead Technician Discovered: A 
corpse in a security uniform 
clutching a bloodstained notepad. 
His eyes are missing.
6
Lightning Strike! A bolt of 
lightning hits the tower, forcing 
a DEX save (DC 15) or take 3d6 
damage. The shock momentarily 
activates the broken broadcast 
system. What does it say?
Final Notes

This rooftop area offers a major tactical 
advantage but also risks exposure to 
external threats.

The radio signals could provide escape 
routes… or lure in something dangerous.

sites.name: Skybridge to Parking Garage
sites.bookText:
Skybridge to Parking 
Garage (Collapsed)
“The skybridge stretches ahead, a once-pristine glass 
tunnel  linking  the  mall  to  its  towering  parking 
structure. Now, half of it is gone—shattered panels 
and twisted steel beams leave a gaping wound in the 
walkway. The remaining section sways slightly in the 
wind, its cracked floor tiles dusted with dried blood. 
Below,  the  horde  shifts  and  groans—dozens  of 
zombies trapped in the wreckage of crumpled cars. 
The only way across is a desperate leap, a makeshift 
bridge… or a riskier idea altogether.”
Description:

Layout:
The intact portion of the skybridge remains attached to 
the mall’s upper level, leading 20 feet toward the 
collapsed gap (a 15-ft-wide missing section).
The parking garage side is still accessible, but only by 
crossing the gap.
Shattered safety glass crunches underfoot, and 
hanging support cables dangle from the breach.
A handmade rope bridge (DC 15 Dexterity check to 
use) stretches precariously across.
Bloodstains suggest someone tried—and failed—to 
make it.

Threats:
o
Fallen zombies writhe in the 
wreckage below. They can’t climb up, 
but if players fall in, they’re trapped in 
a nightmare.
o
A single Stalker zombie clings to the 
ceiling, waiting to drop on the first 
person to attempt crossing.
o
Biker gang tracks (fresh tire marks, 
graffiti) suggest possible raiders 
nearby.

Hazards:
o
Strong Winds (Dex Save DC 12) – 
Sudden gusts shake the weakened 
structure.
o
Weak Floor Tiles (Dex Save DC 14) 
– Some sections collapse under too 
much weight.
o
Rope Bridge (Dex Save DC 15 or 
Athletics DC 12) – A survivor built 
this, but it’s old and frayed.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Bloodstained Notebook – 
Survivor’s last log details a failed 
escape attempt. The final words are 
smudged.
2
Military Drop Bag – Contains an 
MRE (food, 5 SV), flashlight (10 
SV), and a combat knife (1d6 dmg, 
15 SV).
3
Abandoned Toolbox – Contains 
hammer, nails, and enough scrap 
to construct a sturdy makeshift 
bridge.
4
Bolt-Action Hunting Rifle (1d10 
dmg, 5 rounds, 75 SV). The 
previous owner is lying nearby, 
throat torn out.
5
Parking Garage Keycard – Grants 
access to a hidden vehicle storage 
area.
6
Disturbing Map – Scrawled 
warnings, weird symbols, and 
references to “the ones in the 
dark.” (Lore Clue)
Ambiguous Lore Clues
d4 Roll
Mysterious Evidence
1
Military Memo – Orders 
 496 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
mentioning “containment breach 
near civilian zones.”
2
Cultist Markings – Graffiti in 
blood: “The Crossing is Sealed, 
but They Will Find Another Way.”
3
BioDyne Research Clipboard – 
Notes discussing zombie 
migration patterns and “Phase 3 
testing.”
4
Survivor’s Message (Scratched 
Into Metal) – “The island is real. 
But it’s not what you think.”
Tension Impact

Falling debris, loud noises, or gunfire here 
increase Tension by +1d4.

Crossing successfully without noise keeps 
Tension steady.

Triggering a major collapse or fight attracts 
a massive horde (+2d6 Tension).

6

Con Save DC 12 vs. Infection)


o

striking from above.
o

detected unless actively searched for.
Biker Scouts (Raider Survivors)
AC: 12
HP: 18
Weapons: Handgun (1d6), Machete (1d8)
Abilities:
o
Gang Signal: If not taken out in 3 
rounds, reinforcements arrive.
 497 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
o
Junk Armor: Takes half damage from 
shrapnel or environmental hazards.
Optional Challenge: “The 
Leap”

Players can attempt a running jump (DC 16 
Athletics) to cross the gap.

Failure: Fall into the car wreck below, taking 
3d6 damage and facing 2d6 zombies.

If someone falls, a teammate can pull them 
up with a successful DC 15 Strength check.
Narrative Hooks & Future 
Consequences

If the players fully repair the bridge, this 
provides safe travel to the Parking Garage—
but also makes it accessible to zombies or 
raiders.

Survivor factions might try to take control of 
the bridge if they see its value.

The Keycard hints at hidden vehicles or 
supply caches deeper inside the garage.

The Disturbing Map suggests that the mall’s 
collapse was not entirely accidental…
Survivor’s Last Words (Scrawled on the Wall):
“We tried the bridge. We almost made it. If you’re 
reading this… don’t follow us. There’s something under 
the cars. It waits until night.”

sites.name: Rooftop Cargo Elevator
sites.bookText:
Rooftop Cargo 
Elevator (Still Functional?)
“A massive freight elevator looms at the edge of the 
rooftop,  its  steel  doors  partially  open,  revealing  a 
dark, yawning shaft below. A single overhead light 
flickers erratically, casting long, twitching shadows on 
the rain-slicked concrete. A stiff breeze sends the 
tattered remains of an old security vest fluttering near 
the call button, smeared with dried blood. A dented 
control panel buzzes weakly, the call button blinking a 
sickly  green.  Somewhere  deep  below,  something 
shifts in the darkness—was that just the wind in the 
shaft, or something… breathing?”
General Description

Layout:
The freight elevator is a large industrial lift 
designed for transporting cargo between the 
mall’s storage floors and the rooftop. The shaft 
drops four stories into darkness, with a thick 
emergency access ladder lining one wall. A 
caged-off generator box sits nearby, its 
power flickering weakly.

Threats:
o
Possible zombie ambush inside the 
elevator cab, where something 
slumped in the corner might not be as 
dead as it looks.
o
Undead in the shaft—perhaps 
survivors fell inside while trying to 
escape.
o
The elevator may activate suddenly, 
plunging downward with players 
inside.

Hazards:
23. Partially broken floor panels in the 
elevator cab—stepping in the wrong 
place could cause a player to fall into 
the shaft (DEX DC 14 to avoid, 6d6 
damage).
24. Sparking control panel—may cause 
a short-circuit if tampered with 
incorrectly.
25. Noise risk—powering the elevator 
increases Tension significantly as 
the loud machinery whirs to life.
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps (Roll 1d4 upon entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Malfunctioning Call Button: 
When pressed, the elevator doors 
 498 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
slam open with a deafening clang. 
(+2d6 Tension immediately; 50% 
chance zombies arrive within 1d4 
rounds.)
2
Power Surge: The elevator panel 
sparks violently when touched. 
(DEX DC 13 or take 1d8 electric 
damage.) If failed, the whole 
rooftop lights up for 1d4 
minutes, attracting threats.
3
Loose Cables in the Shaft: If 
anyone tries to climb down, a 
frayed cable snaps, sending 
something heavy and rotten 
tumbling past them (WIS Save DC 
12 or be frightened for 1 minute).
4
Elevator Drops Unexpectedly: If 
players restore power, the 
elevator suddenly drops 1d4 
floors before catching itself, 
potentially trapping survivors 
inside (DEX DC 15 to escape in 
time).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Toolbox – Contains pliers, 
wrenches, and duct tape (Useful 
for repairing the elevator, 15 SV).
2
Spare Fuel Canister (Half-Full) – 
Can be used for a generator or 
makeshift Molotov (10 SV).
3
Mall Maintenance Logbook – 
Details old security codes, a 
hidden storage room in the 
basement, and a strange shipment 
marked “Project Eclipse.”
4
Cracked Walkie-Talkie – 
Malfunctions often, but picks up 
eerie radio static. Sometimes, it 
broadcasts whispering voices 
d6 Roll Notable Items
(Lore item, 5 SV).
5
Bloodstained Security Keycard – 
Belonged to someone important. 
Could unlock a high-clearance 
area elsewhere in the mall.
6
Old Security Firearm 
(Malfunctioning) – A jammed 
revolver (1d8 damage, 3 rounds 
left) that may misfire if used (roll 
1d6; on a 1, it explodes, dealing 
1d6 damage to the user).
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered clues hint at the mall’s chaotic downfall, but 
they contradict each other, deepening the mystery:
d4 Roll Clue
1
Scrawled on the inside of the 
elevator cab: “Don’t go down. It’s 
not just the dead anymore.”
2
A torn military dossier in the 
maintenance locker: “Quarantine 
failed. Agents compromised. DO 
NOT ENGAGE subjects from Zone 
3.”
3
Spray-painted on the elevator 
wall: “We heard them calling from 
below.”
4
A broken tablet showing a 
paused video – A desperate 
survivor warning: “They didn’t 
just die. They changed.” Then, 
the feed cuts out.
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action or Loot
SV Reward
Restoring Elevator 
Power
200 SV
Toolbox
15 SV
Security Keycard
50 SV (If used to 
 499 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
Action or Loot
SV Reward
open a locked area, 
+100 SV)
Walkie-Talkie (Lore 
Item)
5 SV
Fuel Canister
10 SV
Securing the Elevator 
& Clearing Threats
150 SV
Tension Impact

Restoring Power to the Elevator: +2d6 
Tension (Loud mechanical noise).

Using the Elevator: +1d6 Tension per use—
zombies may notice movement between floors.

Tampering with the Generator Box: +1d4 
Tension (Sparking, loud buzzing).
Possible Enemies
d6 Roll
Encounter
1-2
Elevator Crawlers (1d4) – Half-
crushed zombies in the shaft, 
weak but desperate to bite.
3
Corpse in the Cab – It looks 
dead… but isn’t. Rises as a 
zombie the moment the players 
enter.
4
“The Screamer” – A bloated 
corpse tangled in the cables 
drops unexpectedly, screaming 
as it falls. This summons 1d6 
zombies in nearby areas.
5
Security Guard Zombie 
(Enhanced) – Still wearing 
armor, harder to kill. Carries a 
rusted keyring (random locked 
doors somewhere in the mall).
6
Horrifying Maw (Mutation) – A 
flesh-warped monster stuck in 
the shaft, its tentacle-like arms 
dragging bodies down. A failed 
elevator ride could send 
players straight into its lair.
Monster Stats
Elevator Crawler (1d4)

AC: 10 | HP: 8

Attack: Bite (1d6, 25% infection chance)

Special: Can latch onto ankles (STR DC 13 
to break free).
Security Guard Zombie (1)

AC: 14 (Kevlar Vest) | HP: 22

Attack: Baton (1d6 bludgeoning) or Bite (1d8)

Special: Stagger Resistance – Reduces all 
non-headshot damage by half.
The Screamer

AC: 9 | HP: 10

Attack: None, but its dying wail summons 
1d6 zombies.

Special: Scream Effect – All creatures within 
30ft must make a WIS DC 14 save or suffer -2 
to all rolls due to sheer panic for 1d4 rounds.
Horrifying Maw (Mutation)

AC: 16 | HP: 45

Attacks: Tentacle Grab (1d8 + grapple), 
Devour (1d10, only on restrained targets)

Special: Dragging Horror – Can yank 
survivors down the elevator shaft (STR DC 
15 to resist).
Final Thoughts

This elevator encounter is a perfect risk-
reward scenario—fixing it could save time 
and open new paths, but it creates massive

sites.name: The “Safe Room”
sites.bookText:
The “Safe Room” (That 
Isn’t Safe)
“A massive steel door, rusted at the edges, stands 
sealed before you. Bold red letters above it read: 
EMERGENCY
 
SHELTER
 
–
 
SAFETY 
GUARANTEED. Scratched  beneath,  in  a  frantic 
hand, are the words: ”WE WERE WRONG.” The air 
is heavy with the smell of mildew and something far 
worse—something  rotting,  something  old.  A  faint 
thump  echoes  from  inside,  rhythmic  and  insistent. 
Whatever is in there… it hasn’t stopped knocking.”
Description
Layout: The shelter is a reinforced panic room built into 
the mall’s structure, meant to house survivors in the 
event of a disaster. It features thick concrete walls, a 
ventilation system, and a secondary access hatch 
leading into the air duct system—though it’s been 
forced open from the inside.
Threats: Something still alive (or undead?) is knocking 
from inside. If unsealed, a twisted monstrosity awaits 
within—a “Hungerling”, a human who survived 
starvation too long and turned into something… 
different.
Hazards:
o
Trapped Pressure Door: Opening it 
incorrectly triggers an airlock-style 
depressurization, throwing anyone 
near the door 10 feet backward (1d6 
bludgeoning damage).
o
Collapsing Ceiling Panel: Rusted 
supports overhead may fall at any 
sudden movement (DEX save DC 13 
to avoid 2d6 damage).
o
Vent Dwellers: If players check the 
open duct hatch, a feral survivor 
(now a ghoul) may drop onto them.
Interactables & Loot

Emergency Food Rations (x6) – Canned 
meat, high-calorie biscuits (+6 days of food, 30 
SV).

Water Purification Tablets (x4 packs) – 
Essential for long-term survival (15 SV).

“Safe Room Manual” – Contains blueprints 
of the mall (can be used to locate hidden 
rooms).

Security Keycard (Red, Level 2) – Unlocks 
storage caches in the underground service 
tunnels.

Corpse with a Notebook – The final log of 
someone who sealed themselves in (contains 
an ominous warning, see Lore Table below).
Ambiguous Lore
(Roll 1d4 to determine what the players find in the 
notebook and on the shelter walls.)
d4 Roll Cryptic Message Found
1
“It wasn’t the food that ran out 
first. It was us.” – Implication that 
survivors turned to cannibalism.
2
“We let him back in… we 
shouldn’t have. The hunger 
changes you.” – Suggests an 
experiment gone wrong or a cursed 
affliction.
3
“The air isn’t clean. Don’t breathe 
too deep. Look at my skin. LOOK 
AT MY SKIN.” – Airborne infection? 
Poisonous mold? The players don’t 
know.
4
“They promised to come back for 
us. They never did. THEY LIED.” 
– Could refer to the government, 
the military, or a private company 
like BioDyne.
 501 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
XP & Survival Value (SV)

Securing the shelter (clearing threats): 300 
SV

Recovering the Emergency Rations & 
Water: 50 SV

Finding the Security Keycard: 100 SV

Gaining access to the “Safe Room Manual”: 
75 SV

Interacting with the “Hungerling” (combat 
or otherwise): Bonus 50 SV
Tension Impact

Opening the door improperly: +1d6 Tension

Triggering a loud event (collapsing ceiling, 
screaming creature, gunfire): +2d6 Tension

If the players leave without sealing the 
shelter: +1 Tension per hour (as things crawl 
out).
Encounter Table
(Roll 1d6 to determine what’s inside when the door 
opens.)
d6 Roll What’s Inside?
1-2
A desiccated corpse, long since 
dead. Nothing moves… at first. 
(No immediate threat, but searching 
the room too aggressively might 
wake something in the vents.)
3
Three huddled corpses in the 
corner, partially eaten. (One of 
them twitches suddenly—but it’s 
just a reflex… right?)
4
A single survivor, wide-eyed and 
whispering: “Please… don’t let me 
eat again.” (They will attack if given 
food.)
5
Something is still moving, hidden 
d6 Roll What’s Inside?
behind supply crates. (A half-
starved, deranged ghoul lunges 
from the dark.)
6
The room is empty… at first 
glance. But the walls? Scratched 
and gnawed at from the inside. 
Whatever was here, it got out.
Hostile Entity – The 
Hungerling
(An emaciated, twitching creature that was* human but 
has lost all recognition of itself.)*

AC: 14

HP: 22

Speed: 40 ft (Moves frantically fast)

Attack: Claw Swipe (1d6 + Grapple) OR Bite 
(2d6, Infection Check DC 14)

Special: “It Still Remembers Hunger” – If 
food is thrown or offered, the Hungerling must 
make a Wisdom Save (DC 12) or stop 
attacking to devour it.
Optional Additions & Horror 
Hooks
(For making the experience even more intense.)
1. The Whispering Vents
If players wait too long outside the shelter, they 
might hear faint whispering from inside the air ducts.
- Perception DC 13: Recognizes multiple voices.
- Perception DC 18: Realizes it’s the same voice, 
repeating over and over.
- At any moment, something could crawl out.**
2. The Paranoia Effect

Anyone who spends more than 10 minutes 
inside the Safe Room must make a Wisdom 
Save (DC 13).
 502 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas

On a failure, they start feeling inexplicably 
hungry.

On a critical failure (Nat 1), they gain 
disadvantage on food-related survival 
checks for 24 hours.
3. The Final Survivor’s Last Words
A dying survivor lies curled in the corner. Their lips 
move… but they have no strength to speak.
- If players succeed on a DC 12 Medicine check, the 
survivor manages to rasp out a final warning before 
passing.
- (Roll 1d4 for final words.)
d4 Roll
The Survivor’s Last Words…
1
“They ate it… and it ate them.”
2
“I locked the real door. This 
one? It was already open.”
3
“The meat wasn’t fresh… but 
neither were we.”
4
“You hear them knocking, 
too? You’re next.”
Final Notes
This encounter creates an excellent blend of survival 
horror, paranoia, and psychological dread. Players 
might expect easy supplies in the shelter—only to find 
that locking yourself away isn’t always the safest 
choice.
They may avoid opening the door entirely, struggle 
with a moral dilemma over a surviving ghoul, or 
unwittingly unleash something into the mall’s 
ventilation system.
Either way—this Safe Room was never safe.

sites.name: Rooftop Barricade Camp
sites.bookText:
Rooftop Barricade 
Camp (Long Abandoned)
“The  wind  howls  across  the  rooftop,  carrying  the 
scent of rain and decay. A half-burned campfire still 
smolders  near  a  makeshift  barricade  of  shopping 
carts,  plywood,  and  rusted  metal  poles.  Sleeping 
bags, torn and stained, are scattered near overturned 
plastic crates filled with empty cans and old water 
bottles.  A  small  wind-up  radio  crackles  faintly, 
repeating  a  message  long  since  lost  to  time.  A 
bloodstained  boot  lies  at  the  edge  of  the  rooftop, 
precariously close to the drop-off. There’s no sign of 
the  camp’s  occupants,  but  something  about  the 
silence feels wrong… like they never truly left.”
Description
Layout: A rough, hastily assembled survivor 
encampment, positioned near a rooftop maintenance 
access door. The area is littered with discarded 
supplies, bedrolls, and half-built barricades. A 
rusted fire escape leads down to the parking garage, 
but it looks unstable.
Threats: No visible zombies at first, but signs of a 
struggle suggest someone—or something—attacked 
this place. A hidden danger still lurks here…

sites.name: Rooftop Swimming Pool & Club
sites.bookText:
Rooftop Swimming 
Pool & Club (Drained & 
Defiled)
“A  wide-open  luxury  space  stretches  across  the 
mall’s rooftop, its once-pristine swimming pool now a 
grotesque ossuary. The drained basin is filled with 
rotting  corpses,  their  bloated  forms  twisted 
together like tangled weeds. Some clawed at the 
walls in their final moments, leaving deep scratches 
in  the  tile.  A  broken  glass  fence  surrounds  the 
perimeter, offering a stunning view of the city skyline
—if not for the occasional shadow moving below. 
Faded  cabana  chairs  and  shattered  cocktail 
glasses litter  the  scene,  and  the  club’s  bar,  still  
stocked  with  long-expired  liquor,  stands  as  a 
monument to the final party that never ended. The 
smell  is  overwhelming. The  air  hums  with  the 
distant sound of static—an old poolside speaker is 
still playing faint, distorted music.”
General Description
Layout & Features:

The Pool (Corpse Pit) – A 15-foot-deep pool, 
filled with piled corpses in varying states of 
decay. Some look recent.

The Club Lounge – A sun-bleached wooden 
deck with overturned cabana chairs, empty 
champagne bottles, and a rusted fire pit.

The DJ Booth – A half-looted sound system 
still humming with power. A mixtape is stuck 
on loop, playing eerie, distorted lounge music.

The Rooftop Bar – Glass shelves are 
shattered, but some alcohol bottles remain 
intact. Cocktail menus list exotic drinks, 
one called “The Final Sunrise.”

The Glass Fence & Skyline View – A waist-
high glass railing, much of it shattered, 
allowing a view of the city and distant plumes 
of black smoke.
Threats & Hazards
Roll 1d4 
on Entry
Environmental Hazard
1
Rogue Shambler – A zombie 
hanging by one arm from the 
shattered glass fence suddenly 
regains movement and lunges 
at the nearest player (Dex 
Save DC 14 or fall prone).
2
Collapsing Pool Floor – Some 
of the tiles around the deep 
end are unstable. A sudden 
misstep (Dex Save DC 12) 
causes a player to slip and fall 
into the corpse pit.
3
Trapped Survivor (or 
Zombie?) – A knocking sound 
comes from an overturned 
cabana. Inside is a barely-alive 
survivor (or a zombie playing 
dead—GM’s choice).
4
Chemical Spill – Broken pool 
chlorine tanks are leaking a 
toxic gas near the poolside 
storage shed. Inhaling too 
long requires a Constitution 
Save (DC 13) or suffer 1d6 
poison damage per round.
Interactables & Loot
Roll 1d6
Loot Found
1
Bartender’s Toolkit – Contains 
small knives, bottle openers, 
and a lighter. (Improvised 
Weapons, 10 SV)
2
High-End Alcohol – Intact 
bottles of whiskey, vodka, and 
absinthe. (Trade Value: 30 SV, 
or morale boost if used 
 506 

Zombie Mall
 
Roof Areas
socially.)
3
DJ’s Laptop (Locked) – Battery 
still partially charged. Contains 
distorted last messages, event 
photos, and an unfinished 
email titled: “What’s 
happening down there?” (Lore 
Clue + 50 SV)
4
Corpse Pit Survivor (Barely 
Alive) – Someone fell in but 
survived. They are starving, 
infected, and delirious. They 
know something important.
5
Hidden Lockbox (Under a 
Cabana Chair) – Contains a 
pistol (25 SV) and 2d6 bullets 
(10 SV each).
6
Military Dog Tag (With Serial 
Number) – What was a soldier 
doing here? The tag has an 
encrypted number scratched 
onto it.
Ambiguous Lore Clues
Roll 
1d4
Lore Clue Found
1
Bartender’s Blood-Stained 
Logbook – Entries describe a 
strange, coughing man who was 
locked in a back room to “sleep it 
off.” The last entry reads: “He 
stopped coughing. Now he’s talking 
to someone. But we locked him in 
alone…”
2
Distorted Security Footage (DJ 
Laptop) – Footage of an 
emergency alert cutting into the 
pool’s live party broadcast. The 
screen flickers violently just before 
people start clawing at their own 
faces.
3
Discarded BioDyne Corp Syringe 
– Found near the bar. The label is 
half-scratched off but still readable: 
“Trial 047A: Neurological 
Synchronization Compound.”
4
Dried Salt Circles & Strange 
Runes – Someone etched occult 
symbols into the floorboards 
beneath the cabanas. They appear 
hurried, incomplete… desperate.

Rewards

SV Earned

Rooftop Pool Area
200 SV

50 SV

(If Present)

Lockbox
50 SV
Safely Securing the 
Rooftop Bar for Use
100 SV
Tension Impact

+1d6 Tension if gunfire or loud combat 
occurs in the open-air rooftop.

+2d6 Tension if the DJ Booth’s sound 
system is turned on (the music may attract 
zombies).

-1d6 Tension if players clear the corpse pit 
and barricade the rooftop entrance.
Potential Enemy 
Encounters
Roll 1d6
Encounter
1-2
1d4 Waterlogged Shamblers 
 507 

Roof Areas
 
Zombie Mall
(formerly pool-goers, now 
bloated and slow-moving)
3
1 Elite Brute (Security Guard) 
– A former bodyguard in riot 
gear, now an unnaturally 
strong zombie
4
1d3 Stalker Zombies – These 
fast-moving, crawling undead 
wait in the corpse pile before 
lunging at prey.
5
A Lone Survivor (Or Is It?) – 
Someone trapped, possibly 
turned.
6
The Drowned Horror (Mini-
Boss Encounter) – A mass of 
corpses fused together, rising 
from the pool like a tide of 
limbs.
Enemy Stat Block Examples
Waterlogged Shambler

AC: 8 | HP: 15 | Speed: Slow

Attack: Claw (1d6) or Grapple (STR DC 12 to 
escape)

Special: Drenched – Physical hits cause 
slippery bile spray (DEX Save DC 12 or fall 
prone).
The Drowned Horror (Mini-Boss)
AC: 14 | HP: 50 | Attacks: Slam (2d6)
Special:
o
Horde Flesh – Takes half damage 
from slashing and piercing.
o
Dragging Hands – Each turn, grabs a 
new enemy (STR Save DC 15 or 
restrained).
o
Death Rattle – On death, screams, 
causing +3d6 Tension increase and 
summoning 1d4 additional zombies 
from the mall below.
Final Thoughts

This open rooftop setting makes it high-risk 
for combat (gunfire is loud), but also a 
perfect potential base.

The pool corpse pit can be a death trap or a 
resource if cleared.

The DJ Booth & Military Clues provide extra 
mystery tying into the mall’s greater 
apocalypse origins.
 508

sites.name: North Lot
sites.bookText:
North Lot (Premium 
Parking)
“A  sea  of  high-end  vehicles—Mercedes,  BMWs, 
Teslas—now sits in eerie silence beneath flickering 
parking  lot  lights.  Many  windshields  are  cracked, 
driver-side  doors  left  open  in  the  chaos  of  the 
outbreak. The valet booth, a small glass box, remains  
eerily intact, with dozens of car keys still hanging 
from labeled hooks inside. Every so often, the distant 
sound of a car alarm blares before abruptly cutting 
off, leaving only the unsettling groans of something 
shuffling between the vehicles. The air smells of oil, 
mildew, and something rotting beneath the sun-baked 
hoods of long-abandoned cars…”
General Description

Layout: A spacious, open parking lot closest 
to the mall’s main entrance, flanked by 
flickering streetlights and rows of luxury 
vehicles. A small valet booth sits near the 
entrance, with a few abandoned kiosks and 
planters offering minimal cover.

Threats: Zombies lurk between the vehicles, 
some trapped inside, others staggering 
between them. Sudden car alarms risk 
alerting more undead.

Hazards:
o
Glass & Debris: Movement requires 
Dexterity DC 12 to avoid stepping on 
broken glass or metal scraps, creating 
noise.
o
Car Alarms: 25% chance per 
unlocked vehicle that the alarm 
triggers, increasing Tension +1d6 
and attracting 1d4 zombies per 
round for 3 rounds.
o
Dead Batteries & Locked Doors: 
Most vehicles are dead or locked. 
Hotwiring requires Intelligence 
(Mechanics) DC 15.
Interactables & Loot
Valet Booth (Locked, AC 12, HP 15)

Contains a key rack with random car keys 
(roll below).

Desk Drawer: Holds a flashlight (15 SV), a 
walkie-talkie (20 SV, limited range), and a 
list of VIP clients.
Luxury Vehicles (Roll 1d6 per searched car)

(30 SV), half-empty water bottles (5

Contains briefcase (locked, DC 16),

4

and a road map with cryptic

hidden zombie inside.

but also distracting zombies 
elsewhere.
2

scouts from a gang arrive to check 
the area. If noticed, they’ll retreat to 
report unless stopped.
3
Incoming Horde (Slow Build-up) – 
Zombies from a distant crash site 
are slowly moving toward the lot, 
arriving in 10 minutes unless

4

might join the group—or betray 
them if things go south.
Final Thoughts
The North Lot is a dangerous but valuable 
scavenging site, offering high-quality loot, vehicles, 
and vital supplies at the cost of noise, 
environmental hazards, and zombie threats.

Strategy Tip: Players should move carefully, 
prioritize stealth, and check vehicles before 
entering.

Risk vs. Reward: Staying too long invites 
Tension events, but a lucky roll might 
secure an escape vehicle.

Long-Term Impact: If the lot is cleared and a 
car secured, players gain a major mobility 
advantage for future raids.

sites.name: East Lot
sites.bookText:
East Lot (Overflow 
Parking)
“A  vast  expanse  of  cracked  pavement  stretches 
before you, littered with the husks of forgotten cars. 
The faded remnants of painted parking lines vanish 
under  layers  of  dirt,  shattered  glass,  and  the 
occasional  dried  pool  of  something  dark.  Rusting 
SUVs and sedans sit at odd angles, some with doors 
hanging open, others still locked up like tombs. The 
distant sound of metal creaking in the wind echoes 
through  the  silence.  A  fallen  traffic  light  leans 
precariously across the entrance, its tangled wires 
exposed like severed veins. In the stillness, the eerie  
feeling  of  being  watched  lingers—this  is  a  dead 
place, but not an empty one.”
Description

Layout: A massive, open lot, packed with 
hundreds of abandoned vehicles in varying 
states of decay. Most cars are looted, but some 
still hold untouched supplies, weapons, or 
personal belongings.

Threats:
o
Scattered Zombies (roll encounter 
table below).
o
Lurking Crawlers trapped under 
wreckage.
o

sites.name: South Lot
sites.bookText:
South Lot (Employee 
Parking)
“The  employee  parking  lot  stretches  out  in  eerie 
silence, the long-abandoned vehicles coated in dust 
and grime. Faded parking lines barely peek through 
cracks  in  the  asphalt,  where  weeds  have  begun 
reclaiming  the  space.  A  rusted  food  truck  leans 
against a crumbling curb, its service window flapping 
in the wind, revealing a pile of rotting sandwiches 
inside.  The  most  disturbing  sight,  however,  is  a 
collapsed chain-link fence near the far wall—behind 
it,  a  mass  of  trapped  zombies  groans  and  claws 
uselessly  against  the  barrier.  They’re  pinned  for 
now…  but  how  long  before  something  sets  them 
loose?”
Description

Layout: A large open parking lot with faded 
lines, cracked pavement, and rows of 
abandoned cars. The southern wall of the 
mall looms ahead, with an employee 
entrance door, a rusted dumpster, and a 
break area with old picnic tables.

Threats:
o
Zombie Herding Zone – A collapsed 
fence has trapped 2d6 zombies 
against the mall wall. They’re helpless 
for now, but noise or a careless move 
could set them free.
o
Hidden Crawlers – 1d4 zombies lay 
beneath certain cars, only attacking if 
someone gets too close.

Hazards:
o
Oil Slick (1d4 locations) – Patches of 
leaked oil and gasoline make running 
hazardous. (DC 13 Dexterity save or 
fall prone).
o
Loose Car Alarms – Any attempt to 
open car doors has a 30% chance of 
setting off an alarm, drawing 
zombies.
Interactables & Loot
Abandoned Vehicles (1d6 Rolls Per Car 
Searched)

Many locked, but can be hotwired (DC 15 
Intelligence + Tools check) or searched for 
loot.
d6 
Roll
Vehicle Contents
1
Keys in ignition – A functioning 
sedan with ½ tank of gas! (Vehicle, 
150 SV)
 133 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall
2
Glove Box Loot – 2d6 loose bullets 
(Handgun or Rifle, 5 SV per bullet)
3
Trunk Surprise – Roll again: 1-3 = 
toolbox (Tools, 20 SV), 4-6 = first aid 
kit (Medical, 25 SV).
4
Zombie Inside! – A reanimated 
driver lunges out (Shambler, Surprise 
Round).
5
Useless Junk – Old receipts, a 
coffee cup, and a terrible air 
freshener.
6
Personal Journal – A survivor’s 
notes hint at a nearby safehouse 
or a hidden stash (DM’s choice).
The Break Room Van (Rusted Food Truck)

Rotting sandwiches and expired energy 
drinks litter the inside.

Loot:
o
Unopened Energy Drinks (x3) – 
Temporary +5ft movement for 1 hour, 
but causes exhaustion afterward (5 SV 
each).
o
Chef’s Knife – Simple melee weapon, 
1d6 slashing (10 SV).
o
Moldy Cooler – Chance for hidden 
loot inside (roll below):
d6 
Roll
Cooler Contents
1-2
Rotten Meat – Completely useless, 
except as a distraction for 
zombies.
3-4
Pack of Cigarettes – Can be used 
for NPC trades (15 SV).
5
Stash of Medicine – Painkillers & 
antibiotics (Medical, 40 SV).
6
Sealed Can of Coffee – Rare 
morale-boosting item (30 SV).
Employee Entrance (Mall Access)

Heavy metal door, slightly ajar. Inside is dark 
and uninviting.

Loot (if searched):
o
Mall Security Keycard (Low-Level 
Access, 1 SV) – May unlock other 
doors.
o
Flashlight (10 SV) – Batteries at 50% 
power.
o
Pack of chewing gum – Worthless, 
but could be used to boost morale.
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered across the parking lot are strange clues 
about the apocalypse’s origins. Players may discover:
d4 
Roll
Clue Found
1
Handwritten Note on a Windshield: 
“Don’t go inside. The basement is 
where it started. If you hear them 
whispering… run.”
2
Corporate Memo (Crushed Under a 
Tire): Mentions “unforeseen 
mutations” in test subjects at 
BioDyne’s off-site storage facility.
3
Religious Flyer Taped to a 
Lamppost: Warns of the Sixth Seal 
being broken, referencing “the dead 
rising in the place of consumption.”
4
Spray-Painted Message Near the 
Employee Door: “THEY’RE STILL 
IN THERE.” But who? And for how 
long?

d6

1-2
Zombie Herd Breakout! The fence 
finally collapses, releasing 2d6 
Shamblers into the lot.
3
Crawlers Under Cars – 1d4 
zombies lie hidden, waiting to grab 
unsuspecting survivors.
4
Lone “Survivor” Approaches – But 
they’re infected and turn mid-
conversation.
5

on the window for help, but can they 
be trusted?


HP: 12 each

AC: 10


save)


numbers.

•
HP: 8
•
AC: 9
•
Attack: Latch (Grapple + Bite, DC 13 STR check to 
break free)
•
Lurk quietly, grabbing ankles when prey gets 
close.
Trapped Survivor (Optional NPC)

HP: 15

AC: 12

Weapon: Makeshift club (1d6)

1-in-3 chance they are infected, turning 
after 1d4 hours.
Survival Strategy & Player 
Choices
•
Risky Quick Escape: Find a working car and drive 
out, but risk drawing attention.
•
Careful Scavenging: Gather supplies quietly, 
avoiding alarms and zombie packs.
•
Tactical Ambush: Use the zombie herd as a 
weapon, luring them toward enemies elsewhere.

sites.name: West Lot
sites.bookText:
West Lot (Delivery Truck 
Lot)
“A sprawling, cracked expanse of pavement stretches 
beyond  the  rear  of  the  mall,  littered  with  rusting 
tractor  trailers  and  the  skeletal  remains  of  looted 
delivery vans. The once-busy loading docks stand 
eerily silent, their massive bay doors yawning open 
like the mouths of dead giants. A jackknifed semi-
truck has spilled its cargo across the lot, cardboard 
boxes  now  torn  open  and  scattered  by  wind  and  
scavengers. An armored truck sits docked by one of 
the  bays,  its  reinforced  doors  battered  but  not 
breached—yet. Near the wreckage, a dusty forklift 
leans precariously, its keys still in the ignition. The air 
is thick with the scent of old fuel and something… 
rotting. The question is, what caused this mess, and  
are they still here?”
General Description

Layout:
o
A large, open-air parking lot with 
numerous abandoned delivery trucks 
and cargo containers.
o
Loading docks with several open, 
revealing mall storage areas.
o
A jackknifed semi-truck has 
collapsed, blocking part of the lot.
o
A docked armored truck looks 
recently disturbed, but unopened.
o
A forklift, still functional, stands near a 
pile of debris.

Threats:
o
1d6+2 Shamblers (trapped inside 
cargo trucks, escape when disturbed).
o
1d4 Runners (lurking inside a 
darkened loading dock).
o
1 Brute Zombie (former trucker, 
inside the tipped-over semi).

Hazards:
1.
Unstable Cargo – Moving near the 
collapsed semi risks a sudden cave-
in (DC 14 DEX save or take 2d6 
damage).
2.
Oil Spill – A slick of spilled motor oil 
makes the ground slippery (DC 12 
DEX save or fall prone).
3.
Horn Trap – A previous survivor jury-
rigged a car alarm on the armored 
truck’s handle. If disturbed, it blares 
loudly, adding +2d6 Tension and 
attracting zombies within 5 minutes.

sites.name: Parking Garage
sites.bookText:
Parking Garage (Multi-
Level)
“A stale, rubbery stench lingers in the cold, damp air 
of the parking garage. Dim emergency lights flicker 
overhead, casting shifting shadows against rows of 
abandoned vehicles. Somewhere in the darkness, the 
sound  of  scraping  metal  echoes—a  door  slowly 
dragging open, or something far worse moving just 
out of sight. The ramps twist upward like a labyrinth 
of rust and decay, leading to the upper levels, where 
the skeletal remains of a crashed helicopter loom 
over  the  top  floor  like  a  monument  to  past 
desperation. The occasional red glow of a security 
camera flickers in the abandoned booth—someone, 
or something, may still be watching.”
General Description
The Multi-Level Parking Garage was once a massive 
vehicle hub, now a sprawling, claustrophobic maze of 
stalled-out cars, cracked pavement, and broken 
barriers. Long, snaking ramps connect its different 
levels, each littered with wreckage, abandoned 
belongings, and the occasional rotting, half-chewed 
corpse.
Layout:
o
Ground Level: Wrecked cars block 
some exits, but there’s cover for 
stealth.
o
Mid Levels: Vehicles here may still be 
usable with repairs. Some car alarms 
might still be active.
o
Top Level: Helipad with a crashed 
police chopper, potential sniper nest.
Threats:
6.
Shamblers (1d6) trapped inside cars, 
bursting out if disturbed.
7.
Silent Stalkers (1d4) – lurking in the 
shadows, moving unpredictably.
8.
“The Watcher” (Unknown) – a 
mysterious observer still using the 
security system.
Hazards:
o
Car Alarms (1d6 chance per floor) – 
Any vehicle interaction might trigger an 
alarm, raising Tension by 1d4 and 
summoning nearby zombies.
o
Collapsed Ceiling (Top Level) – 
Concrete debris makes travel difficult.
o
Oil Slicks (DEX DC 13) – Slippery 
surfaces cause falls (1d6 damage).
o
Undead “Sleepers” – Bodies that 
may rise if disturbed.

sites.name: The Loading Docks
sites.bookText:
The Loading Docks
“The  air  is  thick  with  the  stench  of  rot  and  stale 
exhaust as you step onto the cracked concrete of the 
mall’s loading docks. Stacked pallets, long-forgotten 
shipments,  and  rusting  forklifts  clutter  the  area, 
forming  shadowed  pathways  perfect  for  lurking 
dangers. Heavy-duty steel doors line the loading bays
—some still sealed, others wrenched open, revealing 
glimpses of darkness beyond. A massive eighteen-
wheeler sits jackknifed across two docks, its cargo 
doors  half-open,  an  ominous  trail  of  dried  blood 
leading  inside.  Somewhere  in  the  distance,  metal 
scrapes against concrete—a sound too deliberate to 
be the wind.”
Description

Layout: The loading docks sit at the rear of the 
mall, featuring multiple warehouse-style bay 
doors for receiving shipments. Pallets of 
inventory—some useful, some laughably 
useless—are stacked haphazardly, while 
rusting forklifts and semi-trucks block certain 
pathways.

Threats: A mix of trapped zombies (inside 
trailers), potential bandit ambushes, and 
environmental hazards make this area 
unpredictable.

Hazards:
1.
Loose Stacks of Crates – Any 
movement near them may cause a 
collapse (DEX save DC 14 or take 
2d6 damage, +1d4 Tension).
2.
Oil Spill on the Ground – Moving too 
quickly risks slipping (DEX save DC 12 
 140 

Zombie Mall
 
Exterior Areas
or fall prone).
3.
Cargo Elevator (Power Required) – 
Could allow access to a storage 
basement, if power is restored.
Environmental Hazards & 
Random Events (Roll 1d6 on 
Entry)
d6 
Roll
Hazard/Event
1
Trapped in a Trailer – A survivor’s 
voice calls for help from a locked 
semi-truck cargo hold. When 
opened, it’s 1d4 zombies, not a 
survivor.
2
Forklift Battery Sparks – A nearby 
forklift suddenly shorts out, sending a 
shower of sparks into an oil spill 
(50% chance of igniting a fire).
3
Fallen Worker – A dead mall worker 
is slumped against a supply crate, 
clutching a security keycard for an 
interior maintenance door.
4
Banging from Inside the Mall – 
Something is hitting a sealed door 
from the other side—hard. What’s 
trying to get out?
5
Scavenger Remains – A fresh 
corpse lies facedown near a pile of 
crates, stab wounds visible. A 
notebook in their pocket warns: “They 
saw me. They’re still watching.”
6
Cargo Elevator Buzzes to Life – 
For just a moment, the dormant 
cargo elevator hums, the doors 
slightly ajar… before cutting out 
again. Who—or what—was trying 
to come up?
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Pry Bar – Useful for breaking doors 
and crates (STR check +2, 10 SV).
2
Bolt Cutters – Can open 
chains/locks quietly (15 SV).
3
Fire Axe – Heavy melee weapon, 
loud but strong (1d10 damage, 25 
SV).
4
Medical Crate (Sealed) – Needs a 
crowbar to open but contains 
bandages, antibiotics, and 
adrenaline injectors (50 SV).
5
Semi-Trailer Loot – If successfully 
entered, contains canned goods 
(100 SV) or a zombie ambush 
(GM’s choice).
6
Gasoline Can (Half Full) – Valuable 
for vehicles or Molotovs (30 SV).
Ambiguous Lore: Conflicting 
Clues
d4 
Roll
Strange Clue
1
Blood-Smeared BioDyne Shipment 
Manifest – The contents are listed 
as “Non-Human Bioweapons – 
Subject Zeta-X”. Manifest is signed 
off by a government official.
2
Security Camera Still Blinking – 
The power is out, but one mall 
security camera still flickers with a 
red light—who’s watching?
3
Religious Graffiti on the Walls – 
“The Sixth Seal is Broken. The 
Angels Will Not Save You.” It’s 
freshly painted.
4
Military Emergency Broadcast (If 
 141 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall
Found Radio) – A garbled looping 
transmission states: 
“Containment breach—do not 
engage—hostile variants detected
—secure all exits—end 
transmission.”

Action
SV Reward

300 SV

Medical Crate
50 SV

Trailer Successfully
100 SV

Can
30 SV
Restoring Cargo 
Elevator Power
75 SV
Tension Impact

Breaking Open Cargo Containers or Crates: 
+1d4 Tension (Noise)

Loud Noises (Firing a Gun, Forklift Engine, 
etc.): +2d6 Tension

Opening Certain Trailers or Doors: 50% 
chance to summon 1d4 Shamblers

Using the Cargo Elevator: +2d4 Tension (if it 
activates)
Potential Enemies (Roll 1d6 or 
GM Choice)
d6 
Roll
Enemy Type
1-2
Shamblers (2d4) – Slow, but 
numerous. If alerted, they will crawl 
out of semi-trailers and warehouse 
doors.
3
Crawler Zombies (3) – Hiding 
under pallets, they grab ankles 
(DEX save DC 13 or become 
restrained).
4
Bloated Corpse (Exploder) – Looks 
like a normal dead body—until it 
bursts (Acid spray, 2d6 damage, 
CON save DC 14 or infection risk).
5
“The Watcher” (Human Bandit) – 
Armed with a handgun (2d6 
damage), may flee if outnumbered. 
Possibly a scout for a raider gang.
6
Experimental BioDyne Zombie 
(Fast Variant) – Glows faintly blue, 
moving at terrifying speed (MV 
40ft). If killed, its corpse twitches 
unnaturally.
Enemy Stat Blocks (Compact 
Format)
Shambler (Basic Zombie)

HP: 12 | AC: 10 | ATK: Bite (1d6) | MV: 20ft

Special: Noise Attraction – If one is attacked 
with a gun, +1d4 Tension (moans attract more 
undead).
Bloated Corpse (Exploder Zombie)

HP: 16 | AC: 8 | ATK: No melee, Explosion 
on death (2d6 acid, DC 14 CON save)

Special: Goes off when hit by melee or 
gunfire unless killed silently.
BioDyne “Fast Zombie”

HP: 18 | AC: 13 | ATK: Frenzied Claw Strike 
(2d6 damage) | MV: 40ft

Special: Mutation Instability – When killed, 
50% chance it gets back up next round (1 
HP remaining).
Summary & GM Notes
The Loading Docks are an unpredictable encounter 
zone, great for scavenging (high-value supplies, 
 142 

Zombie Mall
 
Exterior Areas
potential working vehicles, and medical caches) but 
risky due to zombies, environmental hazards, and 
unknown watchers. The cargo elevator hinting at a 
secret basement adds a mystery hook for further 
exploration.

sites.name: Dumpster Alley
sites.bookText:
Dumpster Alley (Behind 
Mall)
“The air is thick with the sickly-sweet stench of rotting 
food  and  industrial  waste.  Massive  dumpsters 
overflow  with  decayed  refuse,  their  lids  barely 
containing  the  writhing  swarm  of  maggots  and 
bloated rats that scurry between piles of filth. Black 
sludge oozes from punctured garbage bags, creating 
a slick hazard on the cracked asphalt. The area is 
eerily  silent,  save  for  the  occasional  rustling  from 
deep within the heaps of trash. A rusted storage shed 
leans precariously against the mall’s outer wall, its 
door half-open. Nearby, a makeshift campfire pit, long 
extinguished, sits next to an abandoned bedroll and a 
few scattered belongings—signs that someone was 
here recently… but where are they now? And more 
importantly—what happened to them?”
General Description
The Dumpster Alley is a service area behind the mall 
where garbage disposal, employee smoke breaks, and 
deliveries took place. Now, it is a festering graveyard of 
waste and decay, partially barricaded by toppled 
dumpsters and piles of abandoned junk.
Layout:

Four industrial dumpsters, some still partially 
closed.

A rusted storage shed filled with cleaning 
supplies and maintenance tools.

A fire-damaged corner of the alley, possibly 
from a past survivor camp.

A broken drainage grate leading into a 
clogged sewer tunnel.

An employee-only exit door, jammed shut 
from the inside.

sites.name: Employee Smoking Area
sites.bookText:
Employee Smoking Area
“The smell of stale cigarettes and burnt coffee lingers 
in the cold night air. A rusting metal ashtray overflows  
with  cigarette  butts,  some  half-smoked,  others 
stained  with  something  darker  than  tobacco. 
Scattered beer cans clink softly in the breeze, some 
crushed under hurried footsteps. A row of dented 
metal benches sits against the grimy brick wall of the 
mall,  their  seats  warped  from  years  of  rain  and  
neglect.  A  single  flickering  security  light  buzzes 
above a  heavy steel back door, its chipped paint 
revealing  layers  of  past  renovations.  A 
faded”Employees Only” sign is barely visible under 
the grime, the door locked but not very secure. A 
weak gust of wind kicks up old wrappers and an 
empty  pill  bottle.  Something  moved  near  the 
dumpsters, but whether it was a rat or something 
worse… you’re not sure.”
Description

Layout: A small, tucked-away employee 
break area behind the mall, accessible through 
a narrow alley near the loading docks. 
Features several metal benches, a rusted 
ashtray, scattered trash, and an old vending 
machine. The locked back door leads to the 
mall’s food court kitchen.

Threats: At first glance, no immediate zombie 
presence—but there are signs of something 
lurking nearby (see Random Threats table).

Hazards: Poor lighting, slippery concrete 
(rainwater pools), risk of alerting zombies 
inside if the back door is forced open 
noisily.
Environmental Hazards & 
Random Threats (Roll 1d6 
on Entry)
d6 
Threat or Hazard
 145 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall
Roll
1
“Is Someone There?” – A lone 
survivor is hiding nearby, watching 
from the shadows. They are 
desperate but unpredictable. (See 
NPC: Terry The Smoker)
2
“It Was Just A Rat… Right?” – A 
scuttling noise from the dumpster
—but it’s a Crawler Zombie (hidden 
inside, will attack if disturbed).
3
Soggy Floor & Loud Noise – 
Stepping into a puddle of murky 
water near the door creates a loud 
splash, alerting anything inside the 
mall. Roll 1d6 zombies in the next 
room.
4
A Horde’s Trail – A large blood 
smear drags from the alleyway into 
the dumpster area. It’s fresh. 
Something was pulled inside 
recently.
5
The Corpse In The Bench – A dead 
mall employee is slumped over on a 
bench, cigarette still in their 
fingers. They reanimate in 1d4 
rounds unless searched. They have 
a master keycard for the food court 
area.
6
“I Heard Something Behind the 
Door…” – The back door handle 
jiggles slightly from the other side. 
Someone, or something, is 
pushing against it. If the players 
listen, roll 1d4:
1-2: A zombie horde heard them.
3: A survivor trapped inside, begging to be let out.
4: It’s just the wind (for now).
Interactables & Loot
d4 
Roll
Loot or Discovery
1
Cigarette Pack (Trade Value, 10 
SV) – Useful for bartering with 
stressed survivors.
2
Beer Cans (Morale Boost, 5 SV) – 
Drinking it slightly restores stress 
but lowers perception temporarily.
3
Employee ID Badge – May grant 
access to locked mall areas, but 
only if readable (50% chance it’s too 
damaged).
4
Lockbox Under Bench – Requires 
Strength DC 15 to break or 
Dexterity DC 12 to pick. Contains 
1d3 of the following: Box of 9mm 
ammo (10 rounds, 15 SV)
Small First Aid Kit (1 use, 20 SV)
Painkillers (Reduce stress, 10 SV, risk of 
addiction on repeated use)
A bloody note that simply reads: 
“DON’T LET THEM IN”
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered around the area are clues hinting at the 
larger mystery. Players may find contradictory 
evidence, keeping the truth uncertain.
d4 
Roll Lore Clue
1
BioDyne Corporation Memo – 
Crumpled in the trash, it warns 
employees: “All off-the-books 
inventory should be stored in the 
basement level immediately. Do not 
discuss Project Egress.”
2
Occult Symbols Scratched on the 
Bench – A warning? A 
summoning? Or just some edgy 
mall goth? The phrase “The Feast 
Comes First” is repeated in three 
 146 

Zombie Mall
 
Exterior Areas
different handwriting styles.
3
Police Report Fragment – “Unruly 
employee detained in back alley, 
ranting about ”eyes under the food 
court” before attacking security.”
4
Mysterious Keyring – Labeled “Mall 
Basement - Do Not Use”. The 
basement level isn’t supposed to 
exist…
NPC Encounter: Terry The 
Smoker
(Optional NPC – Roll on Entry if Players Linger Too 
Long)
Appearance: Middle-aged man in a torn mall janitor 
uniform, smoking the last of his cigarette.
Demeanor: Paranoid, twitchy, desperate, not 
immediately hostile but could become violent if 
threatened.
Knows About:
o
The “hidden area under the food 
court”, but won’t explain clearly.
o
That “the dead don’t just walk here
—they talk”, but what does he mean?
o
“Something bad happened before the 
outbreak, and the managers knew.”
Potential Actions:
o
Bribable with cigarettes or beer to 
share info.
o
Might follow the party if convinced, 
but not trustworthy.
o
If provoked, he fights with a 
crowbar (1d8 damage).

Action or Loot Secured
SV Reward
Lockbox Opened (If Found)
50 SV
Employee Keycard Found
30 SV
Cigarette Packs (Trade Value)
10 SV each
Beer & Lighter Looted
5-10 SV
Terry the Smoker Bribed
+100 SV if 
convinced 
to join (but 
he’s 
unreliable)
Food Court Door Breached 
Without Alerting Zombies
+50 SV 
Bonus
Tension Impact

Opening the Back Door Loudly → +1d6 
Tension.

Triggering a Dumpster Zombie or the 
Corpse on the Bench → +2d4 Tension.

Firing a Gun in the Area → +3d6 Tension 
(immediate zombie swarm from inside the 
mall).

Negotiating With Terry Successfully → -1d6 
Tension (if he trusts the players, he’ll mislead 
other survivors away).
Possible Zombie 
Encounters (1d4 Roll on 
Noise or Delay)
d4 
Roll Enemy Type
1
Shambler Pair (2 Zombies) – Former 
employees, wearing tattered 
uniforms, still clutching keycards.
2
Crawler in the Dumpster (1 Zombie) 
– Lying in wait, will lunge at the first 
 147 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall
person digging through trash.
3
Horde Response (1d6 Zombies) – 
Attracted to noise, will pour out of the 
food court door if disturbed.
4
The Janitor’s Last Stand – A 
massive brute zombie, still wearing 
a stained mall janitor uniform, 
slumped against the wall. If 
attacked, it awakens with unnatural 
speed…

sites.name: Burger Prince
sites.bookText:
Burger Prince 🍔
“The towering golden burger sign flickers erratically, 
its neon glow barely visible through the grime. The 
drive-thru menu board is riddled with bullet holes, 
shattered speaker grills humming with static. Inside, 
overturned tables and blood-smeared counters tell a 
story of panic. The scent of rancid grease lingers in 
the air, mixing with something far worse—decay. A 
half-eaten burger, mold-ridden and swarmed by flies, 
sits abandoned on a tray near the register. Beyond 
the  shattered  glass  doors,  deep  fryer  oil  has 
congealed into a dark, slick sludge, making every 
step  treacherous.  Something  moves  in  the  back 
kitchen—soft,  wet  shuffling  sounds,  just  beyond 
sight…”
General Description
Burger Prince was once a fast-food chain known for its 
“Two-Fisted Mega Burger” and “Royal Fries.” Now, it’s a 
decayed ruin of overturned booths, grease-slicked 
floors, and scattered trays of rotting food.

Layout:
o
Front Counter & Cash Registers – 
Partially looted, but a few locked 
drawers remain.
o
Dining Area – Bloodstains on the 
booths, scattered kids’ meal toys, a 
partially collapsed ceiling in one 
corner.
o
Kitchen & Walk-In Freezer – 
Suspiciously locked freezer door, 
fryer oil spills, and possible working 
stove.
o
Playplace (Optional Side Area) – A 
ball pit full of corpses, slides coated 
in dried blood.

Threats:
10. 1d4 Shamblers stuck behind the 
counter, unable to navigate the 
booths.
11. 1 Crawler Zombie hidden inside a 
collapsed ceiling vent, drops down 
when players enter the kitchen.
12. Something is banging from inside 
the locked walk-in freezer…

Hazards:
o
Grease-Slicked Floor – Dexterity DC 
13 or slip and fall prone.
o
Fryer Oil Trap – Any explosives or 
gunfire near the deep fryer (Dexterity 
DC 15) causes a fire burst (2d6 
damage in a 10-ft radius).
o
Spoiled Food – If consumed, DC 12 
Constitution save or vomit loudly 
(attracting zombies).
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Cash Register Drawer (Locked, 
DC 15 to open) – Contains $500 
in bills, largely useless but 
possibly good for barter.
2
Emergency Crowbar (Mounted 
on Wall) – 1d6 bludgeoning 
damage, useful for prying doors.
3
Expired Soda Bottles (12-pack) – 
Quenches thirst, but flat and foul-
tasting.
4
Working Deep Fryer – Can be 
turned on to use as a zombie trap 
(2d8 fire damage).
5
Walk-in Freezer (Locked) – Inside 
 148 

Zombie Mall
 
Exterior Areas
is a corpse clutching a pistol 
with 4 bullets (Handgun, 25 SV).
6
Playplace (Optional Side Area) – 
Buried inside the ball pit is a 
bloodied child’s backpack 
(contains 3 ration packs, 1 
flashlight, 1 teddy bear).
Ambiguous Lore
d4 
Roll
Ambiguous Clue Found Here
1
Torn Government Notice: Reads 
“Containment Protocol: DO NOT EAT 
CONTAMINATED MEAT.” But… 
what was contaminated?
2
Greasy Fast-Food Employee Log: 
Entry reads, “They told us to keep 
making burgers even when people 
started coughing up blood. Some of 
the patties were moving.”
3
Handwritten Note (Left in a Kids’ 
Meal Box): “Meet me at the mall food 
court, we have to leave tonight. 
They’re inside the meat now.”
4
Security Camera Footage (if 
players check the back office) – 
Glimpses of shadowy figures in 
biohazard suits loading crates into 
the freezer before the feed cuts 
out.
Random Hazards & 
Encounters (Roll 1d6 Upon 
Entry)
d6 
Roll
Event
1
Ceiling Vent Collapse – A zombie 
drops from the vent, ambushing the 
nearest player.
2
Cash Register Alarm – If tampered 
with, it blasts a loud alarm (+2d6 
Tension instantly).
3
Gas Leak – Any fire-based attack 
explodes the kitchen (3d6 fire 
damage, 15-ft radius).
4
Something Stirs in the Freezer – 
Instead of a corpse, it contains a 
survivor turned zombie (HP: 20, 
extra fast).
5
Rat Swarm – A hungry swarm of 
diseased rats (1d6 bite damage per 
round) emerges from the fryer.
6
Weird Transmission – A radio in 
the back suddenly turns on, 
playing a garbled message about 
“THE SIGNAL IS SAFE. THE 
SIGNAL IS SAFE.”
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action or Loot
SV Reward
Securing Burger 
Prince fully
250 SV
Handgun (4 bullets)
25 SV
Rations (3)
10 SV each
Cash (Potentially 
useful for bartering)
5 SV per $100
Teddy Bear (Morale 
Boost, NPC 
Interaction)
10 SV
Tension Impact

Gunfire inside the kitchen: +3d6 Tension 
(due to loud echoes and potential grease fire).

Using the working radio: +1d6 Tension 
(draws nearby zombies).

Breaking into the freezer: 50% chance to 
cause a loud crash (+2d6 Tension).
 149 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall

Leaving food on the ground overnight: 
Attracts 1d6 zombies by morning.
Potential Enemies
Shamblers (1d4)

AC: 8 | HP: 12 | Attack: Bite (1d6 damage, 
infection chance)

Sluggish but aggressive if players are loud.
Crawler Zombie (Hides in 
vent)

AC: 10 | HP: 8 | Attack: Grapple (DC 13 to 
escape)

Special: If it lands a hit, it latches on, dealing 
automatic bite damage each turn.
Frozen Horror (If Freezer is 
Opened)

AC: 12 | HP: 20 | Movement: Fast (40 ft)

Special: Deals cold damage (1d6 per hit). If it 
bites, the wound becomes frostbitten, 
lowering Dexterity by -1.
Final Notes
Burger Prince is more than just a looting opportunity
—it’s a trap-laden, eerie side zone filled with hazards 
and ambiguous clues. Players must decide if the risk 
is worth the rewards, and small choices (frying oil, 
freezer mysteries, abandoned messages) can lead to 
bigger dangers down the road.

Will they figure out what happened here?

Who left that note about “contaminated 
meat”?

And most importantly… do they dare to 
open the freezer?

sites.name: Taco Shack
sites.bookText:
Taco Shack 🌮
“A faded neon sign buzzes weakly above the drive-
thru  menu,  its  cheerful  cartoon  taco  mascot  now 
faded and stained with grime. The front doors hang 
ajar, the smell of old grease and rotting food mingling 
in the stale air. Inside, overturned tables and broken 
trays litter the floor, while a flickering fluorescent light 
sputters,  casting  eerie  shadows  over  the  salsa-
stained tile. The kitchen door is slightly ajar, a faint  
mist  rolling  out  from  within—cold,  unnatural. 
Something—or someone—is in the freezer, waiting to 
be found…”
Description

Layout:
o
The dining area is mostly trashed—
torn booths, shattered condiment 
dispensers, and a beeping order 
screen displaying a never-served 
meal.
o
The kitchen is a mess of overturned 
fryers, spilled bags of flour, and 
mummified taco shells.
o
The walk-in freezer hums unnaturally 
loud, its handle jammed with a 
makeshift barricade of kitchen 
utensils—as if someone desperately 
tried to keep something in.

Threats:
o
Freezer Corpse Surprise – If opened, 
the frozen body tumbles out (Sanity 
check DC 12 to avoid panic).
o
Feral Freezer Zombie (1) – The 
corpse may suddenly twitch to life 
(50% chance). Slower than usual, but 
immune to cold damage.
o
Hidden Swarm – A pack of flesh-
eating rats nests inside the deep 
fryer. Disturbing the fryer triggers 
an attack (1d6 biting rats).

Hazards:
11. Grease Slick (Dexterity DC 14) – The 
floor near the fryer is coated in rancid 
oil; failed check causes a nasty slip 
 150 

Zombie Mall
 
Exterior Areas
(1d4 damage, prone).
12. Leaky Gas Line – If disturbed, the 
kitchen could become an explosive 
hazard (any open flame triggers 3d6 
fire damage in a 10ft radius).
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Survivor’s Stash – A takeout bag

sites.name: Doughnut Barn
sites.bookText:
Doughnut Barn 🍩
“The smell of old fryer grease and dried blood hangs 
heavy  in  the  air.  The  glass  doors  are  smashed 
inward, their jagged edges glistening with dried gore. 
Outside, police barricades form a crude last stand, 
bullet casings littering the pavement. A few  rotting 
officer corpses remain slumped against their squad 
cars, now little more than husks in faded uniforms. 
Inside, overturned tables, scattered trays, and broken 
coffee dispensers tell the story of a  panicked last 
meal—a place where desperation met the inevitable. 
The  display  case  still  holds  a  few  mummified 
pastries,  untouched  for  weeks.  But  something 
shuffles behind the counter…”
Description

Layout: A small fast-food doughnut shop with 
a counter, kitchen, and seating area. The front 
entrance is wide open, with an employee-only 
exit in the back. A drive-thru window is 
slightly ajar.

Threats: Several Shamblers (1d4) roam near 
the counter, drawn to old fryer heat and 
 152 

Zombie Mall
 
Exterior Areas
flickering menu screens. A Crawler Zombie 
lurks beneath a booth. One “sleeping” 
zombie cop is still buckled into his squad car 
outside.

Hazards:
•
Grease Slicks: Old fryer oil has spilled across the 
tile floor. Any character moving faster than half 
speed must roll DEX (DC 14) or fall prone.
•
Stuck Drive-Thru Window: Requires STR (DC 
16) to force open (or use a crowbar). Leads 
outside.
•
Soda Machine Explosion: Tapping the soda 
dispenser releases a pressurized burst, knocking 
over nearby zombies (or survivors).
Environmental Hazards & 
Random Events (1d4)
d4 Roll Hazard/Event
1
Flashing Menu Screen: An old 
motion sensor flickers a neon 
“Welcome to Doughnut Barn!” 
jingle. (+1d4 Tension, attracts 1d4 
Shamblers from outside)
2
Rancid Coffee Pot: Steam hisses 
suddenly from an overheated 
coffee maker, creating a scalding 
hazard (1d4 heat damage if 
touched).
3
Abandoned Doughnut Box: A box 
labeled “Officer Murphy” contains 
an old revolver (6 rounds, 25 SV) 
and a chewed-up police badge.
4
Locked Supply Closet: Requires 
Lockpicking (DC 14) or Strength 
(DC 17). Contains cleaning 
chemicals, rags, and an 
emergency fire axe.
Loot Table (1d6)
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Half-Eaten Doughnuts (Useless, 
but nostalgic) – No value, but eating 
one restores 1 HP (and makes you 
question your life choices).
2
Police Sidearm (Revolver, 6 shots, 
25 SV) – Found inside a police 
officer’s half-open locker in the back 
room.
3
Grease Fire Starter Kit – Jar of 
fryer oil (flammable, throwable for 
1d6 fire damage over time).
4
Old Cash Register (Locked) – 
Requires Lockpicking (DC 14). 
Contains $232 in bills (worth 0 SV 
but might be bartered).
5
Drive-Thru Headset (Functional) – 
Can be used as a short-range 
communicator (within 300 feet).
6
Employee Keycard – Opens a 
hidden storage room behind the 
counter. (Inside: Basic medical 
supplies, bandages, 20 SV worth of 
food rations.)
Ambiguous Lore
d4 
Roll
Clue Found Inside
1
Crumpled receipt showing a 
massive order placed on the night of 
the outbreak. The receipt was 
signed by BioDyne Corporation.
2
Half-burned Bible page stuck under 
the fryer, referencing the Sixth Seal 
and the moon turning blood-red.
3
Blood-stained security footage on 
an old employee monitor shows 
something huge dragging people 
into the back kitchen… but the 
footage glitches right before it’s 
revealed.
4
A child’s drawing pinned to the 
employee board: A smiling 
doughnut mascot, but its eyes are 
 153

scrawled: “He watches.”

1-2

counter, hands covered in congealed 
syrup.
3
Crawler Zombie (1) – Hiding under a 
booth, grabs ankles (DEX DC 13 to 
avoid).
4
“Officer Murphy” (Special Zombie 
Cop) – Buckled in his police car 
outside. Moves slowly, but has riot 
armor (AC 15).
5
Hungry Swarm (2d4 Fast Zombies) 
– Attracted if Tension reaches 50+ 
while in this area.
6
Boss: The Doughnut Man – A 
bloated zombie chef (HP 40, Vomit 
Attack: 2d6 poison damage, AoE

in a grease fire when killed.


Special: Hidden under furniture, Surprise



AC: 15 (Riot Armor)








fire damage per round for 1d4 rounds).

sites.name: Cluckin’ Good Chicken
sites.bookText:
Cluckin’ Good Chicken 🍗
“The smell of burnt grease and stale fryer oil lingers 
thick in the air. The once-bustling fast-food restaurant 
is now a charred ruin, its counter coated in blackened 
soot and shattered plastic trays. The menu boards 
flicker erratically, some still glowing with the promise 
of ‘value meals’ long since rotted away. Behind the 
counter, vats of rancid oil glisten ominously, and a 
layer of congealed fryer grease coats the tile floor like 
an  invisible  death  trap.  Something  drips  from  the 
ventilation  hood  overhead…  was  that  just  oil,  or 
something else?”
Description:

Layout:
o
A small fast-food restaurant 
connected to the mall via a side 
entrance in the food court.
o
Front Counter: Cash registers, 
toppled trays, shattered soda 
machines.
o
Kitchen Area: Deep fryers still filled 
with black, rancid oil, a freezer door 
slightly ajar, and a grease-stained prep 
station.
o
Dining Area: Overturned tables, 
ripped seat cushions, a children’s play 
area filled with eerie silence.
o
Drive-Thru Window: A partially open 
exit, smeared with bloody 
handprints.

Threats:
o
1d4+2 Shamblers roam inside, 
slipping and shuffling across the 
greasy floor.
o
1d3 “Grease Ghouls” (burned 
zombies) slumped behind the counter
—prone but still active.

Hazards:
o
Grease-Slick Floors: Any sudden 
movement requires a DC 13 Dexterity 
(Acrobatics) check or risk falling 
prone.
o
Flammable Oil: Any source of flame 
(gunfire, flares, etc.) near the fryers 
ignites the entire kitchen (2d6 fire 
damage per round).
o
Freezer Corpses: The walk-in freezer 
contains several preserved bodies—
disturbing them may cause a sudden 
Crawler Zombie Ambush (1d6 
Crawlers).
Interactables & Loot
(Roll 1d6 to determine notable finds)
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Fully Stocked Fryer Oil (5 Jugs) – 
Perfect for fire traps, can be used to 
create Molotovs (each worth 10 
SV).
2
Fire Extinguisher – Functional but 
half-used (10 SV, also useful 
against fires/zombies).
3
Rusty Kitchen Knives (x3) – 
Improvised melee weapons (1d4 
slashing, 5 SV each).
4
Emergency First Aid Kit – Left by 
a fleeing worker, contains 1d4 
bandages, painkillers (total 50 
SV).
 155 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall
5
Old Manager’s Safe – Locked, 
requires DC 14 Dexterity (Thieves’ 
Tools) or brute force (DC 16 
Strength) to open. Contains 200 SV 
worth of emergency cash, a 
single-shot pistol (30 SV), and 
stale energy bars (10 SV each).
6
Suspicious Cultist Note – Hidden 
under the register, a handwritten 
order from an unknown figure 
referring to “The Feast.” (Ties 
into ambiguous lore)
Ambiguous Lore
Players may stumble upon cryptic clues that hint at 
multiple explanations for the apocalypse:
d4 
Roll
Ambiguous Clue

something about “an agreement of 
servitude until the cycle is 
complete.” Signed by an unknown 
party.
2

A working drive-thru speaker 
crackles, repeating a faint, garbled 
message: “…the meat… don’t eat 
the meat… please… don’t…”
3

(Labeled ‘Prototype Meat Blend 
#7’) – The box is half-open, 
contents missing. A rancid smell 
wafts from within.
4
Burned Sigil on the Floor – Under

occult symbols in the tiles before 
they burned. The charred remains 
of a ceremonial robe lie nearby.

sites.name: Speedy Gas & Mart
sites.bookText:
Speedy Gas & Mart ⛽
“The air is thick with the sharp stench of gasoline and 
mildew. The flickering neon sign hums sporadically, 
casting eerie red light over the cracked pavement. 
The  glass  storefront  is  shattered,  leaving  jagged 
edges like a broken mouth. Inside, toppled shelves 
spill expired snacks and scattered magazines. The 
register is pried open, but a sticky note taped to it 
reads: ‘GAS STILL WORKS – CHECK THE BACK.’ 
The  fuel  pumps  outside  stand  eerily  intact,  their 
hoses swaying slightly in the wind. Something nearby 
shifts in the darkness, just beyond the dim glow of the 
station’s flickering lights…”
Description

Layout: A small gas station convenience store 
with a back stockroom, locked bathroom 
stalls, and a clerk’s counter. The fuel pumps 
remain strangely functional, their 
underground reserve untapped.

Threats:
o
1d4+1 Shamblers roam aimlessly 
inside.
o
A Crawler lurks behind the counter, 
waiting to grab an ankle.
o
A gasoline-drenched zombie lies still 
in the backroom, highly flammable but 
inactive unless disturbed.
 157 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall

Hazards:
o
Gasoline Leak: A thin sheen of fuel 
coats the floor near the pumps. Any 
gunfire, fire-based attacks, or 
sparks could cause an explosion 
(4d6 fire damage in a 20-ft radius).
o
Locked Gas Pump Controls: The 
main gas pump system requires a 
key or hacking check (DC 15 
Intelligence) to activate.
Interactables & Loot
d6 
Roll
Notable Items
1
Box of Road Flares (3) – Useful for 
distractions or igniting hazards (5 SV 
each).
2
Jumper Cables & Car Battery – 
Needed for vehicle repair or an 
improvised taser (20 SV).
3
Energy Drinks & Expired Protein 
Bars (5 SV) – Useless for healing but 
restores stamina (reduces 
exhaustion).
4
Propane Tank (Highly Volatile!) – 
Can be thrown and shot for an 
explosion (50 SV).
5
Lockbox Under Counter (DC 14 
Dexterity to pick) – Contains $500 
in cash (worthless) and a loaded .38 
Revolver (30 SV, 6 shots left).
6
Employee’s Hidden Stash – A 
stash of painkillers, a flashlight, 
and a handwritten note about ‘The 
Island’ (lore clue) (50 SV total).
Gas Reserves:
- A working pump remains, but fuel must be 
manually siphoned.
- Each fuel container secured grants 15 SV (Max: 5 
refills before depletion).
- Risk: Each siphoning attempt has a 25% chance of 
attracting zombies from nearby areas.
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered throughout the gas station are eerie hints 
about the apocalypse’s origins, each contradictory 
to keep players guessing:
d4 
Roll
Clue
1
Employee’s Notebook: “They came 
out of the storm drains first… like 
something pushed them up.”
2
Government Evacuation Pamphlet: 
“For your safety, please report to 
Zone 6-B” (Zone 6-B does not exist 
on any known map).
3
CCTV Monitor (Still Active?): The 
camera feed loops footage of an 
empty parking lot—until, suddenly, it 
flickers and shows someone 
watching from outside… but when 
you turn, no one is there.
4
Radio Static from an Old CB Set: A 
faint, **monotone voice repeats 
‘Do not trust the water’ over and 
over, before abruptly cutting out.”
Tension Impact

Loud actions (breaking in, gunfire, 
triggering the gas explosion, setting off 
alarms) increase Tension by 1d6+2.

Discreet looting and siphoning fuel (if done 
quietly) increase Tension by only 1.

If the gas station is fortified or the pumps 
are destroyed, zombies may begin to 
migrate elsewhere.

Potential Enemies & 
Encounters
d6 Roll Encounter
1-2
Shamblers (1d4+1) – Wandering, 
aimless but dangerous in numbers.
3
Crawler (Behind Counter) – Hides, 
grabs ankles, restrains survivors 
(DC 14 Strength to escape).
4
Flammable Zombie – Lies still in 
the back, highly explosive if 
ignited. If disturbed, it wakes up.
5
A Survivor Appears? – A 
paranoid scavenger with a 
shotgun (50% chance friendly, 50% 
chance hostile).
6
Military Remnant Patrol (2 
soldiers, lightly armed) – 
Searching for fuel; may demand it 
or open fire.
Stat Blocks for Key Enemies
Shamblers (1d4+1)

HP: 10 each

AC: 8

Atk: Bite (1d6, infection chance)

Speed: 20 ft (Slow)

Special: Clumsy, but immune to fear
Crawler Zombie
HP: 8
AC: 10
Atk: Bite (1d6, +grapple attempt DC 14)
Speed: 5 ft (Immobile, grabs ankles)
Flammable Zombie

HP: 15

AC: 9

Atk: Slam (1d8)

Special:
o
Explodes (4d6 fire) if ignited
o
Fire-resistant unless completely 
burned through
Paranoid Survivor (Optional NPC)

HP: 22

AC: 14 (Leather jacket)

Atk: Sawed-off Shotgun (2d6, 2 shots, reload 
action)

Special: 50% chance of being friendly OR 
hostile

Morale Check: (WIS Save DC 13) – If 
cornered, may surrender or flee.
Survivor Options

Secure the Gas Station: Reinforce doors, use 
it as a temporary base.

Blow It All Up: Use the gas and propane tank 
for tactical explosions.

Siphon and Run: Grab the fuel, avoid 
unnecessary fights.
 159 

Exterior Areas
 
Zombie Mall

Investigate the Lore: Find out what happened 
here—and who might still be watching.
Conclusion
Speedy Gas & Mart is an explosive, high-risk 
location—it can be a goldmine of fuel and weapons, 
but also one wrong move away from disaster. Smart 
players will be cautious, but bold survivors may walk 
away with a game-changing fuel reserve—or a fiery 
grave.

sites.name: Tire World
sites.bookText:
Tire World 
“The scent of burnt rubber and stale motor oil lingers 
in the air. Stacks of tires form makeshift barricades, 
casting long, distorted shadows under the flickering 
parking lot lights. The front windows of the store are 
shattered, jagged glass crunching underfoot as a soft 
breeze  carries  the  distant  groans  of  the  undead. 
Inside, shelves are toppled, display rims are dented, 
and  a  half-looted  register  drawer  dangles  open. 
Somewhere in the darkness, something shifts—soft, 
slow, deliberate. You are not alone here.”
General Description
Tire World is an auto supply shop specializing in tires, 
oil changes, and basic car maintenance. The store’s 
interior is cluttered with overturned shelving units, 
broken tire racks, and dark corners where movement is 
difficult to track.

Layout: Wide-open front with broken windows, 
tight storage aisles filled with car parts, and a 
service bay in the back with hydraulic lifts still 
intact.

Threats: Zombies are trapped in tires, 
making them easy to overlook until it’s too late.

Hazards: Slick oil spills, precarious stacks of 
tires that can collapse, loud metal tools that 
easily attract the horde.

sites.name: QuickFix Auto
sites.bookText:
QuickFix Auto 🔧
“The scent of motor oil and burnt rubber lingers in the 
air as you approach the dimly lit auto repair shop. The 
garage door is partially open, its metal frame bent 
and warped like something tried to claw its way inside
—or out. Inside, flickering fluorescent lights cast eerie 
shadows across overturned tool carts and shattered 
glass. A sedan sits in the middle of the bay, its engine 
inexplicably  still  running,  headlights  casting  long, 
unsettling beams across the cracked concrete floor. 
Something—or someone—was just here… but where 
are they now?”
Description

Layout: A small auto repair shop with two 
vehicle service bays, a cluttered front desk, 
and a tool storage area. Outside, an 
abandoned fuel pump still drips gasoline, and 
a wrecked tow truck blocks part of the parking 
lot.

Threats: At least one zombie (or worse) is 
still inside—but where? Noise may attract 
others from nearby lots.

Hazards: Spilled oil (DEX DC 12 or fall
